chapters.title: Chapter 301: The Conversion and the Return to the Real World
paragraphs: Kai couldn’t help but look at the young man curiously.
The child’s ability had shocked him... not the fact that he was being sold, but the uniqueness of his gene.
A safeguard against mutation, a way to revert to human form no matter what modifications were forced upon him. It was a rare gift, one that could be exploited endlessly.
He could already imagine several uses for this young man if he were that twisted figure.
Still, seeing the expression of some old men and some middle-aged women around, he couldn’t help but feel that he had to try to save this young man at the very least.
’Whatever... I still have a couple of thousand.’Kai muttered to himself as he decided to purchase the man.
Kai had bid fiercely, his hand rising again and again as the numbers climbed.
580 medals had nearly stolen the boy away... It was a bid so high it had to be the pooled resources of a large guild.
They wanted him desperately, whether to save him or to use him, Kai couldn’t tell.
But in the end, Kai made the final bid...
The hammer fell.
"Sold. The child, for 600 Survivor Medals."
The crowd erupted in whispers.
"He spent six hundred..."
"On a child?"
"Does he know what he’s doing?"
Still, Kai ignored them. The boy was bound to him now, just like the super soldiers. He would be safe.
Kai would not allow him to be exploited.
If the boy wanted to test his ability, Kai could guide him. But for now, safety came first.
Kai stood up, ready to leave the hall. He had spent more than he intended, but the acquisitions were worth it.
He got four soldiers and a child with a unique gene...

The soldiers were assets that could change the future of his shelters. As for the child, he could probably do some odd jobs within the shelter. That should be better than being a subject of an experiment.
But then the old man’s voice rang out again, halting him in his tracks.
"Next," he said as a man went to a stage carrying a paper with a picture of a "This lot is not a human. It is a virtual item."
The hall fell into confusion. Survivors glanced at one another beneath their cloaks.
"A virtual item?"
"What does that mean?"
"Is this some kind of joke?"
Many of the survivors had no idea about the Virtual World.
Still, the old man smiled faintly.

"Many of you may not understand. But for those who know of the VRMMORPGPerfect World, you will recognize its value. This item exists within the virtual realm, yet it can be gifted here, in the Auction Realm. Its effects are not limited to the game... If you know the game, you’ll know what I’m talking about."
Kai froze. He knew exactly what the old man meant.

Perfect World. The VR world he had entered before, the one tied to the Neural Gear Interface. The place where gene skills synchronized with reality, where rumors spoke of the Divine Gene blueprint... a perfect genetic enhancement without side effects.
The crowd murmured in confusion. Ninety percent of them had no idea what a virtual item was. To them, it sounded worthless.
But to Kai, and to a handful of others who had touched the VR world, it was priceless.
Nonetheless, Kai looked at the picture being shown, and it was actually a gauntlet.
[ Virtual Weapon: Ether Gauntlet ]
[ Type: Gene‐Linked Armament ]
[ Origin: Perfect World VRMMORPG ]
[ Description: A legendary gauntlet that exists within the virtual realm. When bound to a survivor, it synchronizes with their genetic code, allowing them to channel raw energy into their attacks.
Special Effect:
Energy Channeling: Converts energy into concussive blasts or protective barriers.
Strong Grip: Can fuse temporarily with other weapons or tools, enhancing their output. ]

The old man explained, "It is a weapon of pure force. Those who wield it can strike without steel, defend without shields, and manipulate energy itself. Few understand its worth, but those who do will know it is priceless. Lastly, once it’s bound to you, you can use a Conversion Node on this item! If you don’t have a Vonversion Node yet, you can purchase it separately after this event!"
Kai’s visor gleamed. Since it’s possible to use Conversion Node on this gauntlet, it means that it was a weapon that could exist in both realms, bridging the gap.
That alone was more than enough to catch his interest.
Finally, after the introduction was over, the bidding began hesitantly.
"10 medals."
Most survivors scoffed, dismissing it as useless. But a handful of cloaked bidders raised their hands sharply.
Kai knew that they had touchedPerfect Worldtoo.

Kai leaned forward. He had already spent heavily tonight... 525 medals on the super soldiers, 600 on the child. But this was different. This wasn’t just another acquisition. This was a weapon that could help him level up faster in the Virtual World and, in turn, help him get closer to the Divine Gene.
The guild that had fought him for the child bid aggressively again.
Kai sighed as he decided to make this quick.
"300," Kai said evenly.
The man countered instantly. "320."
The hall grew tense. Survivors who didn’t understand watched in confusion, wondering why anyone would spend so much on a virtual gauntlet.
Kai exhaled slowly.
This time, his opponent hesitated, then raised their sign. "370."
Finally, Kai raised his number once again...
The hall fell silent.
The old man’s smile widened. "Sold. The Virtual Item... Ether Gauntlet, for 400 Survivor Medals."
Kai didn’t rush out of the hall after his last purchase. Instead, he turned to the four super soldiers and the child, wanting to know who they truly were.
Kai introduced himself first...
"I’m Kai. You’re mine now, but not as slaves. You’ll fight with me, and I’ll make sure you live."
They weren’t trusting his words that easily but one by one, they gave their names...
The broadest of them spoke first. "I am Draxen."
The one who had long gray hair spoke next, "Call me Castor."
The third, scarred across his jaw, muttered, "Korval."
And the last simply said, "Serric."
Kai nodded, committing each name to memory. They weren’t faceless soldiers anymore... they were men with identities, men he intended to save.
Then he turned to the child. The boy had a soft voice...
"My name’s Matt... I’m ten."
Kai crouched slightly, meeting his gaze. "Matt, you’re safe now. No one will experiment on you. You’ll have a place in my shelter."
The boy nodded, and although he was still skeptical, there was relief appearing across his face.
With introductions complete, Kai began purchasing items for them.
Armor pieces, several sets of clothes, and even some weapons that Kai couldn’t produce using his Gift Pack... Well, anything that could stabilize the soldiers and keep the boy comfortable was bought.
Hours passed as they moved from stall to stall within the Auction Realm. The gauntlet he had won earlier was secured directly after Kai provided them with his IGN and ID...
He even obtained a Conversion Node for free!
The soldiers tested their new gear, adjusting straps and grips, while Matt clutched a small satchel Kai had given him, filled with food and simple tools.
Soon, every survivor felt exhausted with their cloaks heavy with sweat... The second day of the auction had drained them all.
Finally, a system notification appeared before every participant.
[ Auction Event Concluding ]
[ All transactions finalized. Survivors will return to their shelters shortly. ]
[ Remaining Survivor Medals will be converted to Energy Cores. ]
[ Conversion Rate: 100 Survivor Medals = 1 B‐Grade Energy Core. ]
[ Conversion Rate: 10 Survivor Medals = 1 C‐Grade Energy Core. ]
The hall erupted in chaos.
"What?!"
"You mean they vanish?!"
"I saved over 400 medals... I could’ve bought something!"
"Why didn’t they tell us earlier?"
"This is robbery!"
"I held back for tomorrow’s event — now it’s all gone!"
"They tricked us into saving!"
"I should’ve bought that serum when I had the chance!"
"Do they think B‐Grade Cores are equal to medals? They’re not!"
"Damn it... I had 900 medals, and now it’s just nine cores!"
"I had 190 medals... and it only gave me one B‐Grade and nine C‐Grades? Ninety medals wasted!"
"C‐Grade? That’s pocket change compared to medals!"
"They should’ve warned us... I would’ve spent everything!"
"All those missions, all that risk... reduced to scraps!"
"This system is rigged!"Curses filled the chamber as survivors realized the truth.
Many had hoarded their medals, hoping to use them later, only to discover they would be stripped away and converted.
Kai’s visor gleamed as he read the notification. He didn’t curse. He had spent a lot of his Survivor Medals as well.
He had invested instead of hoarding, and now he would return with assets that mattered.
Still, he had some excess, so thanks to that, he got 21 B-Grade Energy Cores.
But others weren’t so fortunate. Survivors shouted at the organizers, demanding explanations. Some slammed their fists against the benches, furious that they hadn’t known.
"It’s too late to regret now," Kai muttered under his breath.
[ Time Remaining: 30 seconds ]
[ Prepare for transfer. Survivors will be returned to their shelters. ]

chapters.title: Chapter 302: The B-Ranks and New Vessels
paragraphs: In the meantime, the continent of Versailles, the crimson sky lingered above...
The people in New Haven‐45 couldn’t get used to this sky that was like a wound that refused to close.
A day had passed since the colossal mechanical structures appeared, and though they remained motionless, their silence weighed heavily on the defenders.
After all, they had no idea what it would do...
Would it drop some huge humanoid machines or mechas? Perhaps numerous Dragoons would be deployed from the sky?
They had no idea what it could do, and it was simply terrifying...

Althea stood at the watchtower, her eyes fixed on the horizon. The shelter had pulled out its telescopes and binoculars from Kai’s gift packs. As for the telescopes, they were relics salvaged from abandoned observatories and scavenger runs.
Scouts rotated shifts, peering through lenses at the floating constructs.
They magnified the angular surfaces, tracing the outlines of towers and strange protrusions, but no movement was detected.
No drones, no beams, no descent. Just silence...
"Anything?" Augustine asked, climbing the ladder to join her. His voice was hoarse from shouting orders all day.
Althea shook her head. "Nothing. They’re just... probably watching us as well"

Augustine spat over the railing. "Hahaha? Are they actually waiting for the Foreign Survivors? These machines don’t just watch for no reason... They’re definitely waiting and when they move, it’s never good."
He wasn’t one to sit idle. While the telescopes scanned the skies, Augustine had spent the day strengthening defenses.
He ordered trenches dug deeper around the perimeter, their edges lined with sharpened stakes. Pits were camouflaged with dirt and debris, ready to swallow any advancing unit.

Closer to the walls, he had overseen the placement of spike traps... Well, they were crude but effective, made from welded rebar and scavenged steel. If Sentinels, Hounds, and other units tried to climb, they would impale themselves before reaching the barricades, or at least slow them down.
Beyond that, Augustine had devised more elaborate snares.

Thanks to the various wires they had scavenged and numerous ropes that Kai had supplied, they created some weighted nets, rigged with counterbalances. They are mostly hidden beneath loose soil. If triggered, they would spring upward, entangling mechanical limbs and dragging them down into the trenches.
"Diggers worry me most," Augustine muttered as he inspected the ground.
"If they come from below, the walls won’t matter."

To counter that, they had planted some explosives underground and also prepared several grenade launchers so once they stick out, or once they get a hold of their holes, they could easily bombard and collapse their tunnel.
Of course, with their portable disruptor field and the perimeter alarm system set or sensors placed around the shelter, they would have enough time to react...
These devices would at least give a warning if something burrowed beneath.
"You’ve thought of everything... Well done." Althea muttered quietly.
"Not everything," Augustine replied. "But enough to buy us time."
Inside the shelter, survivors worked tirelessly.
Barricades were reinforced with more scavenged scrap metal. Ammunition was inventoried, rationed, and distributed to squads. T
The modified Sentinels stationed at the gate, X‐02 through X‐06, were recalibrated, their optics tuned to detect movement in the crimson haze.
Irene, the infirmary’s caretaker, worked tirelessly to prepare for the worst. She brewed stimulants from Kai’s earlier recipes, improving them with herbs that were cultivated in a greenhouse.
She stocked salves for burns, bandages for wounds, and others... Her hands never stopped moving, and though she spoke little, her presence reassured the defenders.
In the mess hall, Mila, the head chef, took charge of rationing. She organized supplies with her experience, ensuring every defender had enough to last through a siege.
Nonetheless, Althea knew that it would be hard to deal with this matter...
The crimson sky was definitely an omen.
Just like that, night fell, but the sky did not darken.
The crimson glow persisted across the land.
By dawn, the shelter remained safe... and only a couple of hours later, the Foreign Survivors would return...
However, the machines in the sky could no longer wait. In just a few moments, the people assigned to the watchtowers rang the bell.
Clang! Clang! Clang!
The floating island was finally sending out numerous flying vessels. Many headed in different directions, but one of them was coming straight toward New Haven‐45.
"Holy shit..." Augustine muttered as he looked at the sky...
Defenders rushed to the walls, weapons in hand, as they hoped that Kai and the others return immediately!
From the horizon, a vessel came closer... but it was unlike anything they had seen before.
It was not an Impulse Gunship with its sleek cannons. It was not the twin‐rotor aerial gunship that had harassed shelters in the past.
It was not the Dominion, the disk‐shaped anti‐gravity craft.
Nor was it the jetski‐like vessel used by Dragoons.
This was something new.
The vessel moved through the air like a serpent, its body was segmented and flexible with scales of metal...
Then, five humanoid figures clung to its back! They seemed to be armored Sentinels riding this flying snake-like vessel!
Althea couldn’t help but feel shocked... "What in the world..."
Augustine frowned as he wasn’t sure if that snake vessel was only a transportation vehicle or it was also a mechanical beast ready to pounce on them...
"Doesn’t matter what it’s called. It’s coming for us!"
The serpent vessel swooped low, aiming for the shelter.
But as it neared, the Advanced Barrier System activated.
Bam!
A shimmering dome of energy flared around New Haven‐45, repelling the vessel with a thunderous crash...
The serpent buckled and its riders ere thrown off, crashing into the earth outside the walls.
The defenders cheered briefly... until they saw what had landed.
The Sentinels rose from the dust, their armor still looking perfectly under the crimson sky. They weren’t dented at all!
Furthermore, these sentinels were larger, bulkier, and their armor plating was thicker than anything the shelter had faced before.
Augustine’s eyes widened. "Is this... B‐Rank Sentinels? Shit!"
Althea’s heart sank. Their modified Sentinels, X‐02 through X‐06, were only C‐Rank. They had been proud of those machines, but compared to these, they looked fragile.
The defenders murmured in fear. "B‐Rank? We can’t fight those..."
But Althea silenced them with a shout.
"We don’t give up! We have traps, we have weapons, we have each other. Hold the line!"
The battle began just like that...
The B‐Rank Sentinels advanced with their heavy steps, shaking the ground.
Augustine triggered the perimeter traps. Trenches collapsed, stakes impaled, nets sprang upward... but the armored machines tore through them, their plating shrugging off the crude defenses.
B-Rank Sentinels were on a different level for sure!
"Grenade launchers!" Augustine shouted...
Soon, explosions erupted across the field as smoke and fire engulfed the Sentinels, slowing their advance.
One staggered, its armor scorched, but it kept moving.
Althea directed the artillery. "Target the center! Fire!"
The lone artillery piece thundered, its shell slamming into a Sentinel’s chest. The impact knocked it back, denting its armor, but still it rose.
"Damn it, they’re too tough!" a defender cried...
Althea hurled a smoke grenade, the thick cloud obscuring the machines.
"Blind them! Use the disruptors!"

Portable disruptor fields activated and soon, it started distorting the Sentinels’ signals. Stun grenades followed, detonating with blinding flashes. For a moment, the machines slowed d as if their movements became sluggish.
"Now! Rifles!" Augustine roared.
Dozens of defenders opened fire, bullets hammering against the weakened joints.
Clank! Clank! Clank!
Sparks flew as rounds found gaps in the armor.
One Sentinel collapsed soon as it was actually thrown into a fire trap, its systems fried!
Thud!
The defenders cheered, but the victory was short‐lived.
The remaining Sentinels surged forward, smashing through barricades.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
Their weapons, heavy blades and mounted guns, tore into the defenses.
Althea gritted her teeth. "Keep fighting! Don’t let them breach the walls!"
Grenades were thrown, nets were used to keep them in place, and rifles fired continuously...
The battlefield was chaos...
One Sentinel reached the trench, its foot caught in a weighted net.
Augustine seized the chance, firing a grenade launcher directly into its chest. The blast tore through its plating, sending it crashing into the pit, but it wasn’t disabled yet...
Another Sentinel continued slamming the barrier, and they knew it would collapse if they don’t stop it... Thankfully, defenders swarmed it, hurling grenades and firing point‐blank.
Bang! Bang!
Furthermore, the disruptor field seemed to have overloaded its systems, and it toppled backward...
Still, two remained, pressing hard against the defenses. One of them were even slowly standing up to continue...
Althea’s voice rang out, steady despite the chaos. "Focus fire! Aim for the joints!"
The defenders obeyed, rifles and grenades hammering the machines’ knees and elbows.

Althea couldn’t help but feel nervous since each defender had probably used five magazines by now... Since there were 20 or so of them, that was already quite a lot considering that they were only facing five enemies!
Still, slowly, the Sentinels also reached their limit...
Two collapsed under the barrage, with their armor cracked open. The last Sentinel charged, but Augustine triggered the final trap.
Explosives buried beneath the soil detonated, engulfing the machine in fire.
When the smoke cleared, only twisted metal remained...
"We did it—"
However, as they were about to celebrate, they realized that the huge snake-like vessel had already destroyed the barrier...

Irene, the infirmary’s caretaker, worked tirelessly to prepare for the worst.
She brewed stimulants from Kai’s earlier recipes, improving them with herbs that were cultivated in a greenhouse.
She stocked salves for burns, bandages for wounds, and others...
Her hands never stopped moving, and though she spoke little, her presence reassured the defenders.
In the mess hall, Mila, the head chef, took charge of rationing.
She organized supplies with her experience, ensuring every defender had enough to last through a siege.
Nonetheless, Althea knew that it would be hard to deal with this matter...
The crimson sky was definitely an omen.
Just like that, night fell, but the sky did not darken.
The crimson glow persisted across the land.
By dawn, the shelter remained safe... and only a couple of hours later, the Foreign Survivors would return...
However, the machines in the sky could no longer wait.
In just a few moments, the people assigned to the watchtowers rang the bell.
Clang!
Clang!
Clang!
The floating island was finally sending out numerous flying vessels.
Many headed in different directions, but one of them was coming straight toward New Haven‐45.
"Holy shit..." Augustine muttered as he looked at the sky...
Defenders rushed to the walls, weapons in hand, as they hoped that Kai and the others return immediately!
From the horizon, a vessel came closer... but it was unlike anything they had seen before.
It was not an Impulse Gunship with its sleek cannons.
It was not the twin‐rotor aerial gunship that had harassed shelters in the past.
It was not the Dominion, the disk‐shaped anti‐gravity craft.
Nor was it the jetski‐like vessel used by Dragoons.
This was something new.
The vessel moved through the air like a serpent, its body was segmented and flexible with scales of metal...
Then, five humanoid figures clung to its back!
They seemed to be armored Sentinels riding this flying snake-like vessel!
Althea couldn’t help but feel shocked...
"What in the world..."
Augustine frowned as he wasn’t sure if that snake vessel was only a transportation vehicle or it was also a mechanical beast ready to pounce on them...
"Doesn’t matter what it’s called.
It’s coming for us!"
The serpent vessel swooped low, aiming for the shelter.
But as it neared, the Advanced Barrier System activated.
Bam!
A shimmering dome of energy flared around New Haven‐45, repelling the vessel with a thunderous crash...
The serpent buckled and its riders ere thrown off, crashing into the earth outside the walls.
The defenders cheered briefly... until they saw what had landed.
The Sentinels rose from the dust, their armor still looking perfectly under the crimson sky.
They weren’t dented at all!
Furthermore, these sentinels were larger, bulkier, and their armor plating was thicker than anything the shelter had faced before.
Augustine’s eyes widened.
"Is this...
B‐Rank Sentinels?
Shit!"
Althea’s heart sank.
Their modified Sentinels, X‐02 through X‐06, were only C‐Rank.
They had been proud of those machines, but compared to these, they looked fragile.
The defenders murmured in fear.
"B‐Rank?
We can’t fight those..."
But Althea silenced them with a shout.
"We don’t give up!
We have traps, we have weapons, we have each other.
Hold the line!"
The battle began just like that...
The B‐Rank Sentinels advanced with their heavy steps, shaking the ground.
Augustine triggered the perimeter traps.
Trenches collapsed, stakes impaled, nets sprang upward... but the armored machines tore through them, their plating shrugging off the crude defenses.
B-Rank Sentinels were on a different level for sure!
"Grenade launchers!" Augustine shouted...
Soon, explosions erupted across the field as smoke and fire engulfed the Sentinels, slowing their advance.
One staggered, its armor scorched, but it kept moving.
Althea directed the artillery.
"Target the center!
Fire!"
The lone artillery piece thundered, its shell slamming into a Sentinel’s chest.
The impact knocked it back, denting its armor, but still it rose.
"Damn it, they’re too tough!" a defender cried...
Althea hurled a smoke grenade, the thick cloud obscuring the machines.
"Blind them!
Use the disruptors!"
Portable disruptor fields activated and soon, it started distorting the Sentinels’ signals.
Stun grenades followed, detonating with blinding flashes.
For a moment, the machines slowed d as if their movements became sluggish.
"Now!
Rifles!" Augustine roared.
Dozens of defenders opened fire, bullets hammering against the weakened joints.
Clank!
Clank!
Clank!
Sparks flew as rounds found gaps in the armor.
One Sentinel collapsed soon as it was actually thrown into a fire trap, its systems fried!
Thud!
The defenders cheered, but the victory was short‐lived.
The remaining Sentinels surged forward, smashing through barricades.
Bang!
Bang!
Bang!
Their weapons, heavy blades and mounted guns, tore into the defenses.
Althea gritted her teeth.
"Keep fighting!
Don’t let them breach the walls!"
Grenades were thrown, nets were used to keep them in place, and rifles fired continuously...
The battlefield was chaos...
One Sentinel reached the trench, its foot caught in a weighted net.
Augustine seized the chance, firing a grenade launcher directly into its chest.
The blast tore through its plating, sending it crashing into the pit, but it wasn’t disabled yet...
Another Sentinel continued slamming the barrier, and they knew it would collapse if they don’t stop it...
Thankfully, defenders swarmed it, hurling grenades and firing point‐blank.
Bang!
Bang!
Furthermore, the disruptor field seemed to have overloaded its systems, and it toppled backward...
Still, two remained, pressing hard against the defenses.
One of them were even slowly standing up to continue...
Althea’s voice rang out, steady despite the chaos.
"Focus fire!
Aim for the joints!"
The defenders obeyed, rifles and grenades hammering the machines’ knees and elbows.
Althea couldn’t help but feel nervous since each defender had probably used five magazines by now...
Since there were 20 or so of them, that was already quite a lot considering that they were only facing five enemies!
Still, slowly, the Sentinels also reached their limit...
Two collapsed under the barrage, with their armor cracked open.
The last Sentinel charged, but Augustine triggered the final trap.
Explosives buried beneath the soil detonated, engulfing the machine in fire.
When the smoke cleared, only twisted metal remained...
"We did it—"
However, as they were about to celebrate, they realized that the huge snake-like vessel had already destroyed the barrier...

chapters.title: Chapter 303: The Defense and Kai’s Return
paragraphs: Crash!
A massive explosion shook the ground as the serpent‐like vessel slammed into the Advanced Barrier System.
The dome of energy shattered, collapsing into nothingness...
"No way..."
"It’s destroyed!"
"Careful! Look above!"
The vessel itself was torn apart in the blast as the debris fell everywhere... Nonetheless, the damage was done, New Haven‐45’s barrier was gone.
Althea couldn’t help but feel really worried now.

Without the barrier, the shelter had no way to stop flying vessels from entering directly. Their arsenal was limited... rifles, pistols, grenade launchers, disruptor field units, and traps. None of these were true anti‐aircraft weapons.
The only hope lay in the plasma rifles carried by their modified Sentinels. Each rifle could fire twelve shots before requiring a long recharge.
They had been saving those charges for emergencies... and this was one.
Augustine’s voice rang out..."The worst has come."
From the crimson sky, two more serpent vessels slithered into view.
Their segmented bodies gleamed like metallic scales, weaving through the air with unnatural grace.
As they approached, defenders on the walls shouted in alarm.
"Two more!"
"They’re dropping units!"
"Inject the stimulants!"
"Yes!"
Just like that, the vessels swooped low, releasing their riders.
Ten armored Sentinels leapt from the serpents, landing heavily some where outside the shelter, but three managed to land inside...
Dust and debris flew as their massive frames rose, optics glowing with cold precision.
Still, the stimulants were soon used! This boosted their senses, strength, and agility... If they have gene skills, those were also improved.
Althea held her weapon tightly as she looked at the enemies.
"Ten of them... all B‐Rank."

The defenders froze. Their modified Sentinels, X‐02 through X‐06, were only C‐Rank. They weren’t strong enough to fight the B-Ranks head-on, so they had to be smart... These armored units were on another level after all.
The B‐Rank Sentinels had then advanced, their heavy steps started shaking the ground.
It even felt as if their armor was thicker... However, they were sure that their weapons were larger. They had heavy blades and mounted cannons!
They were here to destroy their shelter!
"Hold the line!" Althea shouted, forcing courage into her voice. "We have traps, we have rifles, we have plasma rifles. Fight!"
The defenders obeyed, but fear gnawed at them.
Augustine triggered the remaining perimeter traps.

Soon, all the trenches collapsed, stakes were impaled, and the last nets sprang upward... but the Sentinels tore through them. Their armor shrugged off the crude defenses, sparks flying as steel bent and broke.
"Grenade launchers!" Augustine roared.
Soon, explosions erupted across the battlefield. Fire and smoke engulfed the machines, slowing their advance.
One Sentinel faltered with its armored scorched, but it kept moving!
Another raised its cannon, blasting a barricade apart.
Boom! Boom!
The buildings shuddered, and the defenders were thrown back in screams of pain.
Althea directed the artillery. "Target the closest! Fire!"
The siege artillery thundered with its shell slamming into a Sentinel at close range.
Boom!
The impact dented its chest, knocking it back, but still it rose.
"What?!"
"How is that even possible?!"
"This is crazy! They took it head-on?"
"That’s too much."
The artillery was designed for long‐range bombardment, not anti‐air combat. Forced into close quarters, it seemed that its shots were devastating but limited.
"It’s not enough to get the right momentum."
"Damn it, they’re too tough!" a defender cried, clutching his rifle.
Althea hurled a smoke grenade, thick clouds obscuring the machines.
"Blind them! Use the disruptors!"
Immediately, portable disruptor fields activated, humming with interference wave.
The Sentinels were immediately unable to communicate with the other Sentinels and with so many disruptors working, their optics seemed to be distorting as well!
It didn’t end there, Stun grenades followed, detonating with blinding flashes.
For a moment, the machines slowed...
"Now! Rifles!" Augustine barked.
Dozens of defenders opened fire, bullets hammering against weakened joints.
Sparks flew as rounds found gaps in the armor. One Sentinel collapsed, its systems fried, crashing into a pit.
The defenders were happy to see this but the victory was short‐lived.
The remaining Sentinels charged forward, smashing through simple barricades they created...
Heavy blades cleaved steel, mounted cannons tore into buildings...
The walls shook under the assault as chunks of scrap metal could be seen flying everywhere.
Soon, the deaths piled up!
Guards screamed as they were cut down, blood staining the ground.
Althea gritted her teeth. "Keep fighting! They’re slow! We can overwhelm them!"
Grenades flew even more as the battlefield was chaos... smoke, fire, and explosions were everywhere!
One Sentinel reached the mess hall but its foot was caught in a weighted net.
Augustine seized the chance, firing a grenade launcher directly into its chest. The blast tore through its plating, sending it crashing into the pit.
But it wasn’t disabled yet... its optics still glowed, its arms clawing upward!
"These things are so tough!"
"What are these made of?!"
Another Sentinel slammed against the watchtower...
Bam!
Soon, its cannon blasted defenders from the ramparts. Screams echoed as guards fell, lifeless. The shelter’s defenses were crumbling!
Althea’s voice rang out as she remained in the distance using her rifles...
Though she wanted to figh in close range, she couldn’t do so with so many enemies still gathered.
She was sure that she could win one-on-one against a B-Rank but if she was cornered, it would be a certain death...
"Focus fire! Aim for the joints!"
The defenders obeyed, rifles and grenades hammering knees and elbows.
Slowly, painfully, the machines stopped moving...
One collapsed under the barrage, its armor cracked open.
But more pressed forward. Ten had landed, and only three were down, seven more remained.
They were all battered, but they were still moving!
Then, it was at this moment that the modified Sentinels, X‐02 through X‐06, finally got a better position...
"Now!" Althea shouted.
Their plasma rifles hummed as they gathered energy... Soon, blue light flared as they fired, streams of searing energy tearing into the B‐Rank units.
Whom! Whom! Whom!
Three shots struck in one point, burning through armor plating.
One B‐Rank Sentinel staggered with its chest glowing red‐hot, before collapsing in a heap.
Indeed, three shots in the same spot were needed to break through their armor!
The defenders roared in triumph. But the plasma rifles had limits... only twelve shots each. Every blast had to count.
"Save your charges!" Althea warned.
"Don’t waste them!"
The battle raged on. The artillery fired again with its shell slamming into a Sentinel at point‐blank range!
The explosion tore through its torso, sending fragments flying. But the recoil damaged the artillery itself. Smoke was already pouring from its barrel.
"Artillery’s failing!" a defender shouted.
"Keep it firing until it breaks!" Augustine snapped. He didn’t care about the Artillery anymore...
The Sentinels continued to advance... their cannons were blasting holes in the walls.
Defenders were forced back, their rifles nearly empty.
Smoke grenades and disruptors bought precious seconds, but the machines were not stopping...
One Sentinel breached the outer barricade, cutting down guards with its blade. Blood sprayed as defenders fell, their screams drowned by the roar of gunfire.
"Aaaack! Help me! Please!"
"My arm! The Stimulant! more stimulant!"
"Don’t! You’ve already used one! You’re not a foreign survivor! You’ll get overdosed!"
"We can only have one of them! Our Gene Enhancements wouldn’t be able to endure it."
Althea’s heart pounded. "We can’t hold much longer..."
But she refused to give in. "Fight! Every second counts! Kai will return... we just have to survive!"
The defenders rallied, their desperation was giving them strength...
Soon, another Sentinel fell... But the cost was high... the walls were shattered, guards lay dead, and the shelter was bleeding.
There were still B-Rank Sentinels... Only five were destroyed... The remaining five may be damaged but they’re still moving...
"Cover me..." Althea muttered as she made her move.
She didn’t even wait for Augustine’s reply!
Her dagger manifested in her hand, glowing faintly... It was her Gene Weapon. It pulsed with her energy, bound to her soul, and it was sharper than steel...
She charged forward, with her speed amplified by stimulants and gene enhancements.
The first Sentinel swung its cannon arm, but Althea slipped beneath it, slashing upward.
Sssaah!
Sparks erupted as her dagger carved through the armored limb, severing it clean.
The machine stepped back as it was suddenly out of balance!
Without pause, she spun toward another. Its heavy steps shook the ground, but she leapt high, driving her blade into its knee joint.
Thu!
Metal shrieked as the leg gave way. The Sentinel was still active, but it collapsed sideways.
The third Sentinel came quickly with its massive blade raised to cleave her in two. Althea’s eyes narrowed.
Her dagger sliced across the weapon itself. The heavy blade split, fragments scattering, the machine was momentarily stunned.
She was magnificent... It was a blur of precision and fury, cutting through giants with a Low-Grade Gene Weapon!
The defenders gasped, their morale surging at the sight.
But the surprise ended abruptly. One of the Sentinels recovered, its mounted cannon locking onto her.
Bam!
"Aack!"
A blast erupted, slamming into her side.
The force hurled her across the battlefield. She hit the ground hard with her body nearly thrown into a jagged pipe protruding from the wreckage.
Before she could collide, a hand caught her mid‐fall.
It was strong and steady.
"Good job staying alive, Althea..." Kai muttered as he glanced at the remaining B-Rank Sentinels.

chapters.title: Chapter 304: Remaining Defense
paragraphs: Kai’s boots hit the ground with a heavy thud as he caught Althea...
His full black gear was still equipped, and it was already turning red since it was absorbing the glow of the crimson sky.
After confirming that Althea was fine, he didn’t rush in blindly... his eyes swept across the battlefield, as he calculated the situation.
He saw the number of survivors, their injuries, and the damage done to the shelter...
Every detail was immediately calculated...
He saw the defenders’ dwindling ammunition, the shattered barricades, the broken artillery coughing smoke.
He noted the casualties... too many guards were cut down, blood staining the dirt. He assessed the enemy... five B‐Rank Sentinels still moving.
He frowned.
’They’re strong... but not invincible.’
Spirit Dominion surged within him.
This skill was a fusion of Spirit Pulse, Piercing Roar, and the last chains.

[ Spirit Dominion Lv2: Combines ranged burst, immobilization, and disruption into a single Spirit‐based attack. Releases a concussive wave of Spirit energy up to 15 meters, smashing chains that bind up to 2 targets for 3 seconds, while a piercing resonance destabilizes systems and reduces accuracy by 20% for 5 seconds.
Spirit Point Cost: 60
Cooldown: 18 seconds
Range: 15 meters ]
Energy gathered at his core, his aura flaring.
He raised his hand, unleashing a concussive wave of Spirit that slammed into the nearest Sentinel!
Boom!
The machine seemed to malfunction as its systems were disrupted by the chains of energy lashing around its limbs to hold it in place.
"Focus fire on that one!" Kai ordered the remaining Survivors, itching to kill these invaders.
His voice carried authority, cutting through the chaos.
The defenders obeyed, and rifles and grenades immediately started hammering the immobilized unit.
Bang! Bang! Bang!
As for the reason why Kai did that, it was simple...
’You all need to level up... Don’t waste this chance.’Kai mused.
Soon, their armors were finally taken care of. The B-Rank Sentinel’s defense was no longer a problem!
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Sentinel (B) ]
[ Experience Points distributed among all participants. ]
[ +800 Experience Points ]
Still, another B-Rank charged with a cannon raised.
This time, Kai’s body blurred as his Titan Step activated...

[ Titan Step Lv0: A fused mobility skill that allows the user to phase through attacks, charge forward with Spirit. Allows the user to phase through attacks for 1.5 seconds, gains 40% damage resistance while charging forward, and temporarily transforms the right arm to increase melee damage by 50% for the next strike.
Spirit Point Cost: 75
Cooldown: 25 seconds
Duration: 20 seconds ]

Just like that, with his armored energy coating his frame, his movement became a brutal speed and force. He collided with the machine, shoulder first, sending it skidding back into a collapsed trench.
Boom!
The defenders gasped. Althea, still catching her breath, felt her chest tighten.
’He’s really back... and he’s already turning the tide.’

Kai’s passive skills worked silently in the background. Bio‐Adaptive Constitution kept his body resilient, shrugging off strain. Great Protection layered his defenses, while Slayer’s Flow sharpened his instincts and reaction time...

[ Great Protection Lv0: Combines hardened defense with heightened combat resilience. Provides 25% physical defense, 15% damage resistance and stabilizes Spirit flow to reduce any further damage cost by Skills. ]

[ Slayer’s Flow Lv0: Enhances Spirit efficiency while sharpening instinctive awareness of hostile intent. Reduces Spirit cost of active skills by 10%, increases detection of enemy hostility within 20 meters, and improves reaction speed by 15%. ]
Kai exhaled as he looked at the remaining units...
"A few more... Let’s break them here."
And with that, Kai advanced with his black gear on!
In the meantime, when Alfie had arrived alongside Kai, he immediately went to help the team crushed by debris from the Snake Vessel.
Though his entrance was far less dramatic he didn’t mind it.
While Kai’s black gear was fighting, Alfie was already cracking his knuckles, grinning like a man about to smash open a tavern door.
"Alright, snake‐things," he muttered, hefting his massive mace onto his shoulder. "Let’s see how well you slither when you’re flat as pancakes."
The serpent‐like vessels swooped low, ready to destroy the walls as expected.
Defenders braced themselves, but Alfie didn’t wait.
His Gladiator Talent surged, and soon, his muscles were bulging, veins glowing faintly as Spirit energy coursed through him.
He charged forward, swinging his mace in wide arcs that looked more like a lumberjack chopping trees than a warrior fighting machines.
The first vessel dipped too close!
Alfie roared, leaping higher than anyone thought possible for a man his size, and brought his mace down with a thunderous crash.
Boom!
The serpent’s head crumpled like tin, its riders thrown off in a heap.
Alfie landed hard, laughing.
"Ha! One down! Who’s next?"
The second vessel tried to veer away, but Alfie wasn’t having it.
He sprinted after it, his heavy boots didn’t matter at all.
"Don’t run! I’m not done with you!" Aflie threw his mace like a cannonball, and just like that, the weapon spun over and over before smashing into the vessel’s body...
Crash!
The serpent buckled before it started spiraling into the ground.
Alfie jogged over, picked up his mace, and dusted it off as he’d just dropped a spoon.
"Two for me. Kai, you keeping count? I’m winning."
Defenders stared in disbelief...
Althea couldn’t help but smirk despite the chaos. His ridiculous bravado was even infectious.
He turned to the remaining Sentinels, twirling his mace like it weighed nothing.
"Alright, shiny boys. You saw what happened to the pets. Now it’s your turn. Come on, let’s dance!"
Even in the middle of blood and fire, Alfie’s humor cut through the tension. He wasn’t just fighting... he was performing, making the impossible look like a game.
And somehow, that reckless confidence gave the survivors the courage to keep standing.
Kai glanced at him as his mouth twitched in the faintest smirk. "Just don’t get yourself killed, Alfie."
Alfie grinned back, raising his mace. "Me? Nah. I’m too handsome to die."
And with that, the Gladiator charged again, ready to smash through whatever came next.

His voice carried authority, cutting through the chaos.

[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Sentinel (B) ]

chapters.title: Chapter 305: The Remaining Survivors and the Four Arms
paragraphs: "It’s done."
Soon, the battlefield fell silent as the last of the serpent vessels had been smashed apart, with their metallic bodies scattered across the shelter.
As for the B‐Rank Sentinels, they were now incapacitated, with most of them torn to pieces...
Kai stood amidst the wreckage as he assessed the situation...

He didn’t waste time celebrating. His first thought was for the people he had brought into this world. The four super soldiers and the young boy he had purchased as slaves were hidden, just as he had instructed.
They weren’t properly equipped for combat yet, so as soon as they arrived and realized that there was a battle going on, Kai had made it clear... survival came first.
Soon, he found them hiding away in the shelter’s lower chambers. They looked so worried but they were also unharmed.
Relief washed over him.
’Good. They listened.’
Outside, the defenders began to count the living. The numbers were grim.

Of the thirty or so people Kai had left behind to guard New Haven‐45, only thirteen remained. The rest had fallen in the brutal defense, their bodies lying among the ruins of barricades and shattered walls.
Althea’s face was also pale as she read the tally, Augustine silent beside her.
Kai’s expression hardened. "Thirteen... barely half."
The survivors bowed their heads. They looked so exhausted but alive.
They had fought with everything they had, and Kai knew their courage had bought precious time.
Still, the losses cut deep, even if the modified Sentinels were still active.
Then, through the Guild Chat, Kai reached out to his other bases.
The reports came in quickly, each one worse than the last.
Nadia, who was assigned to Haven-28, replied first.
[ Nadia: Kai, Haven‐28 has fallen. The Sentinels breached the walls after sustained bombardment. ]
[ Nadia: We lost most of our defenses and equipment in the attack. Ammunition and supplies were destroyed or taken. ]
[ Nadia: Out of the full garrison, only twelve people survived. The shelter itself is no longer functional. ]
[ Nadia: Haven‐28 is gone. Survivors are regrouping, but we’ll need relocation or reinforcement. ]
Kai clenched his fist as he read the message. Then, he confirmed the next message...
[ Aurora: Kai, Freedom Shelter has been overrun. The Snake-like vessel called Fangs broke through quickly and destroyed our fields ]
[ Aurora: We exhausted all weapons... rifles, grenades, even the stimulants... but it wasn’t enough. Supplies were destroyed during the breach. ]
[ Aurora: Fifteen survivors remain. The shelter structure is heavily damaged, walls collapsed, and it cannot be defended further. ]
[ Aurora: Freedom Shelter is compromised. Survivors await orders for evacuation or regrouping. Where do we go now? ]
Kai had no answer.
Where do they go? He had no idea... He planned to rebuild his shelter, but after this much destruction, it should be easier to find a different place to rebuild instead.
Then, Vera also sent her report.
[ Vera: Kai, Blue Grass Shelter could not hold. The Sentinels arrived in overwhelming numbers. ]
[ Vera: We made the decision to evacuate instead of defending. Twenty‐five survivors escaped into the wilderness. ]
[ Vera: The shelter itself was abandoned. Supplies and equipment were left behind. ]
[ Vera: Survivors are safe for now, but the shelter is lost. We’ll need guidance on where to regroup and rebuild. ]
"Seriously... So many deaths, and we’re not even here in the first place. That’s cheating." Kai couldn’t help but complain since there was no mention of this event at all.
They were only informed about the Auction Event that would last for two days.
However, the floating city above and the crimson sky weren’t part of it at all!
The weight of it all pressed down on Kai...
From four shelters, barely sixty‐five people remained alive.
The rest were gone, cut down by the machines or killed by the destruction they had created.
Kai clenched his fists.
’This is the cost of war. But it won’t end here.’
He looked at the survivors of New Haven‐45... Althea, Augustine, Irene, Mila, Alfie, and the others who had endured.
Their faces were weary, but their eyes still held fire.
They had seen death, but they had also seen victory.
First, Kai had to stabilize their situation since they had no idea if the floating city would send another attack...
"We lost many. But we’re still here... Let’s bury the dead and leave this place. We’re going to get stronger from now on."
The survivors straightened, their grief tempered by his words.
They knew the fight wasn’t over. The shelters had been bloodied, but they weren’t broken.
Meanwhile, Aurora and the others from Blue Grass Shelter gathered in the ruins, fifteen survivors in total.
Eight of them were the former slaves led by Noli.
The rest included Mei, Juno, Steven, Vera, the sculptor, the scout, and a young man with a common‐grade pyromancer talent.
Mei, as usual, took command. Though she was busy coordinating the group, she had let Vera send the Guild Chat report to Kai.
Now, she outlined their next move.

"We can’t stay here. The shelter’s walls are gone, and every building is shattered. But I remember an abandoned town not far from here. Its structures were still intact the last time I passed through. If we move quickly, we can claim it before anyone else does."
The survivors nodded. It wasn’t much, but it was hope. It was better than building a tent for now...
Before leaving, they gathered what remained of the precious blue grass patches.
Vera carefully bundled them... "If we can replant these, I can keep making concoctions. Without them, we lose one of our biggest advantages."
Mei agreed as she looked at the patches of grass before looking up in the sky... Thankfully, the flying city wasn’t sending out any snake-like vessels or Fangs just yet.
With supplies packed, they set out.
The path was rough, but they pressed on.
Noli kept his group close as the ex‐slaves carried baggage that could save their lives. The scout ranged ahead, while Steven and Juno carried what little remained of their weapons.
Just as the town’s outline appeared in the distance, their progress was halted.
"Stop..." Mei commanded.
A figure stepped into their path... It was a towering man with four arms!

chapters.title: Chapter 306: The Superhuman Guild
paragraphs: "Be careful, everyone..."
"Mhmm... I’m not sensing any hostility yet."
"There might be others lying in ambush," Mei muttered as she assessed the towering man with four arms blocking their path.
Although there was no hostility yet, his presence radiated menace. His eyes scanned the group, lingering on her, Vera, and other female survivors with a faint smirk.
"You’ve got strength,"
The four-armed man spoke with a deep voice...

"And you have some pretty faces too. Perfect for what we’re building. I am Aaron, a recruiter of the Superhuman Guild. Join us, and you’ll receive the Special Mutation Gene. It will improve your power beyond anything you’ve known... in exchange for mutation. That’s a cheap price of survival."

The group froze for a moment, exchanging glances. None of them had expected the towering figure to speak like that. From the way he blocked the road, they had assumed a fight was inevitable... not a recruitment pitch.
Juno tilted his head and muttered, "A recruiter? Out here?"
His tone carried disbelief. They had just been attacked by the Fangs and the B-Rank Sentinels. Being recruited by another Guild was the last thing on their mind.
Steven’s hand rested on the hilt of his weapon as he was still prepared to fight.
"I thought we were about to clash. Didn’t expect him to start offering deals. But don’t get too relaxed. I don’t think he has good intentions."
Vera frowned while clutching her bundled blue grass. "Eww... Special Mutation Gene...? He’s treating this like a trade. But mutation isn’t something you just accept so easily.
Mei kept her eyes on Aaron and answered. "We’re not interested. We already belong to the Codebreakers Guild."
The four‐armed man’s smile vanished. He knew about the Rank 1 Guild!
However, he didn’t believe them. It must be their way to reject and warn them, but that wouldn’t work.
"Codebreakers? I’ve seen a few people claiming that already... I’ll give you one last chance..."
Suddenly, from the shadows, five more figures emerged.
Each bore the marks of mutation.
One had four eyes, glowing faintly in the dark.
Another’s tail lashed like a whip, destroying a rock nearby...
A third had elongated arms with two elbow joints and clawed fingers, reaching unnaturally far.
The fourth also had four arms, but his skin was covered with hardened scales, like armor.
The last, on the other hand, had extra joints along his legs, allowing him to move with unsettling speed and flexibility.
The survivors tightened their grip on their weapons.
These mutants were different...
Still, Mei’s team weren’t completely defenseless...
Aside from X-07 to X-10, their four Modified Sentinels following behind, they had more firepower than ever!
They weren’t afraid. They had just come from the Black Market Auction hours ago.
Though most consumables had been spent against the Fangs and the B‐Rank Sentinels, they had secured several priceless items.
One of them was the cloak!
[ Phantom Cloak ]
[ Grade: Superior Equipment ]

[ Description: A tactical cloak woven with adaptive fibers that disperse and absorb high‐energy attacks. Durability is limited; prolonged exposure to concentrated fire will eventually degrade its effectiveness. ]
The cloak had already saved them from the assault of the B-Ranks... Now, with their own plasma rifles in hand, the survivors knew that they had a chance to fight back!
Mei’s voice was calm but threatening... "If it’s a fight you want, then you’ll get one."
Juno, who had Master‐Grade Telekinesis, also took out his 12 Rare-Grade Knives ready for deployment. These knives were purchased in the Auction Realm for 30 Survivor Medals each!
Then, Steven, with his Superior Iron Will Combatant, brought out his halberd that was also from the Auction Realm!
Meanwhile, Mei just vanished using her Living Camouflage Talent as she was preparing to ambush them for later!
"You’re all stubborn... Don’t worry, I’ll take care of you all!"
The moment Aaron’s smirk faded, the clash began.
Still, only four of the six mutated figures moved first, as they moved forward with unnatural speed.
The one with four eyes scanned the battlefield, staying at the back, giving warnings to his allies as he tracked every movement.
The tail‐mutant, on the other hand, lashed out and smashed a boulder into shards, while the elongated‐armed fighter reached across the ground, targeting Steven in front...
At the same time, the scaled four‐armed mutant advanced like a living tank, while the jointed runner ran in zigzags, too fast for ordinary eyes to follow!
Mei’s command, however, came in an instant!
"Sentinels, fire!"
X‐07 through X‐10 raised their plasma rifles in unison.
The weapons hummed, then unleashed bursts of burning energy.
One of the mutants almost dropped as a plasma bolt tore through his shoulder, but the scaled one pushed forward, deflecting shots with his hardened hide!
Still, as the enemies got closer, using Plasma Rifles would get too dangerous, as they might hit their allies!
"You’re not going anywhere!" Juno shoulted as his knives hovered in the air.
These twelve Rare‐Grade blades were spinning like a deadly storm!

With a flick of his hand, they shot forward, piercing into the tail‐mutant’s flank. The creature roared, whipping its tail wildly due to pain... but Juno’s telekinesis forced the knives deeper, pinning it against the ground!
Thud! Thud! Thud!
Steven stepped into the front line, halberd raised.
His Superior Iron Will Combatant talent made him immovable.
"Come!" He taunted.
The elongated‐armed mutant charged, but Steven caught the strike on his weapon and shoved forward!
Bam!
His sheer resilience broke the mutant’s momentum.
Vera then threw a couple of smoke grenades, forcing the jointed runner to stumble, his speed disrupted.
"Don’t let them regroup!" she shouted.
Meanwhile, Mei had vanished. Her Living Camouflage talent made her invisible to the naked eye.
She circled wide, slipping past the scaled mutant’s guard.
In silence, she prepared her ambush, with her dagger poised for a lethal strike.
Aaron himself finally moved, his four arms flexing as he equipped his four swords!
Thud! Thud! Thud!
Suddenly, plasma bolts slammed into him, but he shrugged them off, his mutated body absorbing the impact so seamlessly!
"You think your toys will save you? Mutation is the only path forward!"

Meanwhile, Mei just vanished using her Living Camouflage Talent as she was preparing to ambush them for later!
"You’re all stubborn...
Don’t worry, I’ll take care of you all!"
The moment Aaron’s smirk faded, the clash began.
Still, only four of the six mutated figures moved first, as they moved forward with unnatural speed.
The one with four eyes scanned the battlefield, staying at the back, giving warnings to his allies as he tracked every movement.
The tail‐mutant, on the other hand, lashed out and smashed a boulder into shards, while the elongated‐armed fighter reached across the ground, targeting Steven in front...
At the same time, the scaled four‐armed mutant advanced like a living tank, while the jointed runner ran in zigzags, too fast for ordinary eyes to follow!
Mei’s command, however, came in an instant!
"Sentinels, fire!"
X‐07 through X‐10 raised their plasma rifles in unison.
The weapons hummed, then unleashed bursts of burning energy.
One of the mutants almost dropped as a plasma bolt tore through his shoulder, but the scaled one pushed forward, deflecting shots with his hardened hide!
Still, as the enemies got closer, using Plasma Rifles would get too dangerous, as they might hit their allies!
"You’re not going anywhere!" Juno shoulted as his knives hovered in the air.
These twelve Rare‐Grade blades were spinning like a deadly storm!
With a flick of his hand, they shot forward, piercing into the tail‐mutant’s flank.
The creature roared, whipping its tail wildly due to pain... but Juno’s telekinesis forced the knives deeper, pinning it against the ground!
Thud!
Thud!
Thud!
Steven stepped into the front line, halberd raised.
His Superior Iron Will Combatant talent made him immovable.
"Come!" He taunted.
The elongated‐armed mutant charged, but Steven caught the strike on his weapon and shoved forward!
Bam!
His sheer resilience broke the mutant’s momentum.
Vera then threw a couple of smoke grenades, forcing the jointed runner to stumble, his speed disrupted.
"Don’t let them regroup!" she shouted.
Meanwhile, Mei had vanished.
Her Living Camouflage talent made her invisible to the naked eye.
She circled wide, slipping past the scaled mutant’s guard.
In silence, she prepared her ambush, with her dagger poised for a lethal strike.
Aaron himself finally moved, his four arms flexing as he equipped his four swords!
Thud!
Thud!
Thud!
Suddenly, plasma bolts slammed into him, but he shrugged them off, his mutated body absorbing the impact so seamlessly!
"You think your toys will save you?
Mutation is the only path forward!"

chapters.title: Chapter 307: Chase
paragraphs: As soon as Aaron taunted, the four Modified Sentinels, X‐07 through X‐10, opened fire in disciplined bursts...
Thanks to their combat programming, they coordinated their attacks well. Plasma bolts passed through the ruins, forcing the mutants to scatter.
Even if they have a hard skin that could protect them for one or two Plasma shots, it didn’t mean that they could take it head-on endlessly.
There must be a limit!
The one with four eyes started giving commands as his vision was tracking every angle.
"Left flank! Duck low!"
His coordination kept the group from being annihilated in the opening volley.
"Tsk..." Mei frowned as her ambush failed because of the four-eyed mutant. It seemed that it had the ability to keep up with her ability...
Still, only one of them could follow her movements, so as long as she timed her attacks, she should be able to deal quite a damage.
At this time, Noli and the ex‐slaves, eight in number, raised their rifles as well. Their formation was tight, as they had already trained for this before.
They weren’t elite fighters, but desperation made them steady.
Soon, gunfire rattled, bullets pinging off stone and striking the jointed runner, slowing his zigzag advance.
Steven braced himself at the front.
The elongated‐armed mutant charged again with its long and sharp nails stretching unnaturally far...
"Ha!"
Steven’s halberd intercepted the strike, and it even created sparks that flew everywhere!
Clang!
Then, with a roar, Steven shoved forward, his Superior Iron Will talent was still making him immovable.
"Bring it on!"
Steven’s Spirit Points were at its peak thanks to the boosting potions he consumed. Thanks to that, his Passive Gene Skills were able to steady himself.
The mutant was pushed back, but Steven pressed forward...
This time, only four mutants would have to be targeted by their gunners!
Just like that, his halberd swept to keep the mutant at bay.
"Don’t forget about me!"
Suddenly, Juno’s knives spun in the air, twelve Rare‐Grade blades orbiting him like a storm.
With a flick, he sent half of them slicing toward the tail‐mutant.
The creature whipped its serrated tail, deflecting two blades, but the rest buried deep into its torso.
Juno clenched his fist... His telekinesis was forcing the knives to twist inside the flesh!
"Just die ugly creature!"
The mutant shrieked in pain as it started thrashing wildly.
It seemed that these mutants didn’t have strong internal organs.
This time, Vera hurled another vial he bought in the Auction Realm...
Crash!
It shattered at the scaled mutant’s feet, releasing a burst of corrosive smoke!
The creature coughed, and its skin or scales started sizzling! Still, it pushed forward regardless, its armored hide resisting most of the damage.
"Damn it, he’s tougher than I thought!" Vera muttered, already reaching for another concoction.
Mei, on the other hand, was nowhere to be seen.
Her Living Camouflage talent made her invisible, and she used it to circle behind Aaron.
Because of the four-eyed mutant, she stayed behind the cover of the smokes and moved silently as a shadow... She then crept closer, with her dagger ready.
As soon as Aaron charged with his four swords, Plasma bolts struck him, but his mutated body absorbed the energy!
Thud!
He slammed into the Sentinels, blades clashing against their metallic body!
X‐08 blocked Aaron with its rifle, while X‐09 countered with a bayonet strike.
Thud! Aaron grinned, his four arms overwhelming their defenses.
Crash! Crash!
With a wave of his sword, both X-08 and X-09 had their heads severed!
It was at this time that the jointed runner recovered from Vera’s smoke and charged forward.
Because its legs bent at unnatural angles, it was actually so difficult to predict its movement..
As they thought that he would dash forward, he suddenly leapt high instead, aiming for Juno. But Noli’s group opened fire, bullets riddling his body mid‐air.
He landed hard, bleeding, yet still alive.
"Keep shooting!" Noli shouted.
Steven also roared as he locked weapons with the elongated‐armed mutant. The halberd clashed against claws, neither side giving ground.
Then Steven injected himself with the Gene Stimulant and pushed harder, his Iron Will was giving him strength as well!
With a brutal shove, he impaled the mutant through the chest. Blood sprayed, and the creature collapsed, twitching. One down.

Juno redirected his knives, sending them spinning toward the four‐eyed mutant. But the creature anticipated every strike, dodging with uncanny precision. "Behind you!" he shouted to his allies, his extra vision giving him perfect battlefield awareness.

The tail‐mutant lashed out, sweeping its serrated appendage across the ground. It struck two of Noli’s men, sending them sprawling with deep cuts. Juno snarled, telekinetically driving his knives deeper into the creature’s torso. With a final twist, the mutant collapsed, tail thrashing weakly before falling still. Two down.
Aaron’s swords clashed against the Sentinels, his strength forcing them back.
X‐07 fired point‐blank, and its plasma bolt seared into his shoulder.
"You!"
He grunted at the pain but kept fighting!
"You can’t win! Mutation is the future!" he roared.
Mei struck then.
She appeared behind him with a dagger!
SSaaakk!
Her blade sank into his side, piercing flesh.
It was a move that the four-eyed mutant failed to notice!
Aaron roared in pain, but he started spinning with his swords. Unfortunately, Mei just vanished again, slipping back into the smoke and used her camouflage before he could retaliate.
"You coward!"
Vera hurled another concoction, this one was exploding into flames. The jointed runner screamed as fire engulfed him!
He collapsed, burning!
But the scaled mutant was still advancing.
Plasma bolts ricocheted off his armored hide, and even Vera’s concoctions barely dented him. He slammed into Steven, four arms hammering down.
Steven blocked with his halberd, but the sheer force drove him to his knees.
His Gene Stimulant was losing its effects already!
Juno sent his remaining knives at the scaled mutant, but they bounced off the hardened scales. "He’s too tough!" Juno shouted.
Aaron regrouped with the scaled mutant and the four‐eyed one. "Fall back!" he ordered, realizing the battle was turning against them.
Two of them were basically immobilized and would soon die at this point...
However, Mei wouldn’t just let them escape!
"Chase after them!"
It was at this point that the two remaining Modified Sentinels, including Noli’s group, used their Emergency Thruster Packs to chase!

chapters.title: Chapter 308: The New Shelter and the Reputation Store
paragraphs: The thruster’s engine noise filled the area...
These compact propulsion packs were small, but they were capable of lifting about 100kg of weight!
Just like that blue flames burst downward, lifting Noli’s group and the two remaining Sentinels into the air.
The sudden acceleration carried them above the battlefield, granting a vantage point that Aaron and his allies hadn’t anticipated.
The survivors immediately positioned themselves, cutting off the escape route.
From above, rifles and plasma fire rained down, forcing the scaled mutant and the four‐eyed one to retreat into cover.
Aaron was filled with fury as he raised his four swords, but the thruster‐borne assault was not stopping at all!
"Block their path!" Mei commanded from below as she was not letting these members of the Superhuman Guild just leave after they tried attacking them and looked at them with those lecherous gazes.
Soon, the airborne squad angled their thrusters, landing in specific positions that sealed off their escape...
The mutants were trapped.
Now, they just had to execute their plan!
Grenade launchers were raised. Then, compact tubes clicked, and it was followed by explosions...
Boom! Boom! Boom!
After the blast, there was smoke and fire engulfing the scaled mutant! His armored hide cracked under the bombardment.
"Shit..." The four‐eyed mutant was also unable to find a solution, his coordination wasn’t that important anymore!
Aaron tried to shield them with his sword-spinning defense, but the grenades detonated too fast, too close.
The Modified Sentinels advanced and, thanks to their programming, they calculated every angle, forcing Aaron to parry desperately.
Noli’s group also fired from above, and thanks to that, their rifles struck the mutants with suppressive fire.
Steven charged again with his halberd...
"Take this mutant!"
He slammed into the scaled mutant, driving the weapon through a weak point in its cracked armor. With a burst of his Spirit Energy, the figure collapsed, lifeless!
Juno’s knives also moved swiftly, piercing the four‐eyed mutant’s chest.
His telekinesis twisted the blades, shredding his organs!
It happened so quickly. The mutant fell, and his extra vision faded into darkness... He barely had the time to process the pain because of how his organs failed immediately.
"Finally..." Mei muttered as she saw how this mutant perished.
Still, Aaron continued to fight with his four swords, clashing against plasma bolts and steel.
But the grenade barrage had weakened him...
Soon, smoke started choking his lungs, wounds accumulated, and after the bombardment ended, Mei struck from behind once more.
Thud!
This time, her dagger sliced deeper...
"Y-you—"
She wanted to continue, but she sensed Aaron’s attempt to cut her arm!
She immediately leapt back to escape, but she didn’t forget to give her command.
"End it!" she shouted.
The remaining Modified Sentinels and Noli’s group fired in unison. Plasma bolts tore through Aaron’s body...
Even Steven’s halberd followed, cleaving across his chest while Juno’s knives pinned him in place!
But for some reason, the mutated human was still not dying!
"You’re stubborn!"
Vera finally threw her last vial... It was an incendiary concoction that exploded in flame!
Soon, Aaron roared, defiant to the end, but the combined assault overwhelmed him. His body collapsed amid fire and smoke, swords clattering to the ground.
Silence fell. The thrusters powered down, and the survivors landed back on solid ground.
The enemy was annihilated!
Mei sighed in relief as she felt that her body could no longer take any more Gene Stimulant or Spirit Boosting Potion.
"It’s finally done."
Noli’s group regrouped as they confirmed that their thruster packs only had 30% of their fuel reserves.
"I think we should leave this place now..." Vera muttered as she checked the bundles of blue grass, still intact.
Steven leaned on his halberd and nodded.
Juno also recalled his knives as he looked at Mei.
They had won. The Superhuman Guild’s ambush had been crushed, but there might be more of them.
"Let’s go... I just sent Kai a message through the Guild Chat. All the scattered shelters will gather in that abandoned town I mentioned... They’re all riding motorbikes, so they’ll be quick."
Meanwhile, Nadia led the weary survivors of Haven‐28 westward...
It had been a couple of days since they returned from the Auction Realm.
Because of the battle against the Fangs and the B-Rank Sentinels, their bikes were destroyed, and they had to travel on foot.
Well, it was also better this way as they could easily hide from the canopy of the trees if needed.
At this time, however, her boots were crunching against the broken asphalt. Apparently, the group finally reached the outskirts of the abandoned town Mei had mentioned through the Guild Chat.
The twelve of them moved cautiously, weapons still in hand, eyes scanning for threats.
They had endured the fall of their shelter, and though exhaustion weighed heavily, the sight ahead stirred a flicker of hope.
Wooden palisades were already being erected along the perimeter.
Survivors from other shelters hammered beams into place, and even from afar, they could tell that these people working under the sun had sweat streaking their faces...
They could also see how they worked with urgency.
Thud! Thud! Thud!
The rhythmic thud of mallets and the scrape of timber echoed across the field...
Soon, Nadia slowed, raising a hand to signal the others to halt.
Well, she noticed a few guards eyeing them already, and she didn’t want to cause any misunderstandings.
Henry, rifle slung across his shoulder, muttered, "They’re already fortifying. Looks like Mei wasn’t lying."

Enzo adjusted the strap of his pack. As he observed through the outskirts of the town, he immediately noted the crude but effective construction. "Not bad. With reinforcement, these walls could hold against another wave."
Renji walked silently beside them with his two androids, Android‐9 and Android‐18, flanking him like sentinels.
Meanwhile, the rest of the survivors were finally filled with joy...
Finally, they could rest after walking for so long! They wanted to take a bath, have a warm meal, and sleep like a log!
They knew that it was possible if Kai, the Guild Leader with mysterious magic to produce resources, was present!
While Nadia and her group were on the outskirts of the town, Kai was also busy.
He was inside the vast warehouse, the first building repaired after entering the abandoned town.
He stood among towering stacks of crates and pallets.
This was now the main storage of the newly christened Codebreakers Shelter, a fortified quarter of the town that would unify the survivors from all four scattered shelters under his command.
The warehouse smelled of fresh timber and oil, and its walls were reinforced with steel plates.
It wasn’t like Cameron City, with its vast defenses and capacity to repel B‐Rank and even A‐Rank machines, but Kai knew this place could become formidable in its own way.
With his Infinite Gift Pack system, he could produce resources endlessly, and that alone gave them an edge.

From the Energy Gift Packs, Entertainment Gift Packs, Food Gift Packs, Medical Gift Packs, Shelter Gift Pack, Stealth Gift Packs, Survival Tools Gift Packs, Transport Gift Packs, Water Gift Pack, and Weapon Gift Packs, Kai was able to stabilize the supply of the whole shelter.
Including the bulk items bought from the Auction Realm, plus the chickens and other resources, their small shelter seemed really great right now.
The warehouse was filled quickly, aisles lined with equipment that no ordinary settlement could hope to gather.
Soon, other Survivors moved among the stacks as they itemized them. For them, this was more than supply... it was proof that the Codebreakers Guild had a future.
"This should be done for now." Kai muttered as he looked around.
All these items could be retrieved by the Survivors in exchange for Survivor Medals.
This included the Skill Fusion Crystals on display. These crystals were rare, capable of merging Skill into stronger forms, but they came at a cost.
Originally, he planned to sell them for 10 Survivor Medals each for Guild Members.
"But we all have zero Survivor Medals," Kai muttered, recalling the reset after the Auction Realm event.

No one could afford them outright. Instead, he had tied the crystals to Guild Missions... tasks that would earn resources, including survivor medals through service and risk. For those desperate, loans could be arranged, but repayment would be mandatory.
He looked over the warehouse again... and with a satisfied smile, he returned to his tent...
Of course, this was a field tent from the Enhanced Shelter Gift Pack and was quite spacious.
Well, since most buildings were still under construction, they had to set up several tents for now.
Anyway, as soon as he returned, he just washed himself for a bit and opened the Reputation Store. There should be a reset right now.
[ Reputation Store Accessed ]
[ Current Reputation Points: 85 ]
[ Store Inventory - Weekly Rotation ]
’Just eighty-five, huh... It’s really hard earning them right now.’Kai muttered as he looked at the first item.
[ Miniature Pulse Mine ] [ 15/15 ]
[ Cost: 1 RP ]
[ Effect: Deployable mine that detonates with a violent magnetic surge. On activation, it overloads circuits, fries processors, and permanently disables mechanical units within a 10-meter radius. ]
