With his Infinite Gift Pack system, he could produce resources endlessly, and that alone gave them an edge.

From the Energy Gift Packs, Entertainment Gift Packs, Food Gift Packs, Medical Gift Packs, Shelter Gift Pack, Stealth Gift Packs, Survival Tools Gift Packs, Transport Gift Packs, Water Gift Pack, and Weapon Gift Packs, Kai was able to stabilize the supply of the whole shelter.
Including the bulk items bought from the Auction Realm, plus the chickens and other resources, their small shelter seemed really great right now.
The warehouse was filled quickly, aisles lined with equipment that no ordinary settlement could hope to gather.
Soon, other Survivors moved among the stacks as they itemized them.
For them, this was more than supply... it was proof that the Codebreakers Guild had a future.
"This should be done for now." Kai muttered as he looked around.
All these items could be retrieved by the Survivors in exchange for Survivor Medals.
This included the Skill Fusion Crystals on display.
These crystals were rare, capable of merging Skill into stronger forms, but they came at a cost.
Originally, he planned to sell them for 10 Survivor Medals each for Guild Members.
"But we all have zero Survivor Medals," Kai muttered, recalling the reset after the Auction Realm event.
No one could afford them outright.
Instead, he had tied the crystals to Guild Missions... tasks that would earn resources, including survivor medals through service and risk.
For those desperate, loans could be arranged, but repayment would be mandatory.
He looked over the warehouse again... and with a satisfied smile, he returned to his tent...
Of course, this was a field tent from the Enhanced Shelter Gift Pack and was quite spacious.
Well, since most buildings were still under construction, they had to set up several tents for now.
Anyway, as soon as he returned, he just washed himself for a bit and opened the Reputation Store.
There should be a reset right now.
[ Reputation Store Accessed ]
[ Current Reputation Points: 85 ]
[ Store Inventory - Weekly Rotation ]
’Just eighty-five, huh...
It’s really hard earning them right now.’Kai muttered as he looked at the first item.
[ Miniature Pulse Mine ] [ 15/15 ]
[ Cost: 1 RP ]
[ Effect: Deployable mine that detonates with a violent magnetic surge.
On activation, it overloads circuits, fries processors, and permanently disables mechanical units within a 10-meter radius. ]

chapters.title: Chapter 309: The Status Crystal and the Construction
paragraphs: "Miniature pulse mine for only 1 RP? You’re all mine!" Kai exclaimed as he saw the first item.
Of course, it was cheaper compared to the previous pulse mines because of its limited range, but Kai was already satisfied with this.
He immediately purchased them all, leaving him with only 60 Points.
Then, he continued checking the other items. If he spent more, he probably had to complete more Guild Missions to get a few more Reputation Points, but he didn’t mind.
He needed to rebuild his base since he had no idea when the floating cities would act up again.
[ Muscle Fiber Enhancer ] [ 10/10 ]
[ Cost: 3 RP ]
[ Effect: A single‐use injectable serum that temporarily strengthens muscle fibers. Increases Strength and Endurance by 25% for 30 minutes. ]
[ Note: Overuse may cause muscle tearing and fatigue. ]
[ High‐Jump Boots ] [ 5/5 ]
[ Cost: 3 RP ]
[ Effect: Mystical boots with movement amplifiers. Allows the wearer to leap up to 6 meters vertically or 10 meters horizontally. ]
[ Note: Spirit Points must be paid after each use. ]
[ Nightly Vitality Tonic ] [ 15/15 ]
[ Cost: 3 RP ]
[ Effect: A rare tonic designed to restore and enhance natural vitality. Permanently improves reproductive health, stamina, and overall physical vigor regardless of age or prior damage. ]
They were all quite interesting...
’Nightly, huh...’
Kai chuckled as he knew exactly about its real purpose.
Anyway, it wasn’t the most important item just yet.
[ Spirit Pill ] [ 5/5 ]
[ Cost: 100 RP ] [ Effect: A rare alchemical pill that permanently increases the user’s maximum Spirit Points by 100 ]
[ Note: Extremely rare. Only compatible with survivors who have stable constitutions. Risk of rejection if consumed recklessly. ]
"What?" Kai was shocked to see the item being sold.
It was a permanent increase, and it wasn’t a measly ten points, it was a hundred points!
That would give him a huge advantage. After all, he could cast several more Gene Skills with that much.
In the meantime, Tomas wiped the sweat from his brow as he looked at their new shelter, the Codebreakers Shelter...
The sun was high up in the red sky as he hauled another slab of stone into place.
His arms ached, but his Iron Skin passive skill made the strain bearable.

Even at Level 0, it gave him resilience that others lacked... Thanks to that, cuts from sharp rock barely scratched him, bruises faded quickly, and the blunt force of heavy lifting didn’t cripple his muscles the way it did for the younger survivors.

Weeks ago, when the Status Crystal revealed his level and skill, Tomas had felt a surge of pride. He was actually Level 5, and it wasn’t extraordinary compared to the Guild’s elites, but for someone who barely gotten a reward of Golden Liquid before, it meant that he had some talent.
Then, during the siege of the Fangs and the B‐Rank Sentinels, he had stood at the front, firing grenade launchers at close range.
The explosions rattled his bones, but Iron Skin kept him steady. Without it, he might have been torn apart.
Now, though, since he hadn’t checked his status in weeks, he wondered if his mastery had improved, if Iron Skin had grown tougher, or if another skill had awakened.
The thought lingered as he worked, but for now, orders were orders.
Nadia had assigned him to wall construction, and Tomas knew his strength was needed here.
The wall itself was ambitious.
They weren’t covering the entire town... that would take months that they didn’t have.
Instead, the Guild had decided to fortify one‐quarter of the settlement and inaugurated the Codebreakers Shelter.
The plan was to build a two‐meter‐thick stone wall around this section, reinforced with steel beams scavenged from collapsed warehouses.
Tomas grunted as he lifted another block, setting it into place beside Enzo’s team.
Looking around, everyone was busy.
Thud! Thud! Thud!
He heard the pounding of hammers.
Scrape! Scrape! Scrape!
There was also the grinding of stone against stone.
Clang! Clang! Clang!
Finally, there was the ringing sound of steel rods being driven into the foundation.
Dozens of survivors worked side by side.
Their hands were already blistered from labor, but thanks to their warm food and some potions, they were able to work efficiently...
Some carried timber, others mixed mortar, while the stronger ones, like Tomas, hauled stone. The wall was rising slowly, but it was at a steady pace.

He paused for a moment and took a break by leaning against the half‐finished barrier. From here, he could see the outline of the town... broken streets, shattered buildings, the temporary tents, and the Modified Sentinels patrolling.
Well, these X-Series of Sentinels weren’t that capable of complex tasks just yet.
They were only good at combat, but definitely not at tasks involving construction. They’d cause more trouble.
Nonetheless, beyond the perimeter, the wilderness stretched. They had no idea if there would be another attack, so they had to hurry with their work.
Tomas then whispered a prayer... "Please, let the Advanced Barrier Generator activate soon..."
That device was their true hope. Once powered, it would project a barrier field over the walls, amplifying their strength and repelling assaults.
Without it, the stone wall was only a first line of defense. Against another wave of B‐Rank Sentinels, or worse, it might not be enough.
Still, Tomas kept working.
Each stone was important, and they were hoping that it would be completed within a week, or at the very least, if they didn’t run out of stone.
Clank... Clank... Clank...
Nearby, Tomas heard the sound of mechanical joints and realized that Renji’s androids were carrying beams...
Unlike the X-Series of Sentinels, these ones were more adept at controlling their strength and balance. They could also receive complicated instructions, allowing them to be helpful in construction.
At this time, Tomas noticed how Nadia supervised from the scaffolding... She was still as beautiful as well.
Then, he saw Steven and Juno inspecting the firing positions along the wall.
They seemed to be making sure that they could defend properly... Everyone had a role.
Tomas’s role was simple... use his strength.
As soon as he rested for a bit, he finally got back to work...
As the sun dipped lower, shadows stretched across the construction site.
The wall was already waist‐high in some places, nearly complete in others. Tomas felt his muscles burn, but he kept going, stone after stone, beam after beam.
Later on, he heard that they could use the Status Crystal again. It would be available for 50 people. He had to line up after this.
He imagined the Status Crystal glowing again, showing him not just Level 5, but perhaps Level 6. Maybe Iron Skin had reached Level 1, granting him resistance to blades or even bullets.
The thought made him smile faintly.
’Hehe... Maybe I can request a Gene Skill Crystal or something...’
"Hey, Tomas! What are you doing?" Henry called from the scaffolding. "We need another load on the west side. Think you can manage?"
Tomas nodded, hefting another slab onto his shoulder. "On it."
The weight pressed down, but his body held firm.
Iron Skin absorbed the strain, and his muscles refused to give in.
He trudged across the site, setting the stone into place with a grunt...
"I can do this... The dinner will be super tasty later."
Just like that, the wall rose higher.
The Guild’s shelter grew stronger and soon, the work for the day was over...
It was already eight in the evening, but none of them minded it at all.
Now, it was time for dinner!
Dinner that evening was a welcome relief after the long hours of construction.
Mila, the shelter’s chef, had taken charge of the warehouse supplies and transformed the scattered rations into something hearty and comforting...
From vacuum‐sealed packs, she prepared steaming bowls of instant soup, adding some vegetables and a touch of protein concentrate to thicken the broth.
Canned goods were opened and simmered together with some beans, corn, and meat chunks, creating a stew that smelled far richer than its humble ingredients.
On another stove, she boiled instant noodles, mixing them with mayonnaise and canned tuna to make a creamy, filling dish.
Granola bars were crumbled into bowls alongside dried fruits and nuts, turning them into a sweet dessert.

Coffee sachets and tea bags were brewed in large kettles as well. Of course, for those who don’t drink coffee, fruit juice packs were chilled in basins of cold water, ready to refresh the exhausted workers.
By the time the food was laid out, the survivors gathered eagerly...
Mila also moved among them, making sure everyone had enough.
"Thanks for the meal!"
Tomas ate quickly, savoring the warmth of the soup and the crunch of nuts. Soon, he felt renewed. When the meal ended, he stood and stretched, then made his way across the open field.
There, a tent had been set up, and inside it was the Status Crystal that everyone could use!
It was only available for 50 people, so he didn’t want to be late.
As soon as he got closer, he soon heard some exclamations inside!
"Whooo! Amer! You got a new Gene Skill?! Awesome!"

chapters.title: Chapter 310: The New Skills
paragraphs: The blue panel showing the status of the Survivors wouldn’t last for long. There was only a 10-second timeframe before it was gone.
Because of that, Tomas moved quickly as he was also curious about Amer’s status.
He heard how Amer consumed several types of Gene Enhancement Serums and how he reached level 10, so he knew that he’d have an extraordinary status compared to them.
Thud...
Tomas was able to enter the tent and realized that there were already seven people inside.
Still, his attention swiftly focused on the blue crystal at the center.
[ Name: Amer ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 11 ]
[ Physique Rating: D- ]
[ Active Skills: Silent Dash ]
[ Passive Skills: Spirit Sense Lv1, Dexterity Flow Lv1 ]
[ Silent Dash: Channels spirit energy into legs, propelling the user forward in a sudden burst of speed up to 5 meters that ignores terrain obstacles.
Cost: 20 Spirit Points.
Cooldown: 12 seconds. ]
[ Spirit Sense (Level 1): Heightens awareness through spirit energy, detecting subtle movements and threats. It gives a minor boost to reaction speed. ]
[ Dexterity Flow (Level 1): Enhances coordination, improving agility and precision. It improves evasion chance. ]
"Silent Dash..." Tomas repeated as he saw the Gene Skill.
With Amer’s Spirit Sense, his sensitivity to spiritual energy was leagues beyond theirs.
So it wasn’t really that surprising if he was able to obtain a Gene Skill. Still, Tomas and a few others couldn’t help but feel a little jealous.
"Let me try next!" Another man spoke.
Tomas recognized the man since he was also part of the construction group.
Based on their previous conversation, the last time he had checked, he was only Level 5 with only one passive skill, Hardy Constitution.
Over the past weeks, he had a few drops of Golden Liquid so he should have a decent level by now.
[ Name: Leron ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 7 ]
[ Spirit: 50 / 50 ]
[ Physique Rating: E+ ]
[ Active Skills: None ]
[ Passive Skills: Hardy Constitution Lv4 ]
[ Hardy Constitution (Level 4): Grants minor resistance to fatigue and illness. Slightly improves recovery rate when resting. ]
"What?!"
"Level four?"
"How did you increase your mastery so quickly?"
"I guess you can’t get sick anymore with that constitution, huh."

Leron was also unsure of the answer. Still, he felt like it was related to the fact that he had been exposed to a lot of the poison or the strange herbs that Aurora had been managing in the Freedom Shelter before.
’It must be related to that, but I’m not sure.’
Anyway, a few more Survivors continued checking, and aside from being two or three levels higher, there was only a slight increase in their Skill Mastery.
It was unlike Amer, who gained a new skill.
Soon, it was Tomas’ turn.
"Ohh... Tomas. We’ll wait for you. Let’s report our progress to Sir Kai together."
"Yes!"
Just like that, the others waited for him as they needed to inform Kai or his representative about their new skill or any progress, so they could be given proper jobs depending on their stat.
Soon, Tomas touched the crystal, and after a few seconds, his new stat appeared.
[ Name: Tomas ]
[ Title: None ]
[ Level: 9 ]
[ Physique Rating: D ]
[ Active Skills: Silent Breathing Lv0, Shadow Step Lv0 ]
[ Passive Skills: Iron Skin Lv1, Sharpshooter Lv0 ]
[ Iron Skin (Level 1): The body’s surface has toughened further, granting resistance to cuts, bruises, blunt force, and minor blade damage. Reduces physical damage taken by 15%. ]
[ Sharpshooter (Level 0): Enhances firearm accuracy through refined muscle control and focus. Slightly increases hit rate when wielding firearms. ]
[ Silent Breathing (Level 0): A stealth technique that slows heart rate and controls breath. Reduces noise and presence, making detection harder that lasts until you move.
Cost: 50 Spirit Points
Cooldown: 30 seconds ]
[ Seven Silent Step (Level 0): Channels spirit energy into the body, allowing the user to move silently and reduce presence for seven steps. The effect is significantly better in the darkness.
Cost: 25 Spirit Points
Cooldown: 30 seconds ]
The moment Tomas’s new status appeared, the tent filled with gasps.
"Level nine?! Your improvement is even better than mine!" Amer blurted out.
"He gained two active skills at once... Silent Breathing and Seven Silent Steps!" another said in disbelief.
The envy could be seen...
Tomas had gone from a sturdy frontline worker to someone with stealth techniques that most of them could only dream of.
"I didn’t know I had these skills... How am I supposed to use them?"
"Now that you know the, you just have to imagine it... Maybe call out the name of your skill in your mind..."
"What a pity... If I knew I had these skills, I wouldn’t struggle during the siege."
"Right... Sir Russel said that he didn’t know he was using his Roar Skill as well. It’s okay to not know you have a skill."
Tomans wryly smiled.
His Iron Skin had gotten better, and now he had Sharpshooter precision on top of it.
The others looked at him with a mix of admiration and frustration, wondering why their own progress hadn’t been as dramatic.

Tomas scratched the back of his neck, embarrassed by the attention. "It seems the serum I took works well with me. Right, it wasn’t just Alpha Gene Enhancement... it was Prime Gene Enhancement. Maybe that’s the reason. I guess I was compatible."
That explanation only fueled the envy further.
Several survivors exchanged glances, already considering whether they should request Prime Gene Enhancement Serums instead of the standard Alpha ones.
If Tomas could get new skills, then perhaps they could too.
Soon, the group left the tent together to make their report.
Outside Kai’s tent, they were surprised to see Sera waiting...
She still looked beautiful as ever.
"Are you here to report your progress?" She asked.
"Yes!"
"Let me hear about them instead." Sera said softly.
None of them rejected the idea, and soon, she received their report, even congratulating all eight of them for their progress.
Her words made them blush... There was pride mixed with embarrassment before they left quietly afterward.
Inside, Kai opened his tent flap and asked what had happened...
At this time, Sera noticed some changes in Kai’s pupil and recalled something...
"Have you reached Level 40?"

How am I supposed to use them?"
"Now that you know the, you just have to imagine it...
Maybe call out the name of your skill in your mind..."
"What a pity...
If I knew I had these skills, I wouldn’t struggle during the siege."
"Right...
Sir Russel said that he didn’t know he was using his Roar Skill as well.
It’s okay to not know you have a skill."
Tomans wryly smiled.
His Iron Skin had gotten better, and now he had Sharpshooter precision on top of it.
The others looked at him with a mix of admiration and frustration, wondering why their own progress hadn’t been as dramatic.
Tomas scratched the back of his neck, embarrassed by the attention.
"It seems the serum I took works well with me.
Right, it wasn’t just Alpha Gene Enhancement... it was Prime Gene Enhancement.
Maybe that’s the reason.
I guess I was compatible."
That explanation only fueled the envy further.
Several survivors exchanged glances, already considering whether they should request Prime Gene Enhancement Serums instead of the standard Alpha ones.
If Tomas could get new skills, then perhaps they could too.
Soon, the group left the tent together to make their report.
Outside Kai’s tent, they were surprised to see Sera waiting...
She still looked beautiful as ever.
"Are you here to report your progress?" She asked.
"Yes!"
"Let me hear about them instead." Sera said softly.
None of them rejected the idea, and soon, she received their report, even congratulating all eight of them for their progress.
Her words made them blush...
There was pride mixed with embarrassment before they left quietly afterward.
Inside, Kai opened his tent flap and asked what had happened...
At this time, Sera noticed some changes in Kai’s pupil and recalled something...
"Have you reached Level 40?"

chapters.title: Chapter 311: The Cube and the Mutants
paragraphs: "Not yet... just Level 39," Kai replied. He had consumed his remaining Gene Enhancement Serums to forcefully raise his level.
This was only possible because his Bio‐Adaptive Constitution had now reached Level 9, allowing him to absorb more serum without suffering backlash.

Normally, consuming Gene Enhancement Serum had strict limits. There was always a small chance of mutation since the gene was being forcefully upgraded. However, thanks to his advanced constitution, the backlash was no longer a concern.
The only limitation was how many vials his body could handle.
Previously, Kai had to wait thirty days before consuming another dose. As his constitution improved, that waiting period shortened... first to twenty days, then fifteen, and eventually just one day.
Now, with his Level 9 constitution, he could safely consume up to ten vials of a single type of Gene Enhancement Serum.
Because of this, he had used all his remaining stock of Prime Gene Enhancement Serum.
Unlike the other variants, Prime Enhancement focused on strengthening the physique, with only a small chance of unlocking new Gene Skills.
Yet by consuming so many at once, Kai had gotten lucky... he obtained a few new skills.
"No wonder your eyes look like they’re glowing. You’ve just completed your enhancement," Sera commented as she studied his face.
She also noticed how Kai’s features seemed better, and his presence seemed more intimidating despite not doing anything.
The enhancements had not only elevated his abilities but had subtly refined his appearance as well.
Soon, Kai learned about the advancements of the others.
Amer’s Silent Dash and Tomas’s stealth‐oriented skills were impressive, and together they could do something greater.
"Right... That’s possible."
At this time, Kai realized he could confidently build a proper scout or assassin team.
Mei, with her talent Living Camouflage, was the natural choice to lead.
She had already proven herself capable of blending into environments and moving unseen, and now she would have a squad worthy of her skill.

Russel and Augustine, the two original scouts, had long been the backbone of reconnaissance. Their Gene Skills were already specialized for survival and infiltration, and with Amer and Tomas joining them, Mei’s team would finally have depth and versatility.
Kai knew that he could trust them with their skills. Perhaps, they just need to level up a few more times.

With the supplies they had stockpiled, Advanced Camouflage Gear, thermal detection goggles, portable disruptor field units, flashbang grenades, decoy emitter devices, and sensor‐disrupting smoke grenades, the team would be more than just scouts.
They could function as assassins, saboteurs, or infiltration specialists.
Still, Kai knew defense had to remain the priority.
He turned the discussion toward the possible threat of the Digger Units.
These units could literally destroy a shelter.

Furthermore, according to the World Chat, these machines had destroyed countless shelters by tunneling beneath defenses. They had already experienced them once, so it wouldn’t be surprising if they attacked once more.
To counter them, Kai had purchased miniature pulse bombs designed to disrupt underground machinery.
Thankfully, the other survivors had also invested their reputation points wisely, and together they had acquired over a hundred of the devices.
Installation had already begun.
The bombs were buried in layers across the outskirts of the shelter, forming a deadly minefield beneath the soil.

If the Diggers tried to breach their shelter, they would be shredded before surfacing. And if any managed to push through, Kai had ensured that disruptor field units were stationed inside the shelter itself.
With those, the defenders could scramble the machines’ coordination, making them easier to destroy.
"There’s no issue installing them so far. Several Survivors on our side had good hands. There’s no accident." Sera reported.
"That’s good to hear."
Then, as Kai was considering his next move, Althea arrived.
Kai had been planning to go out and train his new Gene Skills, but her sudden appearance shifted his focus.
This time, Althea wasn’t here to deliver news.
She carried something in her hands... It was a cube with restrained energy.
Kai’s eyes widened. "Wait... is that—"
"Yes," Althea interrupted, her voice steady. "A Gene Weapon."
. Kai reached out instinctively, but stopped short.
Gene Weapons were rare, powerful artifacts that bonded directly with the user’s genes.
They weren’t just tools... they would become extensions of the body, capable of unlocking devastating abilities.
"Where did you find it?" Kai asked.
Althea’s answer came without hesitation. "It wasn’t found in the ruins or scavenged from traders. It was in our deepwell. The cube got caught when we were retrieving water."
Kai blinked in surprise.
A Gene Weapon surfacing from something as mundane as a water source was unusual.
Althea continued, "It was Emiru who discovered it. Vera’s assistant. She said the cube gave off a strange resonance while she was drawing water."
Kai recalled Emiru clearly.
She has that passive Gene Skill, Herbal Sense. She was only Level 5 back in Bluegrass Shelter, more of an apprentice alchemist than a fighter.
Her skill was useful for identifying herbs and toxins, but she wasn’t someone who could wield a Gene Weapon effectively.
Kai knew immediately that it would be better in the hands of a fighter. Still, Emiru had contributed something invaluable.
"She deserves a reward," Kai said firmly. He turned to Sera. "Guide her into the vault tomorrow. She can take any three items she wants."
Sera raised an eyebrow. "Three? That’s generous."

Kai nodded. "I wanted to give more, but there are Skill Fusion Crystals and small vials of Gene Enhancement Serum stored there. She might use all the chances for the vials. Those are too critical to hand out freely."
"Haha... Got it." Sera chuckled as she imagined that it could happen.
With that settled, Kai appraised the cube himself. The panel confirmed his suspicion... it was only low‐grade. His interest waned immediately.
For someone at his level, it wasn’t worth binding.

"As for who should have it..." Kai looked at Althea and Sera. "What do you think? Should we store it and trade it later for something more precious? Or give it to someone who could benefit now, so they can become useful against the A.I. Army?"
The three of them weighed the options carefully...
But before they could reach a conclusion, a shout echoed from outside.
"We’re surrounded! Around sixty mutants on sight!"

chapters.title: Chapter 312: The Mutants and the New Weapons
paragraphs: Wilfred, commander of the Superhuman Guild, marched at the head of his squad as he carried the Signal Jammer in his hand.
This Jammer allowed them to move undetected by even C-Grade units of the A.I. Army.

Unlike ordinary survivors, the guild he belonged to had gained access to rare Special Gene Enhancement Serums... concoctions that didn’t just strengthen the body, but warped it into something monstrous.
Their mutations were varied...
Some bore four arms, able to wield multiple weapons at once.
Others had four eyes, glowing faintly in the dark, granting them incredible perception.
A few had mouths in their palms, able to bite or consume directly during combat.
One even had a massive jaw that could swallow a human whole.
Still, there were other mutations like having double knee joints or double elbows, twisting their limbs unnaturally.
Right, there were even those with spines protruding like spiky armor, or tails tipped with bone blades.
None of them cared about their appearance anymore.
In this apocalypse, survival outweighed vanity. And survival was exactly what these mutations offered.

One of the greatest benefits was their altered physiology... their satiety was extraordinary. They only needed to eat once a week, freeing them from the constant hunger that plagued ordinary survivors.
But tonight, survival wasn’t their only goal.
Wilfred had come for vengeance.
"Wait for me, brother... I’ll avenge your death."
Apparently, Aaron, one of their recruiters, had been killed while attempting to bring new members into the guild.
Whether the shelter ahead was responsible or not didn’t matter. The Superhuman Guild needed blood to ease its rage, and this survivor base was the perfect target.
Wilfred raised his hand, his four‐eyed lieutenant then stepped closer...
"We’ll raid the place. If they resist, we’ll tear it apart. If they surrender, we’ll take their supplies. Either way, Aaron’s death will be answered."
"Yes, Sir!"
The mutants behind him looked so excited. Soon, flexed their warped bodies, eager for violence.
Soon, the dark outline of a shelter came into view. Torches or perhaps emergency lights could be seen faintly along its perimeter, and Wilfred’s lips curled into a cruel smile.
"Perfect," he muttered. "They won’t even know what hit them."
None of them realized yet that the shelter they were about to assault was Codebreakers Shelter...
As soon as Wilfred’s squad advanced, the mutants brought out their weapons.
About thirty of them carried revolvers, their crude but reliable firearms...
Others hefted plasma rifles, the rare weapons were even humming with stored energy. The rest had to rely on javelins for long‐range attacks, and swords and shields for close combat.

They moved quickly, their twisted bodies shifting unnaturally as they closed the distance. The shelter’s defenders had already noticed them... several moved along the walls, and the faint glint of scopes revealed that snipers were in position.
"Release the Bomber Drones!"

Wilfred’s men released a swarm of drones, each carrying small explosive charges meant to obliterate the gates. The buzzing machines darted forward, but before they could reach their target, sharp sound echoed across the night.
One by one, the drones were shot down mid‐air, their payloads detonating harmlessly outside the perimeter.
"Snipers," Wilfred frowned while his four‐eyed lieutenant confirmed with a nod.
The mutants didn’t stop however...
A group carrying tower shields surged forward, their limbs bracing behind the heavy slabs of reinforced steel.
With their defensive gear and mutation‐enhanced resilience, they pressed on, determined to reach the shelter’s walls.
Behind them, the revolver‐wielders fired sporadic shots to suppress the defenders, while the plasma rifle carriers prepared to unleash devastating bursts once they had a clear line of sight.
Thud! Thud! Thud!
The clash was inevitable. The Codebreakers Shelter had spotted them early, but Wilfred’s force was quick!
With shields raised and weapons ready, the mutants advanced step by step!
However, the defenders of Codebreakers Shelter had prepared for this moment.
Snap!
The first trap triggered... a line of concealed wooden barricades swung down from hidden hinges, slamming into the advancing shield‐bearers.
Thud! Thud! Thud!
The impact staggered several mutants, forcing them to break formation.
Crunch!
Moments later, a series of spike pits opened beneath their feet.
"Aack!"
"Shit! It’s filled with traps!"
"Careful, everyone!"
Covered with thin planks and dirt, the traps gave way under the weight of the charging mutants. Screams erupted as bodies fell onto sharpened stakes, impaling those unlucky enough to be caught.

Wilfred roared as the four‐eyed lieutenant giving orders to regroup. But the defenders weren’t finished. From the walls, survivors triggered another mechanism... rolling log traps, even massive beams, were released from hidden ramps. They thundered down the slope, smashing into the mutants’ front line and scattering them like ragdolls.
Then came the most devastating blow... oil‐fire trenches ignited along the perimeter. Flames roared to life, cutting off the direct path to the gates.
"Aack!"
"It hurts!"
The mutants were forced to slow their advance, their shields barely holding against the sudden inferno.
"Push forward!" Wilfred roared as the attack stopped..
His voice carried over the chaos. His men obeyed, but their momentum was broken. The traps had done their work... the assault line was fractured, their numbers thinned, and their confidence shaken.

And just as they tried to regroup, the defenders unleashed their countermeasure. Bombardment began. Mortar‐like launchers hidden within the shelter fired volleys of explosive shells, raining down on the mutants.
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Each detonation tore through their ranks, sending shockwaves across the battlefield!
The night lit up with fire and gunfire, the clash between the Superhuman Guild and Codebreakers Shelter fully underway!
Back inside the shelter, Kai stood on the observation platform, watching the mortar crews at work.
Two survivors operated each launcher, and they were all quite slow because they were new weapons from the Auction Realm, but it didn’t matter.
One of them was in charge of loading shells. The next one was focusing on adjusting the angle and firing it...
The thunderous blasts shook the ground, and each explosion outside lit up the night as mutants were thrown into disarray...
Box after box of ammunition was consumed.
However, against sixty mutants who were Level 20 at most, it was all necessary!
’We don’t know what kind of Gene Skills they possess... Better to end them while they’re still at a distance.’

chapters.title: Chapter 313: The Superhuman Guild’s Base
paragraphs: Back inside the shelter, Kai’s eyes swept across the battlefield...

The mortars had done their work, but Codebreakers Shelter wasn’t relying on artillery alone. They had fighters... They were survivors who had experienced numerous battles at this point, each with Gene Skills that made them stand out.
Alfie, the Gladiator, was already preparing to move out, his combat style built for melee clashes, so he would be supported by several more Survivors.

There was Ralph, with his Sharpshooter Talent, who had taken position on the upper walls. At this time, he was the one making the most killing thanks to his Ruger Mini Rifle purchased from the Auction House. His precise shots were cutting down mutants who dared to expose themselves.
Sera and Althea, each wielding low‐grade Gene Weapons, stood ready to reinforce the lines behind Alfie...
Aside from them, Wallace, clad in full body armor from the Auction House, was a walking fortress, his layered Gene Skills making him nearly impervious to small arms fire.
And beyond the human fighters, Codebreakers Shelter had its machines.
A dozen X‐Series Sentinels patrolled the perimeter, with their mechanical bodies equipped with many weapons.
Renji’s two androids also coordinated really well, covering blind spots and coordinating with the defenders.
Finally, there was Kai’s trump card... the S‐Grade Sentinel, Black Atom.
The machine stayed at the center of the shelter just in case Digger Units could somehow pass through their defenses and destroy their inside...

For now, Kai had deliberately kept it inactive. Black Atom’s energy consumption was immense, and its destructive potential was meant for battles against S‐Grade Machines, A‐Grade machines, or high‐level survivors above Level 50.
To unleash it now against Wilfred’s force would be wasteful.
Kai couldn’t waste Black Atom’s energy reserve and would only move it when absolutely necessary.
"Do not worry about the bullets! Just use them all of needed! No need to fight in close quarters unless we’re forced to!"
Indeed, unlike many other shelters that these mutants attacked before, they were not worried about the ammunition consumption at all.
With Kai’s Infinite Gift Pack Talent, he was able to produce all the ammunition except for the mortars.
"Yes, Sir!"
"We’ll not let them set foot in our shelter!"
"Defend our home!"
Just like that, the battle raged on.
The mutants did their best to defend using various Gene Skills, hoping that the bombardment and the firing of rifles would stop after a few minutes...
However, it wasn’t happening at all!
"What is going on?!"
"How are they not running out of ammo!"
"They should be stopping soon! Don’t give up!"
But as they tried to advance, the traps, mortars, and defenders tore through their ranks. Twenty of them fell, their grotesque bodies burning in the trenches or shattered by shrapnel.
The survivors tried to regroup, but when they reached the gates, they were met with something unexpected... a force field barrier.
"What?!"
"This..."
Bullets, plasma bursts, even javelins bounced harmlessly off the wall of energy. The mutants roared in frustration, hammering against it with weapons and claws, but nothing broke through.
Wilfred’s four‐eyed lieutenant shouted, "Commander, we can’t breach it!"
Wilfred frowned as he was also unsure if they could break it. He had expected resistance, but not this. The shelter was protected by technology far beyond what his guild had seen.
"Retreat!" he shouted. "Fall back!"
The order rippled through the ranks.
Soon, the mutants disengaged, dragging wounded comrades as they fled into the night.
But retreat was costly. Mortar shells continued to fall, snipers picked off stragglers, and the Sentinels advanced to cut down those who lingered.
By the time the chaos settled, only thirty mutants escaped safely. Half of them had been eliminated!
Kai watched them scatter across the dark fields.
His expression hardened. "They dared to attack us at night. If we let them go, they’ll return with more. We can’t allow that."
He turned to his officers. "We kill them all."
Alfie slammed his gauntlet against his chest. "Then let me lead the charge."
Ralph adjusted his rifle. "I’ll join the chase."
Sera and Althea exchanged a glance as they considered it as well. "We’ll cut off their escape routes. I think they’re headed to the valley."
Wallace’s armored body moved. He wasn’t really able to fight. He wanted the Mutants to reach the walls, but unfortunately, they were too weak to do so.
"I already used a Gene Stimulant. I thought we’d have a huge fight. I want to chase them. I have the Movement Gene Skill with me! I’ll hold the front line."

Kai nodded. "The X‐Series Sentinels will stay to defend the shelter... Renji, stay here with your androids. Mei, take your scouts and check the surroundings. There could be others lurking in the shadows."
Kai then paused for a moment as he looked at Alfie, Ralph, Wallace, Sera, and Althea...
"All of you, let’s use the Dragoons."
"Ahh! That’s right!"
Sera’s eyes lit up, recalling the Dragoons... the modified flying vessels that resembled oversized jet skis.
They were once used by the A.I. Army, but they had been converted into machines humans could pilot.
Each Dragoon carried one driver and one passenger, making them perfect for rapid pursuit.
"Yes! We still have those in the warehouse!" Alfie exclaimed.
Kai nodded. "I stored some of them in my System Inventory. Let’s go!"
Moments later, three Dragoons were activated... Their thrusters ignited as they lifted off.
Six fighters mounted the machines... Kai himself, Alfie, Ralph, Sera, Althea, and Wallace were soaring into the night sky to chase down the retreating mutants.
The pursuit was fast...
The Dragoons skimmed above the treetops, firing their rifles...
At first, the attacks seemed sloppy, deliberately slow, as if missing their targets. But it was a calculated tactic... The mutants were being herded, funneled into open ground.
Sure enough, one by one, they fell. Eight more were eliminated before the survivors realized the trap.
Then Kai’s eyes widened.
Ahead, deep in the forest, was the Superhuman Guild’s base.
"We’re close to their base now! Be careful!"
As he said this, everyone noticed the dozens of tree houses connected by rope bridges!
"This is their base?!" Ralph was shocked as he steered the Dragoon.
Suddenly, gunfire and plasma bolts were fired from the tree houses.
The Guild had defenses ready, forcing the Dragoons to climb higher, retreat, or weave evasively through the barrage!
"Retreat!" Kai ordered as he knew that the six of them couldn’t deal with the whole Superhuman Guild!

chapters.title: Chapter 314: Grim
paragraphs: Kai was already satisfied with the result of their chase.
Now that he was aware of their base, this was a fair battle.
After all, it wouldn’t be fair if only one side was aware of their shelter. His Codebreakers Shelter might be exposed to these mutants, but it was now the same for the Superhuman Guild.
In the meantime, Grim, the Guild Leader, sat in the largest tree house of the Superhuman Guild’s base, a structure built with steel beams scavenged from ruined factories.
Unlike his subordinates, his appearance was deceptively normal.

Long black hair, tanned skin, with a physique that was tall, broad‐shouldered, and refined... It was a body sculpted by countless enhancements yet free of the grotesque mutations that plagued the others.
Indeed, where his guild members bore extra limbs, twisted joints, additional eyes, or monstrous features, Grim’s form had stabilized.

His mutation was like theirs at first, but after a certain condition was fulfilled, it had reversed, reshaping him into something closer to humanity. Still, his vision, speed, and other skills remained...

Furthermore, if he wanted to regain those third and fourth arm he had before, it was quite possible to do so. Unfortunately, the problem would be the fact that it would take quite a lot of them to remove them once again.
In any case, he wore a long white robe, loose and flowing, with nothing underneath.
The garment was symbolic... a reminder that he had transcended the deformities of the serums, that he alone had achieved balance.
His bare chest rose and fell as he listened to the report delivered by his lieutenant.
"Commander Wilfred’s squad failed," the four‐eyed mutant said. "Aaron’s death has been a problem. We lost nearly half of our elite forces. The strange shelter... it is stronger than we imagined."

Grim clenched his fist. His knuckles whitened. "So. The ones who eliminated Aaron are not ordinary survivors. They have barriers, modified Sentinels, modified Dragoons, and seemingly unlimited ammunition. This is a problem... We should’ve approached them differently."
Grim was having a headache.

Unfortunately, aside from physical mutations, these people under him would have a berserk tendency where they would seek excitement through combat. Of course, this does not happen a lot, but when those cases occur, it could be problematic.
He rose from his seat, pacing across the wooden floor.

Lantern light flickered against his robe as he looked outside. "We made a mistake. Recruiting or raiding them shouldn’t be an option. We underestimated them. If we want to raid other shelters for resources, we must increase our levels even further. Otherwise, we will bleed ourselves dry."
Grim sighed, his gaze turned to a few guards near his residence, the forest canopy swayed in the night wind, rope bridges creaking as guild members moved between tree houses.
Their base was vast, but it was fragile.
The problems weighed heavily on him.
First, they have issues with food.

Even with their mutations granting extraordinary satiety... only needing to eat once a week, the guild still struggled. Hunting parties brought back carcasses from the forest, but the supply was inconsistent.
Farming wasn’t an idea in this forest, and scavenging from ruins was dangerous.
They had previously raided a military base where they found many canned goods, but that action resulted in the deaths of many...
Hunger was not constant, but when it struck, it was brutal.
Then, there was also the Digger Units.
The A.I. Army’s subterranean machines were a constant threat.
Grim knew that if the Diggers tunneled beneath their base, the tree houses would collapse. They had tried to install traps and pulse bombs, but their resources were limited.
Every attack forced them to expend precious ammunition and manpower.
"I think this isn’t possible anymore." Grim muttered as he considered how to save these people.
He looked at his own sword as he recalled that they also had problems with weapons.
Their arsenal was crude.
Revolvers, scavenged rifles, and a handful of plasma weapons.
Most of their firepower came from sheer numbers and mutations, not advanced technology. Against ordinary shelters, this was enough. Against Codebreakers Shelter, it was laughable.
Then, there was also concerns about their levels...
None of them were even in the Top 500 Survivors!
The guild’s progress was sluggish. Mutations granted resilience and strength, but they did not guarantee rapid growth.
Many members were stuck at Level 20, unable to break through.
The serums warped their bodies but did not always elevate their combat potential.
Grim himself had reached far higher, but his guild lagged behind.
’Haaa... Why did I even choose this Apocalypse? I should’ve gone with Zombie Apocalypse, that sounds easier. I watched Grimes and Dixon a lot, and I could probably survive there.’
Grim shook his head as he couldn’t turn back time now.
With a sigh, he looked at his shelf...
It contained a total of 12 black cubes.
Needless to say, they were the Gene Weapons.
Gene Cubes and Gene Weapons.
This was also their greatest frustration. For reasons they could not explain, the guild members were rejected by these cubes.
When they tried to fuse or awaken with Gene Weapons, the results were disastrous. The weapons bonded poorly, their power limited, their functions crippled.
Only Grim was different. His physique, refined and stabilized, allowed him to wield Gene Weapons without restriction.
He was the only one compatible. His subordinates could barely use them, if at all.
Grim’s hand tightened around the railing as he looked down at his guild.
Mutants moved below, their grotesque forms illuminated by torchlight.
He believed that this was the right path... As long as they managed to get passed this transformation, they’d be really strong just like him.
Unfortunately, he was also unaware of the condition he fulfilled in order to reclaim his physique.

Grim sighed once more as he watched four‐armed warriors carrying crates. Spined hulks patrolled the perimeter, and some mouth‐palmed mutants gnawed on dried meat. They were loyal, but they were flawed.
He muttered... "We must find ways to overcome our limitations."
The lieutenant bowed his head. "What do you command, Guild Leader?"

Grim turned, his robe flowing behind him. "You all stay here and defend our shelter. No more reckless raids. We will focus on leveling, on training, on stabilizing our mutations. We will hunt those A.I. units that dared to enter the forest, gather resources, and prepare. When the time comes, we will strike again... but not until we are ready."
He paused... "And we will find a way to unlock Gene Weapons for the others. I will not be the only one..."
The lieutenant hesitated. "But the cubes reject us. The weapons were wasted on us."
Grim silenced him with a raised hand. "We will find a way. Even if it means creating our own."
The chamber fell silent.
Outside, the guild continued its nightly routines.
Patrols moved across rope bridges. Watchers scanned the forest.
The Superhuman Guild operated like a colony... Each member looked ugly but they were united.

They had rules. Food was rationed. Patrols rotated every six hours. Mutants with enhanced perception guarded the perimeter. Those with extra limbs carried supplies. Those with armored spines formed the vanguard. Every mutation had a role given by Grim...
Grim had made his decision.
The Superhuman Guild would remain in their forest stronghold, but he himself would act.

He gathered the twelve black cubes... the Gene Weapons that his subordinates could not wield, and stored them carefully in his bag. If there was a way forward, it would be through negotiation, not reckless raids.
At dawn, Grim departed alone.
’They’re not going to attack us yet, right?’He mused, hoping that the shelter hadn’t assembled a team to raid them yet.
Soon, his hoverboard floated a foot above the ground, gliding silently through the forest.
The mist clung to the trees as he approached the shelter he had offended the night before.
It didn’t take him that long, thanks to the hoverboard, allowing him to travel great distances without much of a sweat.
When the walls of Codebreakers Shelter came into view, Grim raised his hand high, signaling he came in peace.
"I represent the Superhuman Guild," he called out, his voice carrying across the perimeter. "I come alone, without hostility."
From the battlements, gunners shifted...
Modified Sentinels patrolled the perimeter, as they quickly scanned him.
Even the watchtowers had some rifles sticking out aimed at him, and Grim could feel more hidden snipers aiming directly at him.
Still, he did not flinch.
Soon, Kai himself appeared.
His gaze was calm and after a moment’s consideration, he gestured for the gates to open. Grim stepped forward, storing his hoverboard into his inventory before entering.
The sight inside stunned him.
"This..."
Though the shelter was still rebuilding, with field tents scattered across the grounds, it was thriving.
Survivors were nicely dressed, food supplies were abundant, and there was no aura of desperation around them... It felt just like any other community.
Then Grim’s eyes locked onto a towering figure near a tent.
A black sentinel stood guard...
His breath caught.
’Shit... Is that an A‐Grade... No, an S‐Grade unit?!’
Grim felt genuine shock. The Codebreakers Shelter was far stronger than he had imagined.

chapters.title: Chapter 315: The Negotiation and the Requirements
paragraphs: Inside Codebreakers Shelter, Grim was escorted through the camp until he reached Kai’s tent. The place was still filled with many field tents, with survivors rebuilding steadily...
Everyone seemed busy as they worked together in order to make this place better.
Still, Grim was unsure how they planned to hide from the A.I. Army. After all, unlike their base, they had the trees or the canopy protecting them from drones or surveilling the area.
At this point, he had no idea about the disruptors allowing them to jam the drones scanning their area.
Nonetheless, as soon as he entered one of the field tents, he saw two beautiful women standing beside the leader like escorts. Their presence was definitely a show of his authority...
Still, the fact that he could have beautiful women made him a little jealous.
"Kai... He’s the leader of those mutants we chased away..." One of the guards escorting him said.
"Right... They really swept so many of our traps. That’s a lot of resources, Kai. We can’t just let him off."
"Hey... Just let Kai decide about his matter."
Another guard said as they gestured for Grim to enter.
Still, as soon as Grim heard their conversation, he was shocked.
’Kai... Kai... Right... Is this guy the Rank 1 Survivor?’Grim repeated in his mind as he heard the others address him with such a name!
It was at this point that he realized that they were dealing with the first-ever Guild that was established, the Codebreakers Guild!
Grim bowed slightly, then placed his bag on the table.
With deliberate care, he revealed the twelve black cubes... "These Gene Weapons... I come in peace," he said firmly. "These are yours. All of them. Let this be the foundation of our truce."
Kai studied the cubes, his expression unreadable.
He didn’t expect to receive this offering for peace...
"Impressive," he admitted, "but not enough."
Grim’s brows furrowed. "Not enough? These are Gene Weapons... They are precious resources. We could’ve traded it for plenty of food..."
Kai smiled as he realized that they had a food problem. Well, it was quite normal for others who don’t have Talents or Skills that could help with food production.
"Ahem... I want more. Maybe the serums you use... the ones that transform your people into mutants. Give me those."
Grim stiffened, shocked by this request.
"You don’t understand. Those serums are limited and dangerous. They warp the body, strip away humanity if you consume too much. If you misuse them, you’ll destroy yourselves."
Kai’s gaze remained steady. He had already decided this.
"We’ll take that risk. If you want peace, you’ll provide them..."
Silence hung for some time... Grim exhaled slowly, then nodded.
"Fine. I will provide them. But know this... once they’re gone, they’re gone. Even we can’t replenish them."
He had to make Kai aware that they couldn’t produce more of these serums. Well, Grim thought that Kai might request additional serums, so it was better to make it clear this early.
Kai’s tone softened slightly, shifting the negotiation... "Then one more thing..."
"Another?" Grim repeated.

"Of course... But this time, I’ll make it worthwhile. You see... the forest where your base stands, its wood is sturdy, stronger than anything we’ve found so far. If you provide timber, I’ll trade food in return. Your people won’t starve."
Grim considered this carefully.
Food was their greatest weakness. The offer was tempting, even if it meant exposing their resources.
Furthermore, there were hundreds of hectares in that forest, providing timber shouldn’t be a huge problem.
Finally, he agreed. "Wood for food. Serums for our peace... and the Gene Weapons as a gesture of trust. Is that how it is?"
Kai was satisfied with this interpretation from Grim. "Then we have an understanding."
Grim nodded, suddenly realized something... It seemed that this wasn’t just a peace negotiation... it was the beginning of a dangerous alliance, one that could reshape both shelters.
After the negotiations were finalized, Kai and Grim discussed the practical details and shook hands.

The timber would be transported in batches, carried by the Superhuman Guild’s mutated laborers, while Codebreakers Shelter would provide food in exchange. To avoid misunderstandings, Kai insisted that all communication be done through their radios, establishing a secure channel between the two shelters.
With the matter settled, Kai leaned back in his chair.
"You’ve done well to come here alone. If you wish, you can stay in the shelter tonight. Rest, eat, and see how we live."
Grim shook his head, his long robe shifting as he stood.
"I appreciate the offer, but I cannot. My people need food quickly, and the timber trade must begin at once. I’ll return when the first shipment is ready."
Kai studied him for a moment, then gestured to one of his guards.
Soon, a box of canned goods was brought forward... It was heavy, packed with enough supplies to sustain Grim’s guild for several days.
"Take this with you. Consider it a gesture of goodwill."
"This... No... This is an advance payment. We’ll immediately get to work." Grim then accepted the box without hesitation.
His physique was extraordinary, refined by countless enhancements, and he lifted the weight as if it were nothing.
With a nod of respect, he turned and left the tent, storing the box securely before stepping back onto his hoverboard.
As he glided away into the misty forest, Kai watched from the shelter gates.
The alliance had begun, but he knew it was fragile.
Grim’s guild was desperate, and the trade of timber and serums would bind them together... for now.
Yet Kai’s mind was already racing ahead, calculating how this partnership could be used, and how long it would last before one side decided to test the other.
Soon, Kai stood at the edge of the shelter walls, watching as Codebreakers Shelter grew stronger...
Survivors worked tirelessly, erecting sturdier defenses, reinforcing the perimeter, and even laying out escape routes in case the A.I. Army or rival guilds ever breached their lines.
Kai himself oversaw the arrangement of these escape paths, ensuring that every member, every fighter, and every machine had a fallback plan.
It was meticulous work, but he knew survival depended on preparation.
That night, after the long day of planning and directing, Kai returned to his tent.
The camp outside buzzed with activity, but inside, silence greeted him.
He sat down, exhaled, and opened the glowing interface of the System.
"Let’s see..."
Notifications appeared before his eyes...
He had reached the full experience points required for Level 39, yet the System had halted his progress.
No serums or A.I. machine elimination could push him to the next level.
Well, the barrier to Level 40 wasn’t just to obtain more experience points.
Apparently, there was a requirement to break through it, and it wasn’t easy.
[ Current Level: 39 (Max Experience Reached) ]
[ Breakthrough Requirement: To advance beyond Level 39, the Survivor must complete a special quest. ]
[ Quest: Forge Your Legacy ]
Requirement 1: Strengthen your foundation further. Possess at least 8 Gene Skills upgraded to Level 7. (Progress: 5/8)
Requirement 2: Possess at least 5 Fused Gene Skills created through Skill Fusion. (Progress: 4/5)
Requirement 3: Consume a Soul Enhancement Serum to unlock higher compatibility with advanced systems. (Progress: 0/1)
[ Reward: Evolutionary Ascension ]
Unlock Veteran Physique Evolution: advanced stat growth, resilience against environmental hazards, and compatibility with higher‐tier Gene Skills and Zodiac Enhancement.
Title upgrade: Expert SurvivortoVeteran of Humanity.
[ Warning: Survivor will remain capped at Level 39 until all requirements are fulfilled. Prolonged stagnation will not affect future advancement. ]
Kai’s eyes narrowed as he read the list.
It was far harsher than the breakthrough at Level 30, where he had only needed 5 Gene Skills at Level 5, 10 B‐Grade Energy Cores, and 3 Gene Weapons bound.
Now, the System’s demands had escalated: mastery of Level 7 skills, A‐Grade cores, more Gene Weapons, fused skills, and even the consumption of an unknown Soul Enhancement Serum.
He leaned back, exhaling slowly.
He clenched his fists.

The requirements weren’t just about strength... they were about transformation. Fused skills meant refining his arsenal into something greater, while the Soul Enhancement Serum hinted at a dangerous evolution of body and spirit.
Kai closed the interface, his resolve hardening. "Level 40... I’ll reach it. Even if I have to tear the world apart to find what I need."
Soon, planned to finish one of the requirements by using the Skill Fusion Crystals in his possession...
It shouldn’t be a problem to attempt several fusions to push his arsenal closer to the breakthrough requirements.
His thoughts raced through combinations... Solid Balance with Meditation or maybe Blood Regeneration and Bio-Adaptive Constitution.
Perhaps, Fast Appraisal and Meditation would even give him a better result.
Still, before committing, he opened the Guild Chat as he recalled something...
As expected, a new message blinked from Farrah, stationed in Cameron City to protect their shop.
[ Farrah: You have to return quickly... Our resources are being depleted. We got some huge clients. ]
Kai’s eyes widened as he knew that he had left resources to last for a couple of months there.
There must be something big going on.
With this in mind, he immediately replied.
[ Kai: I’m coming... ]

Army.

He’s the leader of those mutants we chased away..." One of the guards escorting him said.

They really swept so many of our traps.

We can’t just let him off."

Another guard said as they gestured for Grim to enter.

’Kai...
Kai...
Right...
Is this guy the Rank 1 Survivor?’Grim repeated in his mind as he heard the others address him with such a name!

"These Gene Weapons...
I come in peace," he said firmly.
"These are yours.
All of them.

chapters.title: Chapter 316: Kai’s Shop
paragraphs: Cameron City.
The morning sun filtered through the patched awning of Kai’s Shop...
It was casting warm light across the rows of neatly arranged goods.
Farrah stood behind the counter with her long hair tied back. She had been busy over the past few days, but she wasn’t complaining.
They were earning a lot of cores after all.
’I wonder if there will be more customers...’
At this time, she surveyed the shelves. She had taken charge of the store while Kai was away, and though she was a warrior at heart, she found herself surprisingly adept at managing trade.
Despite having a Spirit Knight Talent, her others skills back on Earth was still helping her.
Beside her, the two blue‐haired siblings, Xian and Xinyi, were busy cleaning.
Xian was quite quick as she moved between shelves with a rag in hand, dusting off jars of mayonnaise and polishing the glass cases that held flashlights and batteries.
His sister Xinyi, her mechanical arm gleaming faintly in the light, carefully stacked survival clothing sets and folded sleeping bags with precision.
Though her physique was still frail, she worked diligently, determined to prove her worth.
The shop had become something of a marvel in Cameron City.

Unlike the scavenged goods most stalls offered, Kai’s Shop displayed items that looked brand new... mountain bikes with shining frames, vacuum‐sealed rations, pristine water bottles, board games with intact pieces, even musical instruments that seemed untouched by the apocalypse. Customers often whispered in awe, wondering how such treasures were obtained.
Farrah adjusted the placement of a signal jammer on the counter just as the first customer of the day arrived.
A grey-haired man with a scar across his cheek stepped forward, as he scanned the shelves.
"I need more emergency two‐way radios," he said bluntly. "The last set I bought here worked better than anything else in the market. Do you have more?"
Farrah offered a professional smile.
"You’re in luck. We just restocked yesterday."
It was obviously a lie since she was simply managing the number of items being sold, so they wouldn’t get emptied immediately.
This way, no one would purchase all their supplies and sell them for a higher price. It was basically a way to protect their store that they would be using for a long time.
She then gestured to Xian, who hurried to fetch a box from the back.
Within moments, the boy returned, lugging a crate of radios... Despite his current level, his face flushed with effort but nonetheless, he looked proud.
The man inspected one, tested the knobs, and nodded...
He looked satisfied after looking at one. "Perfect. I’ll take the whole crate."
Farrah’s brow lifted slightly. "The whole crate? That’s twenty units."
"Exactly. My team needs them. We’re expanding patrols." He dropped a pouch of C‐Grade Energy Cores onto the counter with a clink.
Then, he didn’t stop then and gave three more pouches.
Farrah counted quickly and smiled. They still had a couple more crates of that, so it should be just fine.
"Deal."
As the man left with his purchase, Farrah thought it would be a normal day... a few customers, steady sales, nothing unusual. But she was wrong.
Within the hour, more and more people began arriving. A pair of scavengers came in, marveling at the mountain bikes.
"These look brand new! How much?"
Farrah quoted a price, and they paid without hesitation, walking out with two gleaming bikes.
Next came a family, their children tugging at their sleeves.
They bought board games and musical instruments, desperate for something to distract from the bleakness of survival.
Xinyi smiled faintly as she handed them a guitar, her mechanical arm was also noticed as she lifted it with ease.
Then came a group of what seemed like mercenaries, their armor was dented and worn. They purchased vacuum‐sealed rations, water gallons, and survival clothing sets.
"Your goods are cleaner than anything we’ve seen," one remarked. "Feels like we’re shopping before the world ended."
Farrah kept her composure, but inside she was astonished.
The shop was being swarmed.
Every shelf was touched, every item was inspected.
’Hmm? Did we get some kind of promotion? Why are they all coming to this shop?’
She couldn’t help but worry for a bit... After all, there were still several factions here that might try to stir some trouble.
It would certainly be good to be popular, but there was a limit to that.
This was especially true for the
Xian darted back and forth, restocking as quickly as he could, while Xinyi managed the folding and organization with quiet determination.
By midday, the counter was piled with Energy Cores.
Farrah sorted them carefully... Hundreds of C‐Grade cores, and a few dozens of rare B‐Grade cores could be seen.
She stacked them in a locked case, her mind already calculating how much Kai would appreciate the haul.
Still, the flow of customers didn’t stop.
A hunter bought flashlights and batteries, mentioning night patrols. A medic purchased bandages and water bottles, praising their quality.

Another person from the Aries Faction was also there and acquired as many signal jammers and wristwatches as he could obtain. Furthermore, they were all paying generously... No one ever tried to negotiate for some reason.
’We already priced it a bit higher than we thought since we’re sure that they’ll negotiate the prices. This is weird. What is happening?’
Still, Farrah found herself enjoying her precious time as she saw the piles of Energy Cores piling up.
She would then give quick instructions to Xian and Xinyi as they got used to work.
"Bring more rations from the back!"
"Stack those clothing sets neatly, they’re selling fast!"
The siblings responded eagerly, their faces glowing with pride at being part of something important.
Well, they’d get paid for this after all. The Gene Enhancement Serum they consumed and Xinyi’s Mechanical Arm replacement weren’t free after all
At one point, Xian paused, wiping sweat from his brow.
"Sister Farrah... we’ve never seen so many people. Is this normal?"
Farrah chuckled softly. She was also quite curious what was going on, but she didn’t want them to worry unnecessarily.
"Not normal. This is what happens when you sell quality. People can’t resist."
Xinyi chuckled as her mechanical arm flexed before she lifted a heavy box..
"It feels good... to help. To be useful."
Farrah glanced at her, warmth in her eyes. Xinyi was previously unable to stand up due to pain coming from her necrotic arm...
Thankfully, y she could now move freely after it was replaced.
"Hey... You’re more than useful, Xinyi. You’re part of this guild now. Both of you."
The afternoon wore on, and the shop became a hub of activity.
It seemed that word had spread quickly... Kai’s Shop was the place to find reliable, pristine goods.
Customers lined up outside, waiting their turn. Farrah managed them calmly, ensuring no one pushed or fought.
By evening, the shelves were half‐empty, the stock depleted faster than she had anticipated. Farrah finally relaxed and leaned against the counter... She was exhausted but delighted.
"Haa~ That’s a really long day..."
She then looked at the locked case filled with Energy Cores.
The glow of C‐Grade cores was abundant, and nestled among them were several precious B‐Grade cores. It was more than she had expected.
Farrah allowed herself a small smile. "Kai will be pleased. We’ve done well today."
Unfortunately, as soon as she said this, her Spirit Sense Skill allowed her to notice the presence of some people outside the store.
"Hide... You two." Farrah immediately said to the two helpers.
"W-why--" Xian asked as he was confused. But his sister cut her off.
"Sshhh... Just follow her instructions."
They had no idea but a group of high‐level Survivors approached Kai’s Shop.
Farrah’s Spirit Sense wouldn’t mistake their aura... It was oppressive, and unmistakably dangerous.
Furthermore, their clothing confirmed it... they were from the Cancer Faction.
Through the window, her eyes locked onto one figure in particular.
Cornelio had warned her about him before.
Elder Hao.
His presence was different, and his reputation was infamous.
He was a Level 80 Survivor at the very least.
The five men behind him carried themselves with confidence, their levels likely between 40 and 50.
Together, they radiated a killer aura that made the shop’s humble defenders, Farrah at Level 35, and the two children at Level 9, seem absurdly outmatched.
The door suddenly burst open, not by hand but through force... It was telekinesis or perhaps a wind skill.
The hinges rattled as the group stepped inside.
Elder Hao’s gaze swept the shelves before settling on Farrah.
"Hmmm... This is the shop selling those Signal Jammers," he said coldly. "You’re aware that our faction is the only one allowed to produce them, right?"
Farrah frowned. This wasn’t something mentioned by Cornelio.
"I didn’t know."
Elder Hao’s lips curled into a sneer.
He raised his hand, fingers stretching toward her throat, intent on crushing her spirit along with her body.
But before he could touch her, a sudden wave of Spirit Energy surged through the shop, pressing against him like a wall.
Whom~
The surroundings vibrated, halting his movement...
Farrah’s eyes widened as she recognized the figure who had helped her...
"Sir Hale..."

Together, they radiated a killer aura that made the shop’s humble defenders, Farrah at Level 35, and the two children at Level 9, seem absurdly outmatched.
The door suddenly burst open, not by hand but through force...
It was telekinesis or perhaps a wind skill.
The hinges rattled as the group stepped inside.
Elder Hao’s gaze swept the shelves before settling on Farrah.
"Hmmm...
This is the shop selling those Signal Jammers," he said coldly.
"You’re aware that our faction is the only one allowed to produce them, right?"
Farrah frowned.
This wasn’t something mentioned by Cornelio.
"I didn’t know."
Elder Hao’s lips curled into a sneer.
He raised his hand, fingers stretching toward her throat, intent on crushing her spirit along with her body.
But before he could touch her, a sudden wave of Spirit Energy surged through the shop, pressing against him like a wall.
Whom~
The surroundings vibrated, halting his movement...
Farrah’s eyes widened as she recognized the figure who had helped her...
"Sir Hale..."

chapters.title: Chapter 317: Hale Libra and the Factions
paragraphs: A few moments earlier, Hale Libra had just returned from a mission outside Cameron City.
For the past several days, he had been roaming the wastelands, striking down A.I. Army units and dismantling their patrols.

His reputation as a soldier was well‐earned... unlike many high‐level Survivors who preferred the safety of faction bases, Hale was constantly on the move, fighting, scouting, and protecting human settlements.
Upon his return, he learned that Kai had already visited Cameron City and even established ties with the Aries Faction.
’That kid had grown really well...’
He couldn’t help but recall Kai’s situation in the past, being a lone Level 30 Survivor in a shelter was definitely not easy.
In any case, he was happy that Kai allied with the Aries Faction, one of the decent factions of the city.
This allowed Kai to open a small shop, one that was quickly becoming famous for its pristine goods.
Curious, Hale had visited Kai’s Shop more than once, meeting Farrah and noting her sharp management skills.

He also noticed the two blue‐haired children, Xian and Xinyi, who were clearly talented despite their low levels. Hale respected their determination and silently admired how Kai’s group was nurturing them.
On this particular evening, Hale had planned to purchase a few more Gene Stimulant Injectors from the shop.
But as he approached, his Spirit Sense caught the oppressive aura of another Level 80 Survivor.
"Mhmm?"
He recognized it immediately... Elder Hao of the Cancer Faction.
Elder Hao was infamous for his arrogance, a man who spent most of his time inside the faction base indulging in the virtual gamePerfect Worldrather than fighting the A.I. Army.
Through his spot, Hale saw Elder Hao raise his hand toward Farrah, intent on crushing her throat.
That was enough. Hale stepped in, his Spirit Energy surging through the shop like a storm, halting Hao’s movement...

"They are not breaking any laws here," Hale said firmly. "Your faction may produce Signal Jammers, but that doesn’t mean you’re the only ones allowed to sell them. If I’m not mistaken, these jammers were discovered in abandoned military facilities, not manufactured here."
It was a lie, of course, but Farrah quickly supported him. "If you think we’re making Signal Jammers, no, we are not. We have no technicians capable of that."
Elder Hao frowned upon hearing this.
He wanted to make a scene, to assert dominance and hopefully close down this shop that was creating trouble for many shops owned by their faction... but Hale’s killing intent was suffocating.
The difference between them was clear... both were Level 80, but Hale was battle‐hardened, an active soldier who fought the A.I. Army daily.
Hao, by contrast, was complacent, his strength dulled by inactivity.
Finally, Elder Hao relented.
With a sneer, he lowered his hand and turned away. "Hmph. Very well. But remember, we’re watching you..."
He left with his five subordinates with their killer aura slowly fading as they exited the shop.
The tension eased, and Farrah exhaled shakily.
Haa~
Hale stepped closer, as he could understand Farrah’s situation.
"You need to be more careful. This shop is drawing attention, and not all of it is good. Hire guards, strengthen your defenses. You can’t rely on luck when factions like Cancer are involved."
Farrah nodded, grateful. "Thank you, Sir Hale. I’ll make sure we’re prepared."
Hale glanced at the shelves, then at the two children peeking nervously from the back.
He gave them a reassuring nod.
"You’re doing well here. Don’t let anyone intimidate you..."
Hale lingered for a moment longer after Elder Hao departed, his gaze softening as he looked at Farrah and the two children.
From his satchel, he pulled out a few items he had scavenged during his recent mission outside the city.
"For you three," he said simply.
He handed Xian a small mechanical toy... It was a wind‐up soldier that marched stiffly across the counter once activated.
Clack... Clack... Clack...
The boy’s eyes lit up, and he immediately began winding it, laughing as it clattered forward.
"This is amazing!"
For Xinyi, Hale produced another toy, a delicate bird with wings that flapped when its gears turned.
"It’s beautiful! Thank you, Uncle Hale!"
She cradled it carefully in her mechanical arm, her smile shy but genuine.
Finally, Hale turned to Farrah.
From his palm, he revealed a silver brooch shaped like a crescent moon.
"A souvenir," he said, fastening it gently onto the edge of her cloak.
His tone carried a subtle warmth, it was a silent admiration that he didn’t voice aloud.
Farrah blinked, touched but uncertain about his gesture...
Still, she thanked him politely, though her mind was already elsewhere.
As much as she appreciated Hale’s gesture, her thoughts were consumed by the Cancer Faction. Their threat was real, and the Aries Faction’s support could only go so far.

"Right... I’ve informed the Libra Faction about your shop and how you can supply us with those Stimulants and Decoy Emitters. A representative will visit this shop in a few days, and you can try to get a better deal with him... not just Energy Cores, but maybe you can get something more."
"Thanks for informing me..."
When Hale left, the shop felt quieter, but Farrah’s unease remained.
She knew she had to act quickly.
Sitting behind the counter, she opened the Guild Chat and typed a message to Kai.
[ Farrah: You have to return quickly... Our resources are being depleted. We got some huge clients... and Cancer Faction involved themselves. ]
[ Farrah: You need to come to Cameron City. The Cancer Faction is watching us. I need your help with decisions. ]
She could certainly hire some guards to protect them temporarily... It was not a long-term solution to deal with the Cancel Faction.
Still, Farrah believed that Kai might have better options to deal with this problem.
Thankfully, Kai seemed to be aware of how serious this matter was.
[ Kai: I’m coming... ]
[ Kai: Right... It will take me a couple of days to get there, even with the Dragoon. In the meantime, try to find information about the Soul Enhancement Serum. ]
