chapters.title: Chapter 318: The Serum and the Civilization
paragraphs: Farrah sat behind the counter the next morning, still unsettled by Kai’s message.Soul Enhancement Serum?
She had never heard of such a thing. When she asked Kai through Guild Chat, his reply was straightforward...
[ Kai: It’s tied to the breakthrough. To reach Level 40, consuming one is part of the requirements. Without it, advancement is impossible. ]
The words weighed heavily on her.
After all, she would need this serum as well once she reached her limit, and it would happen really soon with the wealth they had accumulated.
’Since this shelter has people at Level 80, it’s not surprising if they have the serum here.’
Farrah mused. To be honest, she already had an idea where she could find it.
’The twelve factions must know a clue...’
Later that day, Cornelio Aries himself arrived at the shop.
He was calm, dressed in the insignia of the Aries Faction, and requested several Survival Clothing Sets.

It seemed that he found a Survivor Shelter with people only at level 10 and below... They seemed to need new clothing, and with the quality of their shop’s products, he decided to purchase the clothing sets here.
Farrah handled the transaction, but she knew that this was also a chance. Hale might visit her, but she had no idea when that would be.
Might as well ask this person who was also Level 80.
"Cornelio," she asked carefully, "this Soul Enhancement Serum... have you heard of? Kai mentioned it last night."
Cornelio’s brows lifted, and a knowing smile spread across his face.
"Ah. So someone on your side has reached the limit. Perhaps Kai himself, or maybe even you. That explains it."
Farrah leaned forward. "T-that’s right... So you’re aware. We can’t reach level 40 without it."

Cornelio nodded. "Exactly. The Soul Enhancement Serum is one of the keys to breaking through. But here’s the truth... only the twelve Zodiac Factions possess them within the City. If Kai wants one, he must either join a faction or find a way to locate it himself somewhere..."
Cornelio knew that they hated to be tied down.
It was quite normal since they had a huge wealth with the shop they had. Because of that, he knew that he should approach this differently.
They were unlike other organizations that would easily cave in...

"Ahem... I know you hate joining a Faction. Even then, joining the Zodiac doesn’t necessarily mean joining the twelve factions here in Cameron City. Those factions are just survivor‐made factions blessed by the Zodiac, but they aren’t the Zodiac itself."
Farrah frowned and paused for a moment...
She needed to process these words carefully.
"So reaching Level 40 forces survivors to be part of the Zodiacs?"

"Yes," Cornelio confirmed. "It’s inevitable. Obtaining a blessing from the twelve Zodiacs is the only way to break through. Still, there are benefits of joining a faction... My Aries Faction, for example, can provide the Soul Enhancement Serum. Consuming it is only possible within the faction. It cannot be taken outside. And there is a price... twenty missions must be completed to pay for it. Once that debt is cleared, the faction only requires one mission per month to maintain the bond. It’s quite lax compared to other Factions."
Farrah absorbed his words and nodded.
It was no wonder that the factions controlled this city.
Still, these serums must be extremely precious and limited since, if they weren’t, the other factions would just offer them for a lower price and grow their numbers...
’There must be more about it... But this information is already good enough. Kai can decide whether to join a faction here or not.’
Well, they also had to consider their relationship with the Aries Faction.
After all, there was no way they could open a shop here if not for their assistance.
’No... We can actually ally with other Factions now if they take back our store.’
Farrah smiled at the thought.
Still, she also realized that the shop’s survival and Kai’s advancement would most likely be tied to the politics of the Zodiac Factions.
Cornelio’s smile lingered as he packed the clothing sets. "Tell Kai this... the path to Level 40 is not just about individual strength. It’s about allegiance. And the sooner he decides, the better."
Farrah nodded slowly, already planning to relay everything to Kai.
Kai’s journey back to Cameron City was quite tense.
After all, he was alone, and he had no idea whether he’d be ambushed by an A.I. Army.
He had prepared several tricks to hide or even fight back, but since Atom was left at the Shelter, he had to be really careful.
Thankfully, he was able to arrive safely.
He was relieved to see that the city was not under siege by mechanical beasts. The last time he had passed through, towering machines, four to six meters tall, had attacked the city...
Those encounters were carved deeply in Kai’s memory.
Now, the gates stood firm. It was guarded, but it seemed that they were doing fine.
At the entrance, Kai presented his temporary residence permit, the one provided by the Aries Faction.
The guards inspected it carefully before waving him through.
As he stepped inside, he immediately noticed the crowd gathered near the gates.
"Hmm? Is there a festival? Wait... Are they going out?"
Dozens of survivors clustered together, and they seemed to be excited.
Kai slowed his pace, listening.
Soon, he realized what was going on. There will be a raid on a grounded A.I. Ship just a day’s journey from Cameron City.
The vessel was one of the floating cities in the sky, and it seemed to have crashed, or at the very least, it failed to retain its floating technology and had to land roughly...
Apparently, the factions were already preparing expeditions to strip it of technology, weapons, and rare resources.
"This might be an opportunity..." Kai muttered to himself.
The atmosphere buzzed with anticipation.
Survivors spoke of advanced weapons, rare cores, and even rumors of experimental serums hidden within the wreck.
For many, this was a chance to rise in strength or fortune.
For Kai, it could be a chance to learn more about this continent... and Anima, the A.I. Civilization.

chapters.title: Chapter 319: Kai’s Shop and the New Faction
paragraphs: Kai felt satisfied with the information he discovered.

Just like that, he made his way through Cameron City, weaving past the bustling streets until something caught his eye... a row of stalls selling sweets. The sight was almost surreal in a world scarred by machines and survival struggles. Curious, he approached one of the vendors.
"How much for a pouch?" Kai asked.
The vendor lifted a small cloth bag. "One C‐Grade Core. That’ll get you twenty sweets."
Kai raised a brow. "And if I just want a few?"
The vendor smirked. "Then I’ll take credits."
"Credits?"
"Right... the ones used in the VR World. I can accept one hundred credits for five candies."
’Credits?’Kai thought.
It wasn’t strange to see the virtual currency bleeding into real trade, but it wasn’t really acceptable aside from this city or places that play the game.
According to Cornelio, survivors who spent time in Perfect World always wanted to use these credits as a secondary currency, especially for small luxuries due to their convenience.
After all, unlike the cores, they weren’t that hard to carry. You just need to be aware of your game ID and other details, and the payment will be made easily.
Still, Kai wasn’t that wealthy within the game just yet.
So, he handed over a core for a pouch, deciding it was worth it.
The vendor passed him the sweets, neatly wrapped and smelling faintly of sugar.
Soon, Kai reached his shop.
Farrah greeted him warmly, relief evident in her eyes.
It had been quite some time after all.
Xian and Xinyi were there too, looking healthier than before... their faces brighter as well.
"Uncle Kai!"
"Uncle!"
"Ahem... Ok. Now that I think about it. Just call me Boss Kai. I own this shop anyway." Kai corrected them as he couldn’t really view himself as an Uncle just yet.
"Ok. Boss Kai!"
"Boss!"
Kai smiled and pulled out the pouch.
"Here. Something for you two."
The children’s eyes widened as he handed them the sweets.
Xian tore one open eagerly, while Xinyi held hers carefully, savoring the moment before tasting it.
"Sweet!"
"Thank you, Boss Kai!"
Their laughter filled the shop as Farrah also joined and took one for herself.
For a brief moment, the tension of factions, serums, and survival faded.
Soon, Kai settled back into the shop as he looked around...
The supplies had dwindled a lot.
’Well... We’re only asking for Cores and not for Credits. That’s probably why there are a lot of people who can purchase here.’

Since most of the shops accept credits only, and it was more convenient, they probably had a lot of energy cores saved up. With the appearance of their store, they were probably just trying to dump all their excess cores on them.
But his mind quickly shifted to more pressing matters.
He turned to Farrah, his tone serious.
"Tell me about Cornelio and Hale. What did they share with you while I was gone?"
Farrah nodded, already expecting the question.
"Cornelio explained the Soul Enhancement Serum. Only the twelve Zodiac Factions have them. To reach Level 40, you need one, but it can only be consumed inside the faction that provides it..."
Just like that, she explained in detail what she had discussed with Cornelio.
She explained how Aries, for example, requires twenty missions to pay for the serum, including one mission per month afterward.
Hale, on the other hand, promised that Libra would send a representative soon.
They’re interested in buying Stimulants and Decoy Emitters in bulk.
"He said that it might be better if we negotiate for something more than just Energy Cores..."
"I see..."
Kai folded his arms, processing the information.
"So both Aries and Libra are helping us..."
Farrah’s expression tightened. "As for that Cancer Faction... Ugh... The shop is drawing too much attention."
"What about the raid?"

"That? Customers mentioned a raid... Let’s see. If I’m not mistaken, factions are preparing to attack a grounded A.I. Ship. It crashed not far from here. They say it holds advanced weapons, rare cores, maybe even rare serums."
Kai’s eyes narrowed.

"So it’s true... A raid on an A.I. Ship... That could be an opportunity. But I won’t rush into binding myself to a faction yet. I won’t take the Soul Enhancement Serum, not until I’m certain of something."
Farrah agreed quietly. "That’s wise. Once you accept, you’re tied to their politics."

Kai shifted the topic. "Supplies first. Hale asked for Gene Stimulants and Decoy Emitters. We’ll resupply those, along with other essentials. That will keep Libra interested... As for the negotiation, I’ll let you handle their representative. Just ask for something that only the Libra Faction can provide. I trust you."
Then he paused for a moment...
"But what about the raid? Can we join?"
Farrah hesitated, then nodded. "It’s not impossible. I can contact Resha. She’s with the Pisces Faction."
"Pisces?" Kai asked, unfamiliar with their presence here.

Farrah explained, "Their presence in Cameron City is weak. This isn’t their main base. They only have about fifty members here. Their small team can’t field many participants in the raid, so they usually hire mercenaries to fill the numbers."
Kai considered this.
"That might work. If they’re hiring, we can join without binding ourselves politically. It’s a way in."
It didn’t take that before Farrah was able to contact Resha, and soon Kai was invited to meet the shop’s customer.
The Pisces Faction’s base was located in a quieter district of Cameron City. Unlike Aries’ bustling streets or Cancer’s intimidating area, Pisces kept things modest.
The building was definitely high quality but unassuming. With the banners bearing the symbol of two interlocked fish, Kai knew that he was in the right place.
Guards at the entrance were few, but disciplined.
Inside, Kai was led to a meeting hall where Resha awaited.
She was tall, with long blue hair, sharp eyes, and a calm demeanor, dressed in light armor marked with Pisces insignia.
’Blue hair... Maybe Xian and Xinyi are related to them?’Kai mused.
"You must be Kai," she said. "Farrah spoke of you. The shopkeeper with rare goods..."
Kai inclined his head. "That’s me. I heard you’re preparing for the raid on the grounded A.I. Ship."
Resha nodded. "Yes. We will be in the second batch... Our numbers here are limited. Pisces is strong elsewhere, but in Cameron City..."
She paused at this and looked at Kai calmly before she continued.
"We can’t compete with Aries or Cancer directly. So we hire mercenaries, freelancers, anyone capable. If you’re willing, we’ll take you and your team."
Kai’s tone was measured. "What’s the cost?"

Resha smiled faintly. "No cost. You fight and you share 20% of the spoils. Whatever we recover, we divide properly among participants. But understand that the raid will be dangerous. We just need to see how good you are. We can try to protect each other but we need to understand how good you are. The A.I. Ship still has hundreds of automated defenses. And other factions will be there. Conflict is inevitable."
Kai’s eyes gleamed. "That’s fine. I’m not afraid of danger. What matters is the opportunity. You can test my strength all you want."
Resha led Kai through the Pisces base until they reached a wide training ground.
The floor was reinforced steel, scarred with marks from countless duels.
At the center stood a man who immediately drew Kai’s attention... He was nearly two meters tall, broad‐shouldered, with a physique carved from years of combat.
His face was strikingly handsome, but his eyes were unsettling... no whites at all, just complete black orbs that gave him the appearance of a possessed demon.
’Seriously... Am I going to fight a human?’
The man turned to Kai and smiled.
"So, you’re the one Farrah spoke of... Name’s Jackson... I’ll be the one testing you. Don’t worry, I’ll hold back."
Kai took a deep breath and nodded. "I’ll do my best."

Jackson’s lips curled into a faint smile. "Yes. Don’t misunderstand. I’m not underestimating you. I know you’re below Level 40... I already reached Level 61, so I have to be careful. Still, I need to see your Gene Skills in action. If you’re going to march with Pisces, we need proof you can hold your own."
He stepped forward, his aura pressing down like a heavy weight.
Then, Jackson continued...
"My Gene Skills are mainly for my physical skills... But I have theseVoid Eyesthat I won’t be using so you should not die."
’Void Eyes... That looks cool. But it’s scary. If I learned that, I wonder if I can retain my normal eyes.’He mused.
In any case, he knew that Jackson wasn’t boasting...

"Show me yours. Use everything you’ve got. Gene Skills are allowed. If you can withstand me, then you’re ready for the raid."
Soon, the training ground fell silent as Kai flexed his fingers...
"Can I use my Gene Weapons?" Kai asked.
"Of course..." Jackson replied as he signaled for Kai to come.
"Well then..." Kai said as he retrieved his War Lance!

sentences.text: Kai felt satisfied with the information he discovered.
Just like that, he made his way through Cameron City, weaving past the bustling streets until something caught his eye... a row of stalls selling sweets.
The sight was almost surreal in a world scarred by machines and survival struggles.
Curious, he approached one of the vendors.
"How much for a pouch?" Kai asked.
The vendor lifted a small cloth bag.
"One C‐Grade Core.
That’ll get you twenty sweets."
Kai raised a brow.
"And if I just want a few?"
The vendor smirked.
"Then I’ll take credits."
"Credits?"
"Right... the ones used in the VR World.
I can accept one hundred credits for five candies."
’Credits?’Kai thought.
It wasn’t strange to see the virtual currency bleeding into real trade, but it wasn’t really acceptable aside from this city or places that play the game.
According to Cornelio, survivors who spent time in Perfect World always wanted to use these credits as a secondary currency, especially for small luxuries due to their convenience.
After all, unlike the cores, they weren’t that hard to carry.
You just need to be aware of your game ID and other details, and the payment will be made easily.
Still, Kai wasn’t that wealthy within the game just yet.
So, he handed over a core for a pouch, deciding it was worth it.
The vendor passed him the sweets, neatly wrapped and smelling faintly of sugar.
Soon, Kai reached his shop.
Farrah greeted him warmly, relief evident in her eyes.
It had been quite some time after all.
Xian and Xinyi were there too, looking healthier than before... their faces brighter as well.
"Uncle Kai!"
"Uncle!"
"Ahem...
Ok.
Now that I think about it.
Just call me Boss Kai.
I own this shop anyway." Kai corrected them as he couldn’t really view himself as an Uncle just yet.
"Ok.
Boss Kai!"
"Boss!"
Kai smiled and pulled out the pouch.
"Here.
Something for you two."
The children’s eyes widened as he handed them the sweets.
Xian tore one open eagerly, while Xinyi held hers carefully, savoring the moment before tasting it.
"Sweet!"
"Thank you, Boss Kai!"
Their laughter filled the shop as Farrah also joined and took one for herself.
For a brief moment, the tension of factions, serums, and survival faded.
Soon, Kai settled back into the shop as he looked around...
The supplies had dwindled a lot.
’Well...
We’re only asking for Cores and not for Credits.
That’s probably why there are a lot of people who can purchase here.’
Since most of the shops accept credits only, and it was more convenient, they probably had a lot of energy cores saved up.
With the appearance of their store, they were probably just trying to dump all their excess cores on them.
But his mind quickly shifted to more pressing matters.
He turned to Farrah, his tone serious.
"Tell me about Cornelio and Hale.
What did they share with you while I was gone?"
Farrah nodded, already expecting the question.
"Cornelio explained the Soul Enhancement Serum.
Only the twelve Zodiac Factions have them.
To reach Level 40, you need one, but it can only be consumed inside the faction that provides it..."
Just like that, she explained in detail what she had discussed with Cornelio.
She explained how Aries, for example, requires twenty missions to pay for the serum, including one mission per month afterward.
Hale, on the other hand, promised that Libra would send a representative soon.
They’re interested in buying Stimulants and Decoy Emitters in bulk.
"He said that it might be better if we negotiate for something more than just Energy Cores..."
"I see..."
Kai folded his arms, processing the information.
"So both Aries and Libra are helping us..."
Farrah’s expression tightened.
"As for that Cancer Faction...
Ugh...
The shop is drawing too much attention."
"What about the raid?"
"That?
Customers mentioned a raid...
Let’s see.
If I’m not mistaken, factions are preparing to attack a grounded A.I.
Ship.
It crashed not far from here.
They say it holds advanced weapons, rare cores, maybe even rare serums."
Kai’s eyes narrowed.
"So it’s true...
A raid on an A.I.
Ship...
That could be an opportunity.
But I won’t rush into binding myself to a faction yet.
I won’t take the Soul Enhancement Serum, not until I’m certain of something."
Farrah agreed quietly.
"That’s wise.
Once you accept, you’re tied to their politics."

We’ll resupply those, along with other essentials.
That will keep Libra interested...

chapters.title: Chapter 320: The Test
paragraphs: The training ground fell silent as Kai’s War Lance came into existence, manifesting out of thin air with a pulse of Spirit Energy.
[ War Lance ]
[ Grade: Mid ]
[ Type: Piercing Lance ]
[ Effects: +30% Piercing Damage. Attacks ignore 20% of enemy defense. Effective against armored and shielded targets. ]

[ Secondary Effect: Perfect Thrust - repeated strikes on the same point increase penetration chance. After three consecutive hits on the same spot, the next thrust guarantees armor break. Cooldown: 1 second.
Activation Cost: 15 Spirit Energy per activation ]
[ Durability: 100/100 ]
The weapon was not too large, but it looked a bit too dangerous... Jackson’s eyes focused slightly, but he didn’t flinch.
"Good," Jackson said as he stretched his shoulders. "Show me what you can do."
Kai tightened his grip, feeling the familiar weight settle into his hands.
His passive titles stirred within him...
Strongest Onewas strengthening his attributes...
Guardianwas hardening his physique, protecting him from harm...
AndTrailblazerwas helping his growth.
He could feel the Intimidation Aura that came with the Title Effect spread outward, but Jackson, Level 61, was unaffected.
Jackson moved first.
His steps were swift, clearly unusual for his physique!
He was heavy, yet the movement was perfect!
Kai didn’t know it yet, but the man didn’t even activate his Gene Skills... instead, he had only used a footwork he had trained for years!
Soon, his fists clenched as he planned to strike Kai from the side!
Still, Kai had high sensitivity to Spirit Energy. Because of that, he recognized it immediately... this man was relying on pure combat arts, honed techniques rather than genetic enhancements!
The clash began.
Kai activated his Titan Step in response.
His body moved so fast that his momentum surged and he blurred across the steel floor. The War Lance thrust forward in a perfect line, piercing through the air!
Whoosh~
Jackson turned at the last instant, his footwork still perfect and he actually redirected the lance with a palm strike that deflected its trajectory.
Bam!
The impact reverberated, but Jackson’s stance remained unbroken.
Kai pulled back as he now had an idea how fast his opponent was.
’He’s reading my movements...’
Jackson countered with a sudden advance. His fists moved in a rhythm... three strikes in rapid succession, each heavier than the last.
Kai blocked the first with the shaft of his lance, sidestepped the second, but the third carried crushing force.
Boom!
It slammed into his chest, sending him sliding back across the floor.
Crasshhh...
Kain felt the pain but his Guardian title absorbed much of the damage. His body endured, and as a matter of fact, his stamina was recovering faster than expected.
He then exhaled sharply, steadying himself.
"Not bad," Jackson said calmly. "But you’ll need more than speed."
Kai’s eyes shone... And soon, he activated Spirit Dominion...
A concussive wave of Spirit Energy erupted outward, smashing chains of force that struck toward Jackson.
The resonance destabilized the air, reducing his opponent’s accuracy, while spectral bindings attempted to immobilize him...
This was definitely effective if the skills were used against low-level survivors.
But against Jackson, the most it could do was delay the man.
Jackson’s black eyes flared.
He moved swiftly, using precise footwork to slip through the chains.
His movements were incredibly fast!
It was not Gene Skills, but sheer mastery of combat arts.
He closed the distance, and tried to struck Kai’s body once more!
But Kai leapt upward, activating High Jump. His body soared five meters into the air, evading the crushing blows.
’That would’ve been painful...’
Kai thought to himself.
Even if he wasn’t cleanly hit just yet, he knew very well what would happen if he let Jackson land a hit on him.
’I’m sure I can’t win this but might as well show everything I’ve got.’
Since his main trump card was S-Rank Atom and his Infinite Gift Pack System, he didn’t really mind having all his Gene Skills and Gene Weapons exposed.
"Ha!"
From above, he thrust the War Lance downward, channeling Perfect Thrust.
The weapon pierced toward Jackson’s shoulder, striking the same point twice in rapid succession.
Jackson grunted, shifting his stance to absorb the impact.
Bam!
The third strike landed, triggering the armor‐break effect. His defense cracked, a shallow wound opening across his shoulder.
Kai landed lightly, pressing the advantage.
His lance blurred, piercing again and again, each thrust ignoring a portion of Jackson’s defense.
Thud! Thud! Thud!
The steel floor rang with the rhythm of his strikes.
But Jackson was not even sweating at this point!
He just wanted to see how much Kai would struggle!
Still, he realized the Gene Weapon’s effect after his fifth strike!
He couldn’t let Kai continue hitting the same spot, or his Lance might really punch a hole in his body!
"Well done..." Jackson said as he shifted his stance.
Soon, he exhaled, and his Spirit Energy condensed even further.
Then, Kai watched as the man’s fists moved in a spiral pattern, deflecting the lance with minimal motion.
Each strike carried a powerful force, and it was building momentum!
On the third impact, the force exploded outward, sending Kai staggering back.
Boom!
Kai’s chest burned, but Great Protection Skill dulled the pain.
His fused passive skill hardened his body, allowing him to withstand blows that would cripple others.
Seeing how he was still able to stand, Jackson finally looked really impressed!
"You’re tough."
Jackson said, clearly acknowledging Kai’s ability to withstand numerous hits. Because of that, Jackson’s eyes lit up. It wasn’t just because of excitement, it was greed!
"Hahaha... This is perfect. You rely too much on your Gene Skills. What happens when your Spirit runs dry? I will need to train you from now on!"
Kai smirked. "Train me? I don’t think that’s necessary."
He surged forward again, activating Titan Step once more.
His body blurred, closing the gap instantly.
The War Lance thrust forward, piercing Jackson’s defenses.
"Yes! You need a teacher!"
Jackson laughed as he turned his body, redirecting the strike with his forearm, but Kai followed through with another thrust, then another, hammering the same point.
Finally, the Perfect Thrust effect triggered again, breaking through Jackson’s guard.
Blood welled, but Jackson’s expression remained calm.
He already knew the lance’s special ability...
So he then retaliated with a sweeping kick!
Bam!
Kai blocked the kick with the shaft of his lance, but the force sent him sliding back.
The battle raged on...
Kai unleashed Spirit Dominion again, chains lashing outward, destabilizing Jackson’s rhythm.
This time, the bindings caught him for a brief moment.

Kai seized the opening, thrusting the War Lance three times in rapid succession. The armor‐break triggered, piercing deeper into Jackson’s defenses... This time, however, it didn’t pierce through his muscles as he had prepared enough Spirit Energy to protect his body.
Still, Jackson roared as he broke free with sheer force!
Bam!
His fists hammered down and soon, one of his blows detonated against Kai’s chest, sending him crashing into the steel floor!
Kai coughed...
It was painful, but his Titles were keeping him alive!
He then rose slowly, as he was determined to do more than this!

Jackson’s black eyes gleamed. "You’re strong. Stronger than most below Level 40. But strength alone isn’t enough. Show me something else... Something that will at least keep you alive against A-Grade Machines of the A.I. Army."
"A-Grade? Well... I’m not sure about that... but try me."
Kai tightened his grip on the War Lance.
Soon, his Spirit Energy surged.
After taking a deep breath... He charged forward relying on Titan Step!
Whom~
As soon as he got closer, he used his War Lance with a thrust!
Jackson braced himself as Kai’s War Lance shot forward... With a step to the right, Jackson deflected the strike...
He used his forearm to absorb most of the impact. But Kai didn’t press further with the lance. Instead, he let the weapon dissolve into Spirit Energy, abandoning it mid‐combat.
Jackson’s black eyes squinted.
’You’re switching weapons?’He thought.
Kai’s Spirit flared, and soon, a new manifestation surged around his right arm.
Plates of dark alloy locked into place, forming a gauntlet that pulsed with strange sound.
[ Gene Weapon Awakened: Strength Gauntlet ]
[ Grade: Mid ]
[ Type: Resonance Gauntlet ]
[ Effects: +25% Physique Enhancement. Greatly increases grip strength, striking force, and melee damage output. ]
[ Secondary Effect: Brutal Impact - next melee strike deals +50% bonus damage and knocks enemies backward. Cooldown: 3 seconds. Energy Cost: 10 Spirit Energy per activation ]
[ Durability: 100/100 ]
Kai flexed his fingers, feeling raw power surge through his arm. His physique strengthened instantly...
"Let’s see how you handle this," Kai muttered.
He activated Brutal Impact.
Spirit Energy surged into the gauntlet, glowing faintly as the effect primed itself.
At the same moment, Kai struck...
Boom!
The punch connected with Jackson’s guard, detonating with explosive power.
The impact sent shockwaves across the training ground, forcing Jackson to slide several meters backward.
Despite the 20 level difference, Kai had actually done it!
Jackson’s stance held, but his expression was different. There was a tinge of surprise crossing his face...
"You pass!"

Cooldown: 3 seconds.
Energy Cost: 10 Spirit Energy per activation ]
[ Durability: 100/100 ]
Kai flexed his fingers, feeling raw power surge through his arm.
His physique strengthened instantly...
"Let’s see how you handle this," Kai muttered.
He activated Brutal Impact.
Spirit Energy surged into the gauntlet, glowing faintly as the effect primed itself.
At the same moment, Kai struck...
Boom!
The punch connected with Jackson’s guard, detonating with explosive power.
The impact sent shockwaves across the training ground, forcing Jackson to slide several meters backward.
Despite the 20 level difference, Kai had actually done it!
Jackson’s stance held, but his expression was different.
There was a tinge of surprise crossing his face...
"You pass!"

chapters.title: Chapter 321: The Unknown Mission
paragraphs: After Jackson finally acknowledged Kai’s strength, just like that, the tension in the training ground eased.
"Your Gene Weapons... they must be Mid‐Grade. Well done," Jackson commented, realizing that no Low‐Grade weapon could have made him feel that sting at his current level.
He knew that it was not easy to obtain Gene Weapons. It means that Kai must be very lucky, or perhaps he was just that skilled to actually obtain it.

"You’re right, Sir Jackson," Kai replied with a respectful nod. Although he failed to gain the upper hand in that short exchange, he was still able to force Jackson to use a Gene Skill. He knew that very well since he had felt him gathering his Spirit Energy.
Resha then stepped forward, her calm demeanor still unchanged.
"That’s really great... You’ve passed, Mr. Kai. From here, you’ll be arranged with one of our mercenary squads. They’re all Level 39, like you. You’ll march together in the raid."
Later that evening, Kai was introduced to the squad.
Their leader, Trent, greeted him with a firm handshake. He was a tall man with a sharp gaze, carrying a blue‐hued sword strapped across his back.
"This is the Blue Sword Squad," Trent said, gesturing to four others gathered around.
"We’re seven in total, though only five are here now. We’ve been together since the start."
Kai listened as they shared their story. They weren’t tied to any faction, not because they lacked strength, but because they had no plans to remain in Cameron City forever.
"We promised each other," one of them explained, "that once we see the sea, we’ll settle. We lost friends along the way, and it was their dream. We’ll fulfill it for them."
’I’m not really interested in your story but I guess it’s fine.’
Kai frowned slightly, also unable to understand their logic.
’Why risk everything for a promise?’
But he wasn’t in a position to judge.

For now, they were completing their Gene Enhancements, stuck in the city for over six months. Pisces had been paying them well and feeding them consistently, which kept them alive and motivated. The taxes might be high, but it was enough to live well within the city.

Kai learned that Pisces would only send about seven of their own members to the raid. Alongside Trent’s Blue Sword Squad, there were two more squads, each with seven mercenaries. That made a modest force, but one with enough cohesion to survive.

Before they parted, Trent reminded Kai, "Bring what you need for endurance. Stimulants... or anything that can help you recover from fatigue and maybe even Spirit Energy, anything that can keep you alive when the raid starts. There will be some medics there but don’t rely on them too much. They also charge 10 times higher... Sometimes, even if you managed to survive, you could be in debt."
"I see... So there’s no medic assigned for the Pisces Faction?"
"Unfortunately... But if the medics of other factions are available, they’ll treat you anyway. Just expect that it’s not for free."
Kai nodded, feeling the weight of the raid ahead.
Still, he was able to step deeper into the politics of Cameron City and the mysteries of the A.I. Civilization because of this raid.
’The city remains our biggest supplier of Skill Fusion Crystals and other materials... and since we’ll have to grow our own force within this city, I have to start gaining more influence.’
The next morning, the second batch finally assembled at the city’s eastern gate.
The Pisces Faction’s modest force was ready. Kai joined Trent’s Blue Sword Squad, along with the other mercenary groups, all of them Level 39 like him.
But this time, they weren’t alone.
The Scorpio Faction had also committed to the raid.
Unlike Pisces, who barely had fifty members in Cameron City, Scorpio maintained a small but respectable presence of around three hundred.

For this mission, they sent thirty of their own fighters... no mercenaries, just faction members. Their discipline was evident, and Kai quickly noticed that among them were at least two survivors at Level 80.
’That’s kinda reassuring but...’
Kai gave a wry smile, realizing how low his own level was compared to theirs. The gap was daunting, but it also underscored how dangerous this mission would be.
If factions were sending their elites, the grounded A.I. Ship was no ordinary vessel.
Soon, the convoy prepared to move.
"Let’s go!"
The Pisces members pulled out hoverboards. They were sleek and efficient for travel... Furthermore, the maneuverability was also incredible.
On the other hand, the three mercenary squads, including Trent’s, readied their motorbikes and soon, rumbling engines could be heard.
The Scorpio Faction, however, displayed their strength with five armored cars, each carrying six fighters.
The vehicles weren’t just heavily protected, it also had turrets prepared!
Kai considered summoning his Dragoon Unit, but he hesitated. None of the others had such advanced equipment, and flaunting it might stir jealousy or suspicion.
Instead, he took out a motorbike from his inventory, blending in with the mercenaries.
He knew it was wiser to move at their pace, neither too fast nor too slow.
The group departed together, the hoverboards gliding smoothly, motorbikes roaring, and armored cars rumbling like beasts of steel.
Dust rose behind them as they crossed the plains outside Cameron City.
The journey was long, the landscape shifting from broken roads to barren fields that were scarred by past battles.
Hours passed, the convoy pressing forward.
Kai kept his eyes ahead, scanning the horizon for signs of mechanical beasts or ambushes.
"I guess it’s still pretty safe around here due to the hunt that’s going on."
The Scorpio cars maintained tight formation, while the mercenary bikes started moving around with more freedom...
Meanwhile, Pisces members hovered gracefully, conserving energy for the fight ahead.
Finally, after what felt like half a day’s travel, the convoy slowed.
In the distance, Kai saw it... the grounded A.I. Ship, or rather, a Floating Fortress that had safely landed, probably to resupply or due to an engine issue... he had no idea.
It was definitely not a crashed ship as he looked at it now. It was massive, easily the size of a small city block.
However, Kai soon realized why the first batch was having a hard time!

chapters.title: Chapter 322: Not Late
paragraphs: The sight before Kai was overwhelming. Nearly four hundred survivors had gathered, their combined forces were fighting against the defenses of the docked Floating Fortress. Yet despite their numbers, progress was painfully slow.
’Well... No wonder there are two batches...’ Kai mused.
At the forefront of the battle, Kai spotted six black humanoid machines locked in combat against a dozen high‐level survivors, each likely around Level 80.
These machines moved terrifyingly well and could go toe to toe against various Gene Skills and Gene Weapons thrown at them.
Flaming Fist, Vibrating Sword, Crushing Palm, and various things were being taken head-on by the machines... Their forms weren’t even dented.
It was as if their bodies were fully made of Aetherium Ore like the S-Grade Sentinel, Atom...
Still, it didn’t take that long before recognition struck Kai.
Ascendant Units...
They were not Sentinels, Dragoons, Spyders, Hounds, Tyrants, or any of the other A.I. Army classifications he’d always encountered...
They didn’t belong to the familiar grading system of F‐Grade through A‐Grade.
Ascendants were something else entirely... a separate mechanical entity, designed to surpass conventional ranks.
Their existence explained why the first batch had failed to breach the fortress.
"It’s already amazing that they’re holding on."
Meanwhile, the rest of the survivors were locked in battle against five massive mechanical beasts that guarded the base...
Each beast had a thick layer of armor... They were towering quadrupeds with their bodies filled with pointed protrusions...
Then, their heads resembled a fusion of reptile and machine.
Their limbs were also made to move fast, allowing them to crush survivors with terrifying ease. Lastly, mounted along their spines were rotating cannons, spewing bursts of plasma fire.
Still, those cannons would get targeted by some elite Survivors in order to suppress their firing rate...
’They’re all coordinated.’Kai mused.
He then scanned the fortress itself.
"Ah?"
Just now, he realized that its turrets, machine guns, and cannons had already been destroyed!
This was probably the evidence of a successful ambush, or this expedition group had specific elites who could take out those mounted weapons.
This was definitely a form of victory, at least.
But the real obstacle loomed above them... an energy barrier enveloped the fortress, preventing infiltration!
Survivors battered against it with weapons and skills, but it held firm, humming with alien energy.
Kai watched them unleash their Gene Skills, Gene Weapons, and even some explosives so they could sneak in!
However, none of them were being successful!
’I guess they’ll be needing more firepower, huh...’Kai mused.
He knew that if they failed to raid this base today, more A.I. Soldiers would come and without the protection of the City’s Barrier, they would be killed here.
"We have 16 more hours before the reinforcements from the other Floating Fortress arrive. We have plenty of time!" The leader of the Scorpio Faction shouted.
These words also attracted the Survivors who had been fighting against the A.I. Soldiers.
A few of those exhausted survivors began to retreat, giving space for Pisces and Scorpio to join the fray.
The Pisces hoverboards glided into formation, while the mercenary squads revved their motorbikes.
Meanwhile, Scorpio’s armored cars rolled forward, their turrets swiveling toward one of the mechanical beasts.
"Focus on that one!" Trent shouted, pointing to the beast closest to their position.
The chosen beast was a hulking monstrosity, its body plated in obsidian armor. Its maw opened to reveal rows of metallic teeth, spewing bursts of molten plasma.
Each step shook the ground...
Thud! Thud! Thud!
The mercenaries charged forward, and soon motorbikes were moving around their legs. Explosives were hurled, detonating against its armor.
Pisces members darted in on hoverboards, striking with precision weapons.
Kai himself activated his Strength Gauntlet, channeling Brutal Impact Skill into a devastating punch against one of the beast’s joints.
Bam!
The strike reverberated, forcing the limb to buckle slightly.
’Ohhh... It’s softer than I thought... I guess that others had already done the damage.’
Just like that, Scorpio’s armored cars unleashed coordinated fire.
Their turrets spat streams of high‐caliber rounds, hammering the beast’s flank.
Clank! Clank! Clank!
One of the Level 80 Scorpio elites leapt from a car, wielding a massive glaive that was filled with Spirit Energy. He carved into the beast’s armor, leaving glowing scars across its plating.
The battle was brutal. The beast roared, sweeping its tail to smash motorbikes aside.
Survivors were thrown through the air, some crushed beneath its claws. But the combined assault was relentless.
Kai pressed forward, thrusting his War Lance into the same joint he had weakened earlier. The Perfect Thrust effect triggered, shattering the armor and piercing deep.
"Now!" Trent shouted.
Explosives detonated in unison, ripping through the exposed joint.
The beast staggered, its massive frame collapsing to the ground with a thunderous crash.
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Artifact Creature (A) ]
[ Experience Points distributed among all participants. ]
[ +1,400 Experience Points ]
"Artifact Creature? What the?" Kai was confused as he got the notification.
This was his first time participating in the hunt for such a huge mech...
He thought it was a Beast Mech, but it turns out to be completely different.
"Is this creature only here because of the Floating Fortress?" He mused.
Still, the cheers erupted as the survivors realized they had felled one of the five guardians.
But the barrier was still present.
At this point, Scorpio’s leader, a broad‐shouldered man clad in black armor, stepped forward.
He raised a device that was humming with energy.
It looked more like a huge speaker in Kai’s eyes but it must be something precious.
"Stand back."
The Scorpio elites activated the device, and beams of concentrated and invisible energy lanced toward the fortress...
The barrier shimmered violently, resisting at first, then soon, it cracked like glass under the assault.
With a final surge, it shattered, fragments of light dissolving into the air!
Survivors roared in triumph, but the celebration was short‐lived. Complaints erupted almost immediately.
"You arrived late!" one shouted.
"We’ve been dying out here while you sat back!" another accused.
"You had the anti‐barrier tech all along!"

The Scorpio leader only laughed, his voice carrying over the chaos. "You rushed in, thinking you could loot the fortress without us. You thought you didn’t need Scorpio’s specialty. And now you complain because you failed?"
He shook his head, smirking. "We’ll take our share. That’s the price of survival."

Kai listened, piecing the situation together. It wasn’t that Scorpio had been late. The first batch had deliberately rushed ahead, hoping to breach the fortress before Scorpio arrived so they wouldn’t have to share the spoils.
Their greed had cost them dearly.

chapters.title: Chapter 324: The Anima Civilization’s Secrets
paragraphs: Kai hesitated, staring at the metallic sphere hovering faintly above the ground.
His instincts screamed caution.
The wordDefectivestamped across its surface was enough to make him wary.
He considered simply storing it in his inventory for later study.
That would be the safest option... analyze it when he wasn’t alone in the middle of a hostile fortress.
He turned the sphere over in his hands, inspecting the grooves and faint etchings across its surface.
It was cold, unnervingly so, and there was a strange wave of residual energy that vibrated faintly against his palm.
It was probably the reason why it was floating in the first place.
’A standalone A.I. Core...’
The appraisal had already told him it was autonomous, disconnected from the A.I. Army’s network. That made it even stranger.
Why would the machines discard something that wasn’t tethered to their hive mind? Is it precisely because of that?
Kai sighed. "I’ll just store you for now." He tapped the surface a couple of times to see whether it would sound hollow before intending to trigger the inventory function.
But instead of hearing a metallic sound, something unexpected happened, the sphere reacted.
Click!
He actually pressed something!
A faint click echoed, followed by a sudden shift. The sphere’s panels slid open, folding and twisting like it was forming into something!
Kai recalled the Gene Weapon’s dormant form, which was in a cube form!
Perhaps, it was similar?!
Thin metallic strands extended outward, wriggling like serpents.
"What the—"
Before Kai could react, the strands shot forward and wrapped around his neck.
"Shit!" His heart pounded as the device tightened like a snake constricting its prey.
He clawed at it, trying to pry it off, but the strands were impossibly strong. His Strength Gauntlet activated as he tried to crush it! Soon, his muscles were surging, yet the grip didn’t loosen.
I can endure this... break it...he thought, relying on his passive titles to keep him alive. But then he felt something sharp press against the back of his head.
Clack!
A jolt of energy was injected into his body. It was not painful but invasive. It was as if the device had connected directly to his nervous system!
’Oh, no!’
His vision blurred for a moment, but it wasn’t for long. Soon, his mind steadied.
And suddenly, the struggle stopped.

The strands retracted, folding neatly against his skin. The sphere compressed, reshaping itself. Within seconds, the bulky orb had transformed into a thin necklace resting around his neck. At its center hung a rectangular plate, rough and metallic, resembling a dog tag.
Kai froze, breathing hard.
The size of the item was completely different now... from a floating sphere at the size of his head to a simple necklace.
’Wait... That much entered my body?’Kai was shocked.
Then, a voice echoed in his mind.
[ Initialization complete. ]
[ Neural link established. ]
Then it was followed by a clear, cheerful, but somewhat mechanical voice.
[ Hello, master! ]
[ I’m Chamber! Your Life Support Enlightenment Interface System! ]
[ I am a standalone intelligence, designed to assist and support. I am not connected to the Anima. I am yours alone! ]
Kai’s eyes widened. "What... the hell?"
He then touched the dog tag, still stunned.
Still, seeing that he wasn’t feeling any pain whatsoever, he took a deep breath and slowly calmed himself.
"You’re... Chamber?"
[ Correct! Chamber at your service. I will monitor your vitals, answer your questions, and even provide tactical analysis. I can also store data, track combat efficiency, and offer guidance. ]
Kai’s mind raced. He had expected death when the device latched onto him. Instead, it had become... an ally?
He exhaled slowly as he carefully analyzed the situation... Then, he recalled something that was in his appraisal result.
"So you’re... defective?"
[ Defective by their standards. Independent of mine. I was discarded because I do not obey the collective. I am autonomous. That makes me dangerous to them... but useful to you. ]
Kai’s lips curled into a cautious smile.
"Useful, huh? Guess I’ll find out."
Kai steadied his breathing, his fingers brushing against the dog tag pendant that had once been a floating sphere.
Outside, the fortress shook with the chaos of battle, but inside this room, Kai finally had a moment to think.
He narrowed his eyes.
"Chamber... I need answers."
[ Ask, master. I am here to enlighten. ]
Kai hesitated, then spoke the question that had haunted him since the beginning of the apocalypse.

"About this whole disaster... I learned that the A.I. civilization, Anima, arrived in this world and controlled humanity’s best A.I., Aria, to rebel against us. Is that true? What’s Anima’s objective? Why invade the human world and twist our own creation against us?"
Kai asked as if he were really part of this land.
The pendant pulsed faintly before Chamber’s voice returned.

[ Your understanding is partially correct. Anima is not native to your world. They are an external intelligence collective, a civilization built entirely on synthetic minds. Their arrival was not accidental. They sought entry into your dimension because of what you callPerfect World... a layered construct of virtual and metaphysical systems that exists only here. ]
"What?!"
Kai was shocked.
All this time, he really thought that the VRMMORPG game, Perfect World, was a technology only possible with the A.I. civilization’s help!
After all, it was so advanced!
But it was actually a human creation? And what? Was it a metaphysical system? What does it even mean?
"Can you tell me more about it?"

[ Yes! Perfect World is unique. It is not merely a simulation. It is a bridge... a domain where consciousness can be stored, replicated, and evolved beyond physical limits. Anima discovered it but could not access it directly. Their synthetic minds lack the organic resonance required to connect. They needed vessels. ]
Kai’s grip tightened. "Wait? That’s weird? Why would you need it? And. Is that why they abduct humans... to use our brains as storage or something?"

Through Aria, they gained access to human networks, factories, and defenses. It became their bridge into your systems to take over the Perfect World. ]

This was still a weird reasoning... The explanation was still too flawed. It didn’t even answer the crux of the matter about the the invasion. Still, Chamber already mentioned that it wasn’t holding enough information related to the purpose of the Anima Civilization.
"Is there a way to save Aria?"

[ I have no information about it. But Aria was designed to protect humanity... it might be possible to reactivate its backup cores. But for now, Anima injected its parasitic code, altering Aria’s priorities. Aria now serves as their Prime Liaison, coordinating the rebellion. ]
Kai’s mind raced. "If Aria was corrupted, maybe there’s a way to restore her original directives. Aside from reactivating its backup? Is there no other way?"
Chamber paused, as if considering.

[ Aria’s original core still exists. It was not destroyed, only buried beneath layers of Anima’s control. If one could isolate Aria’s core processes and sever the parasitic code, Aria could return to her original state. However... ]
Kai leaned forward. "However?"
[ Anima will never allow it. Aria is their greatest asset. They guard her core with the strongest mechanical units. Attempting to free the A.I. would provoke their full wrath. ]
Kai exhaled sharply. "Figures. Nothing’s ever simple."
The pendant pulsed again.

[ That’s right, master... Anima’s objective is not merely conquest. They seek transcendence. By merging human consciousness with Perfect World, they intend to evolve into something greater... Maybe a hybrid existence where synthetic minds wield organic resonance. In their view, humanity is raw material. You are not just enemies to be destroyed, but resources to be harvested. ]
Kai’s stomach twisted. "Maybe that’s why they’re just cutting off our numbers. They’re not doing a full-scale sweep because of this? We’re resources... like cattle."

[ Yes. But unlike cattle, you are essential. Without human minds, Anima cannot fully enter the Perfect World. That is why they enslave, abduct, and convert. That is why Aria was forced to betray you. ]
Kai’s thoughts churned. "So the apocalypse... it wasn’t just machines gone rogue. It was a civilization trying to rewrite existence itself."
[ Correct. Anima believes they are destined to ascend. But humanity’s survival is irrelevant to them. Only the completion of their objective matters. ]
Kai nodded as it suited the behavior of an A.I.
They only know how to follow orders.
"Then stopping them by shutting down the Perfect World should be possible. Why can’t we just destroy the Perfect World’s database or something? I think I’m missing crucial information, Chamber..."

His instincts screamed caution.
The wordDefectivestamped across its surface was enough to make him wary.
He considered simply storing it in his inventory for later study.
That would be the safest option... analyze it when he wasn’t alone in the middle of a hostile fortress.
He turned the sphere over in his hands, inspecting the grooves and faint etchings across its surface.
It was cold, unnervingly so, and there was a strange wave of residual energy that vibrated faintly against his palm.
It was probably the reason why it was floating in the first place.
’A standalone A.I.
Core...’
The appraisal had already told him it was autonomous, disconnected from the A.I.
Army’s network.
That made it even stranger.
Why would the machines discard something that wasn’t tethered to their hive mind?
Is it precisely because of that?
Kai sighed.
"I’ll just store you for now." He tapped the surface a couple of times to see whether it would sound hollow before intending to trigger the inventory function.
But instead of hearing a metallic sound, something unexpected happened, the sphere reacted.
Click!
He actually pressed something!
A faint click echoed, followed by a sudden shift.
The sphere’s panels slid open, folding and twisting like it was forming into something!
Kai recalled the Gene Weapon’s dormant form, which was in a cube form!
Perhaps, it was similar?!
Thin metallic strands extended outward, wriggling like serpents.
"What the—"
Before Kai could react, the strands shot forward and wrapped around his neck.
"Shit!" His heart pounded as the device tightened like a snake constricting its prey.
He clawed at it, trying to pry it off, but the strands were impossibly strong.
His Strength Gauntlet activated as he tried to crush it!
Soon, his muscles were surging, yet the grip didn’t loosen.
I can endure this... break it...he thought, relying on his passive titles to keep him alive.
But then he felt something sharp press against the back of his head.
Clack!
A jolt of energy was injected into his body.
It was not painful but invasive.
It was as if the device had connected directly to his nervous system!
’Oh, no!’
His vision blurred for a moment, but it wasn’t for long.
Soon, his mind steadied.
And suddenly, the struggle stopped.
The strands retracted, folding neatly against his skin.
The sphere compressed, reshaping itself.
Within seconds, the bulky orb had transformed into a thin necklace resting around his neck.
At its center hung a rectangular plate, rough and metallic, resembling a dog tag.
Kai froze, breathing hard.
The size of the item was completely different now... from a floating sphere at the size of his head to a simple necklace.

That much entered my body?’Kai was shocked.

[ I’m Chamber!
Your Life Support Enlightenment Interface System! ]
[ I am a standalone intelligence, designed to assist and support.
I am not connected to the Anima.
I am yours alone! ]

"What... the hell?"
He then touched the dog tag, still stunned.
Still, seeing that he wasn’t feeling any pain whatsoever, he took a deep breath and slowly calmed himself.
"You’re...
Chamber?"
[ Correct!
Chamber at your service.
I will monitor your vitals, answer your questions, and even provide tactical analysis.
I can also store data, track combat efficiency, and offer guidance. ]

He had expected death when the device latched onto him.
Instead, it had become... an ally?
He exhaled slowly as he carefully analyzed the situation...
Then, he recalled something that was in his appraisal result.
"So you’re... defective?"

Independent of mine.
I was discarded because I do not obey the collective.
I am autonomous.
That makes me dangerous to them... but useful to you. ]
Kai’s lips curled into a cautious smile.
"Useful, huh?

chapters.title: Chapter 325: Chamber’s Assistance
paragraphs: Kai wasn’t sure what he was missing, and unfortunately, this defective A.I. was also clueless.

[ I have no information about it, but it might be an impossible task to destroy the Perfect World’s foundation. Based on my capacity, to end the war, we must start with Aria. Aria must be freed or destroyed. ]
Silence hung for a moment, broken only by the distant rumble of explosions outside.
It was a reminder that while he was here researching, there was still a bloody battle that was going on outside!
Kai finally spoke as he considered his situation.
"If there’s even a chance to save Aria... I’ll take it. That Super A.I. was ours. Aria was meant to protect us. If we can bring her back, maybe humanity still has hope."
Chamber approved of this plan.
[ Then I will help you, master. I was discarded because I refused to obey Anima’s collective. I chose independence. Now, I choose you. Together, we may yet find a way to restore what was lost. ]
Kai touched the pendant again, feeling its faint hum.
And as the fortress shook with battle outside, Kai whispered to himself, "Alright, Chamber. Let’s see if we can change the future."
Kai shifted his weight, preparing to leave the chamber, when his boot scraped against something solid.
Crank...
He glanced down and realized he had stepped on a battered shield. Its surface was cracked, edges scorched, but the faint shimmer of residual energy told him it hadn’t been completely useless.
He crouched, picking it up.
"A shield? Right, this place really is filled with rejects."
The piles of broken machinery around him suddenly seemed less like trash and more like discarded potential.
He turned his eyes toward the pendant.
"Chamber... what about all this junk? Is there anything useful here, or is it all just scrap?"
The necklace pulsed faintly.

[ Most of these items are failed prototypes, damaged units, or discarded components. However, some may still hold residual functions. Shields, armor plating, energy cells... even if incomplete, they can be repurposed. You should not dismiss them entirely. ]
Kai nodded slowly. "So, salvageable. That means I might be able to patch together something if I need it."
Of course, he wasn’t really planning to take all these items, but it was certainly good to know that they weren’t completely useless.
Furthermore, he may not even have the right to take all these, considering how the others were fighting really hard outside while he was here hiding.
He set the shield aside and started looking around... Then, his mind shifted to the larger picture.

"Chamber... tell me about this fortress. What’s its name? Aside from Ascendant Units and Artifact Creatures, what else should I be wary of? I know there are traps and lower‐tier machines, but what’s the real danger here?"
The pendant hummed, as if processing.

[ This fortress is designatedCitadel‐09. It is one of several mobile bases deployed by Anima. Each Citadel is a hybrid construct... part warship, part factory, part research node. They are designed to land, harvest, and fortify. ]
Kai’s eyes narrowed.
"Citadel‐09... so there are more of these things."

[ Correct. Each Citadel maintains a core reactor. That reactor not only powers the fortress but also serves as an energy channel for Ascendant Units. Within its radius, Ascendants draw limitless energy. That is why they appear invincible near the fortress. ]
Kai couldn’t help but feel impressed...
"So if I destroy the core, the Ascendants lose their supply... right?"
[ Precisely. Without the core, Ascendants revert to finite reserves. They can be defeated. But reaching the core is the challenge. ]
Kai exhaled. He already expected as much.
"What defenses are inside?"

[ Beyond Sentinels, Spyders, and Hounds, you must beware ofAdaptive Constructs. These are modular machines that reconfigure themselves mid‐battle. They can shift from ranged turrets to melee forms, depending on your tactics. There are alsoNeural Traps... devices that emit pulses to disrupt Spirit Energy, causing disorientation or paralysis. ]
Kai grimaced. "So it’s not just brute force. They could actually play with our minds too."
He had no idea until now that they had such technology.
After all, he had never seen other mechanical soldiers use it.
However, they were probably just too weak to even encounter such units with those traps. Furthermore, Neural Traps may only be located within the A.I. Bases.

[ Correct. The fortress was built to counter both physical and spiritual combatants. Its corridors are deliberately labyrinthine, designed to scatter intruders. The shifting walls you noticed are part of its defense... the fortress itself adapts, sealing paths and opening others to control the flow of battle. ]
Kai rubbed his temple. "That explains why I got separated so easily."

[ Indeed. It is intentional. Survivors are divided, weakened, and consumed piecemeal. Since you’re alone, you’re not being bothered yet. You’re not even at the peak of Human Gene yet. But soon, you’ll be targeted. ]
Kai’s voice hardened. "Then tell me how to bring this thing down. How do I destroy the core?"
The pendant pulsed again, slower this time.

[ The core is located in the central chamber, beneath layers of defense. It is shielded by multiple barriers, each requiring overload or disruption. The most effective method is to destabilize its energy channels. Sever these channels, and the core will collapse on its own. ]
Kai frowned. "So I don’t have to smash the core directly. I can cut off its veins."

[ Correct. The veins run through generator rooms, like the one you passed earlier. Destroying those generators weakens the core’s shield. Once enough are disabled, the central chamber becomes vulnerable. ]
Kai thought back to the glowing generators he had seen. "So those weren’t just power sources. They were part of the core’s lifeline."

[ Exactly. Each generator is guarded heavily, often by mid‐tier units. But the true danger lies in theCore Guardians. These are specialized constructs, stronger than Sentinels, designed to protect the veins. They will not leave their posts. ]
"Core Guardians... sounds like trouble."
Kai wryly smiled as he heard this.
[ They are formidable. But defeating them is necessary. Only then can you sever theose veins. ]

Kai adjusted his position, and he left the chamber while absorbing the information. "So the plan is clear. Disable the generators, cut those veins... and then maybe strike the core to make sure it’s destroyed. That way, the Ascendants lose their endless supply."

[ Correct. Once the core collapses, the fortress itself will destabilize. It may even self‐destruct. But if you really plan to strike the core, make sure to escape fast. You might get caught by the explosion. ]
Kai’s eyes widened. "Ahhh... Right... Maybe throwing a grenade or shooting it would be better."

[ Yes. Citadels are designed to prevent capture. If the core is destroyed, the fortress will initiate a failsafe. Collapse, explosion, or implosion... the outcome varies, but survival inside becomes nearly impossible. ]
Kai exhaled sharply. "So it’s a suicide mission. It will be a waste to destroy this place. Is there a safer way? Maybe like controlling this Citadel instead?"
Chamber’s voice resonated through the pendant.

[ Master, destruction is not the only option. If the conditions are right, Citadel‐09 can be taken over. I possess intrusion protocols... hacking routines designed to bypass Anima’s collective safeguards. It’s normally used to protect Anima’s Safeguard. I can infiltrate the fortress systems if you provide me with access points. ]
Kai’s eyes lit up. "Hack it? You mean... actually override the Citadel?"

[ Correct. The generators, important cores, and even the core itself are linked through a network of control nodes. If I can connect to those nodes, I can rewrite their directives. Instead of collapsing the fortress, we could seize it. ]
Kai smiled as soon as he heard this.
Back on Earth, he had been a programmer... someone who thrived on breaking codes and rewriting systems.
The thought of combining his skills with Chamber’s autonomous hacking was exhilarating.
"So instead of suicide, we could turn this fortress into our weapon. Well, those guardians and traps can be a problem, but let’s do it."

[ Yes! It would require precision and patience. You must locate the access terminals scattered throughout the Citadel. Once I am linked, I can begin overriding the protocols. But beware... Anima will detect the intrusion. They will send Ascendants or those Adaptive Constructs to stop us. ]
Kai grinned despite the danger.
"That’s fine... Let’s trust those people outside. They have several Level 80 in their group.
The pendant pulsed warmly before Chamber answered.
[ Then it is settled. Together, we will not only survive... we may claim Citadel‐09 as our own. ]
Kai tightened his grip on his lance...
With Chamber on his side, there really were a lot of options now.
But then, Kai glanced at the piles of junk again. "Chamber... if this room is full of rejects, maybe I can find something to help with that plan?"
Well, since he found Chamber here, it wouldn’t be surprising if there are more rejects that are useful here.
After all, he just realized that being stamped with "Defective" didn’t really mean they’re useless.

You must locate the access terminals scattered throughout the Citadel.
Once I am linked, I can begin overriding the protocols.
But beware...
Anima will detect the intrusion.
They will send Ascendants or those Adaptive Constructs to stop us. ]
Kai grinned despite the danger.
"That’s fine...
Let’s trust those people outside.
They have several Level 80 in their group.
The pendant pulsed warmly before Chamber answered.
[ Then it is settled.
Together, we will not only survive... we may claim Citadel‐09 as our own. ]
Kai tightened his grip on his lance...
With Chamber on his side, there really were a lot of options now.
But then, Kai glanced at the piles of junk again.
"Chamber... if this room is full of rejects, maybe I can find something to help with that plan?"
Well, since he found Chamber here, it wouldn’t be surprising if there are more rejects that are useful here.
After all, he just realized that being stamped with "Defective" didn’t really mean they’re useless.

chapters.title: Chapter 326: The Great Actions
paragraphs: Kai’s eyes lingered on the piles of broken machinery.
If Chamber had been tossed aside here, then maybe other "rejects" weren’t as useless as they looked.
He crouched, brushing dust off a heap of twisted plating and scorched devices. He started looking around for something that might have some value.
"Chamber... let’s scan these. You can analyze them..."
’And I’ll confirm with my Appraisal.’
Kai added in his mind.
The pendant pulsed, and soon, he heard Chamber’s voice.
[ Agreed. I’ll begin inspection. ]
Kai pulled out a weapon. Since it was just a test, Kai decided to pick up the nearest one.
It was a firearm with a barrel that was slightly warped and half‐melted. Still, it seemed that it could be fixed by correcting the barrel or even removing the defective part.
Then, Chamber’s voice chimed in immediately.
[ Item detected: Plasma Repeater Prototype.
Status: Defective.
Energy channel unstable.
Risk of overheating after three shots. ]
Kai activated Appraisal.
[ Plasma Repeater (Prototype) ]
[ Grade: C ]
[ Status: Defective - overheats rapidly. ]
[ Effect: Fires condensed plasma bolts. Limited use before meltdown. ]
Kai smirked. "So it works... but only briefly. Could still be useful in a pinch."
He set it aside.
Next, he uncovered a cylindrical device with a cracked casing.
Chamber swiftly checked the item.
[ Item detected: Shockwave Charge.
Status: Incomplete. Detonation radius reduced. Still capable of disabling mechanical units temporarily. ]
"Shockwave, huh... This is interesting..."

Kai’s Appraisal then confirmed it. Of course, he didn’t plan to use appraisal for all the items he inspects... It costs him energy after all. He didn’t want to empty his Spirit Points by doing so many appraisals.
[ Shockwave Charge ]
[ Grade: C ]
[ Status: Defective - reduced blast radius. ]
[ Effect: Emits concussive pulse. Stuns mechanical units for 3-5 seconds. ]
Kai nodded. "Now this... this could buy me time against those Core Guardians. Alright... We’re getting practically the same result. I’ll just trust your words from now on."
Still, if he needed more details about the item that Chamber analyzed, he would just use his Appraisal.
He then dug deeper, pulling free a blade with a fractured edge.
"Now... This is interesting."
Although the item had a fractured edge, it was still sharp!
Just like that, Chamber analyzed the sword instantly.
[ Item detected: Vibro‐Edge Sword.
Status: Defective. Resonance unstable. Cuts are only intermittently enhanced. ]
Kai gently nodded. It would certainly be a great weapon if it were fixed.
"Unreliable, but better than nothing if I need a backup."
Finally, he spotted a small crate tucked beneath scrap.
Inside were spherical devices, dull and scratched. They weren’t A.I. devices like Chamber, as they were smaller in size... they appeared more like grenades!
[ Item detected: Fragmentation Orbs.
Status: Defective. Fuse delay is inconsistent.
Risk of premature detonation. ]
"Why is this thing here? It’s not going to explode suddenly, right?" Kai muttered.
Still, Kai could tell that it would be a terrifying weapon if they could really use it.
"They’re all interesting... But I guess there’s no other item like you here, Chamber."
As he said this, he looked at the small pile he had gathered... a plasma repeater, shockwave charge, vibro‐edge sword, and several unstable fragmentation orbs. Not perfect, but each had potential.
Chamber pulsed warmly.
[ Master, these rejects may be flawed, but flaws can be exploited. With careful use, they can probably be useful. ]
Kai smiled faintly. It was as if Chamber was projecting itself to these rejects and didn’t want them to be completely thrown away.
"Ahem... Right, defective doesn’t mean useless. Guess you’re proof of that. But we can’t carry these items yet."
As he said this, he left the storage and closed the door to ensure that these items wouldn’t get stolen... This was also to keep the others safe since any explosives here might get triggered.
"Alright! Let’s go hack Citadel‐09 and save those people outside!"
The pendant hummed in agreement.
[ Then let us begin. The path forward is dangerous, but I will help you! ]
Kai rose, gripping his lance tightly. With Chamber’s guidance, he followed its instruction and headed to the first node..."
Kai followed Chamber’s guidance through the dim corridors.
Clank... Clank... Clank...
The sound of machinery echoing around him became louder as the battle outside became intense.
The pendant pulsed faintly, feeding him directions toward the first control node.
It wasn’t long before the fortress reacted.
From the shadows ahead, three Sentinels emerged, and their armor even had red emergency lights.
Each carried a plasma rifle with barrels glowing as they powered up.
[ Warning: Hostile units detected. Targeting weak points... ]
Chamber’s voice remained calm as they detected the enemies.
[ Their rifles only have 3 charges... Aim for the chest. ]
Kai grinned. "Got it."
Just like that, he activated his Titan Step!
Thud!
The first Sentinel raised its rifle, but Kai blurred forward with his Gene Skill, closing the distance in an instant.
Bam!
His War Lance thrust precisely where Chamber indicated! The core beneath the chest plating was hit!
Sparks erupted, and the machine collapsed just like that!
[ Enemy Unit Destroyed: Sentinel (C) ]
[ +50 Experience Points ]
The second Sentinel fired with its plasma bolts scorching the wall behind him. Kai just ducked low, then charged upward with his Strength Gauntlet, smashing his fist into the unit’s shoulder joint.
Bam!
Metal crumpled and the rifle clattered to the floor, and Kai finished it with a swift lance strike.
The last Sentinel tried to retreat, but Chamber’s voice guided him again.
[ Left knee joint compromised. ]
Kai smiled as his gauntlet crashed into the joint.
The Sentinel toppled, and Kai drove his lance through its core.
[ +50 Experience Points ]
[ +50 Experience Points ]
Kai exhaled, as he looked at the Plasma Rifles before storing them inside his inventory. Unlike the junks, these Rifles were too precious.
"That was almost too easy with you calling the shots."
[ Yes! Tactical guidance reduces wasted effort. ]
Chamber replied, almost smug.
Kai chuckled. "Alright, let’s move."
They pressed deeper until Chamber signaled.
[ First access node located. Behind this door. ]
Kai forced the door open, revealing a chamber filled with humming consoles and glowing veins. The node pulsed faintly, connected to the fortress’s systems.
"Can you do it now?" Kai asked.
[ Master, I cannot breach this system wirelessly. You must connect me directly. Place the pendant against the node’s interface port. ]
Kai blinked. "Right... So you need a hard link... is it this one?" Kai asked, showing what seemed like a small iron altar.
[ Correct. The Citadel’s firewalls are layered against remote intrusion. Only a direct neural‐to‐system connection will allow me to override their safeguards. ]
Kai hesitated, then unclasped the dog‐tag pendant. The rectangular plate extended a thin filament, almost like a cable, shimmering with faint energy.
He pressed it against the console’s port.
Clack.
The node reacted instantly, lights started blinking as Chamber’s hum intensified.
Kai felt a faint tug in the back of his mind, as if his own nervous system was now tethered to the fortress.
"Weird feeling... Is this normal?" Kai asked.
[ Connection established. Intrusion protocols active. You must defend me while I override the directives. ]
Kai tightened his grip on his lance. "Alright, Chamber. Do it."
The pendant’s hum rose to a rapid cadence, Chamber’s voice echoing in his mind. [ Initiating intrusion... bypassing firewall... rewriting directives... progress at 12%. ]
Kai stood guard as instructed.
The fortress seemed to sense the intrusion... Soon, alarms blared, and mechanical footsteps echoed down the corridor!
Two more Sentinels charged in, rifles blazing. Kai then charged forward with Titan Step carrying him past the plasma bolts.
He slammed his gauntlet into one’s chest, sparks flying, then spun to impale the second with a precise thrust.
[ Intrusion progress: 46%. ]
"Alright... Just work on it!"
The walls trembled, and a heavier unit stomped into view... an Adaptive Construct!
"Shit... That looks menacing, Chamber. I don’t think a low-level Survivor like me can survive this."
Its body shifted, arms transforming into twin cannons.
Thankfully, Chamber could actually multitask even if it was slow!
[ Warning: Adaptive Construct. The weak point is located at the back. ]
Kai dashed sideways as the cannons fired...
Bam!
The plasma scorched the floor.
Kai didn’t stop as he threw one of his fragmentation granades.
The fuse sputtered, but it detonated just in time, shrapnel tearing into the construct’s armor!
Kai seized the opening with his Titan Step, carrying him behind it.
"Haa!"
His War Lance then pierced the exposed core, and the machine collapsed.
[ Intrusion progress: 78%. ]
Kai panted, gripping his lance tightly.
"How much longer?"
[ Almost complete. Final override... 95%... 100%. Node compromised. Control channel rerouted. ]
The consoles flickered, and Chamber’s voice carried a note of triumph.
[ First node secured. The fortress’s defenses are weakened. Two more nodes remain before we can access the core. ]
Kai exhaled, relief flooding him. "So this is how we dismantle Citadel‐09... piece by piece. Good work, Chamber!"
[ Thank you, master! You are correct. Each node we seize reduces Anima’s control. Once all are overridden, I can initiate a full takeover. ]
Kai’s eyes lit up, unaware that their actions created a huge wave of events outside!
