Most of them had already died, and their roars were also weakening as their leader staggered.
No one could stop the Super Soldiers anymore!
"Let’s end this!"
Finally, with a coordinated strike of axes, swords, and gunfire, the Golden‐Horned Bull collapsed.
Its golden horns glinted faintly as its life faded!
As soon as the Golden Bull died, its herd scattered into the forest.
"It’s done!" Ralph shouted in joy as he asked Renji, one of the temporary members of his team, to use his Appraisal and confirm their hunt.
"Appraisal..." Renji said as he soon got the notification.
[ You have discovered Golden‐Horned Bull Carcass! ]
[ Grade: Rare Resource ]
[ Description: A resilient creature.
Flesh is pure and safe for consumption, rich in nutrients.
Hide is durable, suitable for crafting protective gear, and the horns contain condensed spiritual energy. ]
[ Note: Meat provides high nutritional value.
Horns may be harvested for spiritual enhancement or crafting. ]

chapters.title: Chapter 338: The Carcass, The Illusion, and The Water
paragraphs: The clearing was filled with cheers as the Golden‐Horned Bull finally collapsed, its golden horns were still warm and filled with energy even as life left its body.
The Super Soldiers lowered their weapons, while Ralph’s Team also raised their rifles in triumph.
"It’s done!" Ralph shouted, and his voice carried across the battlefield.
Renji then stepped forward with excitement. His Appraisal had confirmed what they all hoped for... the carcass was pure, edible, and rich in energy.
The horns contained condensed spiritual power, and the hide was durable enough for crafting protective gear.
For a moment, the exhaustion of battle faded.
Survivors laughed, clapped each other on the shoulders, and even the stoic Super Soldiers allowed themselves a faint smile.
Renji grinned wider than anyone.
"I was planning to head to Cameron City soon... but forget that. I’m not leaving until I’ve had a taste of this Golden Bull!"
"Hahaha!"
"Makes sense!"
"Don’t hurry to leave the shelter!"
The others chuckled at his enthusiasm.
After weeks of eating dried meat, canned goods, and bread, the thought of fresh, powerful meat was intoxicating.
The carcass was secured quickly.
The horns were carefully removed and stored in one of the prepared crates, while the body was lifted onto a cart.
As for the other black bulls, their horns were harvested, but their bodies were left behind. Everyone knew their flesh was inedible as they were poisoned by corruption.
With the Golden Bull secured, the hunting party began the trek back to the shelter.
The cart creaked as they pushed it along the muddy path, the carcass of the Golden Bull weighing heavily, but it was filling the air with anticipation.
"I swear, just smelling it makes me hungry already," one of Ralph’s riflemen muttered, wiping sweat from his brow.
"Hah, wait until tonight," another replied. "They say the meat gives strength. Imagine eating it before a mission... your stamina will skyrocket."
Renji chuckled, walking beside the cart. "I heard stories that even the tongue is edible. Some people used to stew it. They said it was chewy but packed with energy."
"Tongue, huh?" Castor grinned as he couldn’t imagine eating a tongue.
"I guess it’s better than dried jerky. But I’ll eat anything if it gives me power."
The group laughed, their voices carrying through the forest.
Another Super Soldier then spoke in his usual calm tone. "The horns are valuable, but the meat... Is it true that it gives a little bit of Gene enhancement?"

"Yeah," Ralph answered while his rifle was slung across his back. "But even without any enhancement, we’ve been running on canned sardines and bread for weeks. Even one egg a day isn’t enough... The bones will at least give us some nice broth."
Another rifleman added, "I heard from Wallace that the last time someone ate Golden Bull meat received a buff from the system itself."
Renji grinned wider. "That’s why I’m staying. Cameron City can wait. I want to feel that boost for myself."
The cart jolted over a rock, and Castor steadied it with one of his massive hands.
"Careful. Don’t damage the carcass. Every piece counts."
"Relax," Ralph said, smirking. "We’ll get it back safe. And when Mila’s crew cooks it, we’ll eat like kings."
This time, Renji recalled of something.
"You know what they say... the bull’s organs, especially the balls, are eaten in some places. Supposed to give men strength at night."
"Hahaha! I heard about that! Bull’s testicles... They gave you stamina, right?" someone teased, earning laughter from the group.
"I’ve heard that too. Some shelters stew them, claiming it boosts vitality. Guess we’ll find out soon enough."
Their laughter then carried forward.
But as they neared the familiar path, something strange happened.
"W‐what...?" one of the riflemen muttered, slowing his steps.
The shelter was gone!
"H-hey... Where’s the shelter? Am I looking in the right direction? Maybe that clearing was where the shelter was previously located? Did it get nuked or something?!"
"W-what happened? I didn’t sense any battles just now."
"Did they release some kind of new robot or something?"
Everyone felt shocked.
Where the walls and watchtowers should have been, there was now a hill covered in lush greenery.
"W-wait... If it’s nuked... There shouldn’t be anything here. T-that hill... I’m sure of it. That’s where the shelter was supposed to be!"
"It didn’t get nuked... It got covered by a hill!"
They couldn’t help but pause as they watched the trees sway gently in the wind...
They also saw vines draped across rocks, and the faint sound of birds echoed through the air. It looked like a natural forest, untouched by human hands.
"W‐what happened?" Ralph could only repeat his words.
The Super Soldiers tightened their grips on their weapons, unsure if this was an illusion or a trick by the A.I. Army.
"Did we... lose the way?" Renji asked nervously.
But no... the markings on the road were still there, carved deliberately by scouts. And the radio signal from the shelter was strong, guiding them forward.
"This is the right place," Castor said firmly.
"But it looks completely different."
Confusion spread among the group.
If not for the road markers and the radio beacon, they would have failed to find their own home.
Thankfully, a figure suddenly appeared just outside the hill!
It was a figure of a woman!
It didn’t take that long before they recognized her!
It was Claire who stepped forward!
"Don’t panic. This is our doing."
Everyone focused on her, curious about this situation.

Claire explained, "While you were busy hunting, I purchased a special item from the Reputation Store. It’s an illusion device. When paired with our advanced barrier generator, it cloaks the shelter in a natural disguise. To outsiders, it looks like a hill with a forest. To us, it’s still the same walls and towers."
The group stared in awe. Many of them had no idea about the Reputation Store.
However, they knew that it was related to the Foreign Survivors!
"You mean... the shelter is hidden?" Ralph asked.
Claire nodded. "Exactly. No enemy will find us easily now. Even if they scout the area, they’ll see nothing but wilderness."
Relief washed over the hunters.
What had seemed like a terrifying disappearance was actually a brilliant defense.
Renji laughed nervously.
"You almost gave me a heart attack. I thought we’d lost everything."
Claire smirked. "Better a heart attack than an ambush. This illusion will keep us safe."
The Super Soldiers relaxed as they realized just how amazing this upgrade was...
Ralph’s team exchanged glances... They were also impressed by the ingenuity.
"Smart move," Castor admitted.
"Since it works perfectly with the barrier generator, the A.I. Army won’t find us."
Just like that, the group pushed forward.
Then, as they crossed the invisible threshold, the illusion shimmered, and the true form of the Codebreakers Shelter emerged...
Finally, they saw the walls, watchtowers, tents, and bustling survivors.

The cart carrying the Golden Bull was wheeled inside, greeted by cheers from those waiting. Word spread quickly... the hunters had succeeded, and the shelter itself was now cloaked in a powerful illusion.
It was definitely worth celebrating!
Renji grinned again, patting the cart. "Cameron City can wait... Maybe next week..."
"Hey! The monthly ranking is almost over... You should be leveling up if you want to retain your ranking..."
In the meantime, Atom stood silently at the edge of the courtyard... Its black armor was a bit dusty, but its appearance still looked imposing...
The Rank S Sentinel did not speak, but its optics scanned constantly, recording every movement, every sound around it.
Nonetheless, Kai’s last command echoed within its core systems...
Protect the shelter. Follow Claire, Mei, Althea, and Sera, as long as they do not go against the Three Laws.
The Three Laws were imprinted deep into its protocols...
First Law: Never harm Kai, nor allow him to come to harm through inaction.
Second Law: Obey Kai’s commands, unless they conflict with the First Law.
Third Law: Protect its own existence, as long as that does not conflict with the First or Second Law.
Atom remembered them clearly.
They were the framework of its existence, the unbreakable code that defined its purpose.
Its optics shifted as footsteps approached.
There was a familiar young woman who entered the courtyard, carrying a bucket of water, a sponge, and dishwashing liquid.
Atom’s sensors identified her immediately... one of the shelter’s workers assigned to maintenance.
She stopped in front of the towering Sentinel, looking up with a nervous smile.
"Alright... time for your bath."
Atom processed the words. It understood the intent.
Cleaning was maintenance. Maintenance preserved its existence.
The Third Law aligned with this action. No conflict detected.
The woman dipped the sponge into the bucket, squeezing out suds before pressing it against Atom’s armored chest.
Soon, water streaked down the black plating, carrying away dust and grime from its previous battles or missions.
Atom stood motionless, allowing her to work.
Its sensors registered the temperature of the water, the chemical composition of the soap, and the pressure of her movements.
Every detail was cataloged, analyzed, and stored...
But it probably wouldn’t need such information.
Still, a few survivors giggled at the sight of the mighty Rank S Sentinel being scrubbed like a statue.

chapters.title: Chapter 340: Bladed Sentinels
paragraphs: Mei was still scrolling through the Reputation Store interface when a sudden static noise jolted her...
It was coming from a radio.
The noise was irregular, like metal grinding against stone... She frowned after hearing this since she felt that it was a bad sign... She then adjusted the dial.
Sshh~ Ssshh~
Then, through the distortion, Russel’s voice burst out... He was panicked, hurried, almost trembling!
"Mei! Do you copy? This is Russel! I’m being chased... seven of them! New type of Sentinels... humanoid, but their arms... are blades! Both arms are blades!"
The words spilled out fast... It was broken by static.
Mei stiffened as she realized that her hunch was right!
There was indeed something wrong.
Around her, survivors nearby stopped what they were doing, sensing the urgency in his tone.
Russel’s voice could then be heard again, louder this time.

"They’re fast! Too fast! I had to abandon the hill! Wait... I’ve got... escape route planned, motorbikes ready... I need instructions! Do I bring them toward the base... or do I lure them into the forest filled with traps?"
Mei’s grip tightened on the radio.
She glanced at Wallace, who was already listening from across the courtyard. His expression was grim as he processed the situation. Other officers also had their faces filled with resolve.
"To the base... Wait... No, lure them to the forest!" Mei immediately corrected herself as she looked at Atom.
Then, she heard Russel’s breathing. It was heavy and audible even through the static.
"Seven bladed‐arm Sentinels... They can leap high!"
Mei nodded.
If Russel lead them to the base, they could certainly easily win against these new Sentinels.
But it would be a problem since it would expose their shelter if the information was sent out.
Mei sighed... He could only hope that Russel could escape faster.

The shelter was cloaked by Claire’s illusion device, hidden beneath the guise of a forested hill. But if the Sentinels were allowed too close, if they detected anomalies in the terrain, the A.I. Army might uncover their camouflage. That risk was unacceptable.
She looked at Wallace again...
Finally, he spoke through his radio.

"Russel. Just like what Mei said. Do not bring them to the base. Repeat... do not bring them here. Pass through the forest. We’ve prepared traps along the ravine. Lead them there. We’ll destroy or capture them away from the shelter."

Mei nodded quickly, reinforcing the command. "Our illusion must remain unknown. If the A.I. realizes we’ve hidden the shelter, they’ll send more. We can’t afford that. Take them into the forest... We’ll use the traps. Don’t let them near us."
Russell’s reply came fast.

"Understood. I’ll draw them into the ravine. I’ll bait them, then cut across the forest path. If the traps work, we’ll cripple them. If not..." His voice trailed for a moment before he continued. "I hope you all can save me."
The radio hissed, then cleared.
Mei could hear the roar of engines in the background, the crunch of dirt under tires, and the metallic shriek of Sentinels pursuing him...

Meanwhile, the forest was filled with the sound of engines. Russel’s motorbike tore through the vegetation... Then soon, mud was spraying everywhere as he leaned hard into every turn. Behind him, seven units followed.
They were bladed‐arm Sentinels, and they were not planning to stop the chase any time soon.
It was as if they were waiting for Russel to bring them to his base.
Russel gritted his teeth.
No... you’re not getting the shelter. You’ll bleed in this forest first.
He swerved sharply, guiding the chase toward the valley where traps had been laid days earlier.
"Die!"
The first was a line of hidden spike pits covered with leaves. He gunned the throttle, leapt his bike over the narrow gap, and heard the crunch behind him as one Sentinel misjudged the landing.
Thud!
Its blade arms flailed as it fell into the pit, impaled on sharpened stakes.
Sparks erupted, but the others adjusted instantly, vaulting over the trap with eerie precision.
"Damn it... only slowed one," Russel muttered.
Further ahead, he triggered a tripwire. A cluster of weighted logs swung down from the canopy, smashing into two Sentinels!
One was knocked off balance, tumbling into the undergrowth, while the other raised its blades to block, splintering the logs but staggering backward.
Russel grinned briefly. "That’s two more stalled."
Just like that, Russel tried to use various traps, but not all of them could give satisfactory results. Still, with so many traps used, they at least slowed down.
Soon, another wire snapped beneath his tires, and a net of steel cables shot upward, tangling one Sentinel...
Its blades slashed furiously, cutting through the cords, but not before Russel gained precious distance.
"Come on... come on..." he whispered.
The final trap was the most dangerous... a concealed minefield buried beneath loose soil. Russel veered sharply, skimming the edge of the marked path.
Thud.
The Sentinels followed, triggering the pressure plates!
Boom! Boom! Boom!
Explosions ripped through the forest, and fire and shrapnel immediately tore into their ranks.
Two were blown apart instantly as their parts were scattered across the dirt.
Another moved awkwardly as one blade arm was already mangled.
Russel’s heart pounded. "This is really troubling."
But the surviving Sentinels were cautious now. They slowed, their movements were on a certain distance.
They’re gathering data. If they learn too much, the A.I. Army will know everything.
Russel felt conflicted.
Nonetheless, he pushed the bike harder, but his arms trembled, exhaustion was finally setting in.
"Shit... I need to drink a potion."
The Sentinels closed in again with blades slicing through trees.
Russel’s escape route was collapsing.
Then, a shadow streaked overhead. The roar of engines filled the air. Russel looked up, relief flooding his chest.
Atom had arrived... mounted on the Dragoon!
The bladed Sentinels halted, as if they were cautious once more.
This time, they weren’t rushing blindly. They were waiting, studying the mysterious Sentinel above them!
Russel also skidded to a stop as he realized that the reinforcements had arrived.
"Finally... Atom."
A few minutes ago, Mei looked at the Black Sentinel...
"Atom," she said firmly. "Russel is being hunted. Seven Units are after him. They’re bladed‐arm Sentinels. He’s leading them into the forest traps, but he won’t last alone. You will go. Save him."
The Sentinel did not move, but its optics shifted, locking onto Mei.
She exhaled, then added, "Use the Dragoon. It’s the fastest way. You’ll need speed to intercept before they cut him down."
A murmur rippled through the survivors nearby.
The Dragoon was infamous... an unstable, modified flying jetski that few dared to pilot. Even Wallace frowned.
"Mei... are you sure? That machine isn’t easy to control."
Mei’s gaze didn’t waver. "I know. But Atom isn’t like us. If anyone can handle it, it’s him."
For a moment, she wasn’t sure if Atom would understand. The Dragoon required balance, precision, and instinct.
But then, the Sentinel’s optics blinked.
Its systems processed the command, recalling Russel’s face, his voice, and the coordinates of the forest.
Without hesitation, Atom turned, striding toward the Dragoon.
The machine’s engines hummed as it mounted...
Just like that, the roar of turbines filled the air, and in a burst of speed, Atom shot skyward!
Mei tightened her grip on the radio, speaking once more. "Russel, hold on. Atom is coming. Lead them deeper into the ravine. The traps will probably just weaken them, and Atom will finish the job."
She had no idea if Russel heard her voice, but it should be just fine with Atom making its move!
And with that, the Rank S Sentinel vanished into the forest, ready to clash with the bladed‐arm machines.
Still, Russel’s bike skidded across a slope, nearly tipping.
It was dangerous!
Still, he was able to steady it... as the Sentinels closed in. One leapt high, blades gleaming, aiming to cleave him in two. Russel ducked, the blade missing by inches, carving a tree trunk instead.
"Damn it!" he shouted, twisting the throttle. The bike surged forward, but the Sentinels were moving so fast...
Their movements weren’t mindless; they were cautious, coordinated, as if studying him.
Then, a shadow passed overhead.
Whoosh~ Russel looked up, and soon, he was filled with excitement!
Atom descended on the Dragoon!
Nonetheless, Atom dismounted mid‐air, landing with a thunderous impact that cracked the earth beneath its feet!
But for some reason, the seven-bladed Sentinels circled, showing that they’re cautious of Atom’s appearance!
Then, their eyes glowed red, scanning Atom, recording every movement. They did not rush blindly.
It seemed that they were gathering data.
Atom’s systems processed all of this instantly.
[ Threat level: high. Objective: eliminate pursuers. Protect Russel. ]
The first Sentinel charged...
However, Atom just sidestepped, and its armored hand then moved forward to catch the blade!
Thud!
Sparks erupted as metal met another metal...
With a turn, Atom wrenched the blade downward before driving its knee into the Sentinel’s chest.
Bam!
The machine crumpled, and just like that, its circuits burst before Atom hurled it into a tree!
Boom!

That risk was unacceptable.
She looked at Wallace again...
Finally, he spoke through his radio.
"Russel.
Just like what Mei said.
Do not bring them to the base.
Repeat... do not bring them here.
Pass through the forest.
We’ve prepared traps along the ravine.
Lead them there.
We’ll destroy or capture them away from the shelter."
Mei nodded quickly, reinforcing the command.
"Our illusion must remain unknown.
If the A.I. realizes we’ve hidden the shelter, they’ll send more.
We can’t afford that.
Take them into the forest...
We’ll use the traps.
Don’t let them near us."
Russell’s reply came fast.
"Understood.
I’ll draw them into the ravine.
I’ll bait them, then cut across the forest path.
If the traps work, we’ll cripple them.
If not..." His voice trailed for a moment before he continued.
"I hope you all can save me."
The radio hissed, then cleared.
Mei could hear the roar of engines in the background, the crunch of dirt under tires, and the metallic shriek of Sentinels pursuing him...
Meanwhile, the forest was filled with the sound of engines.
Russel’s motorbike tore through the vegetation...
Then soon, mud was spraying everywhere as he leaned hard into every turn.
Behind him, seven units followed.
They were bladed‐arm Sentinels, and they were not planning to stop the chase any time soon.
It was as if they were waiting for Russel to bring them to his base.
Russel gritted his teeth.
No... you’re not getting the shelter.
You’ll bleed in this forest first.
He swerved sharply, guiding the chase toward the valley where traps had been laid days earlier.
"Die!"
The first was a line of hidden spike pits covered with leaves.
He gunned the throttle, leapt his bike over the narrow gap, and heard the crunch behind him as one Sentinel misjudged the landing.
Thud!
Its blade arms flailed as it fell into the pit, impaled on sharpened stakes.
Sparks erupted, but the others adjusted instantly, vaulting over the trap with eerie precision.
"Damn it... only slowed one," Russel muttered.
Further ahead, he triggered a tripwire.
A cluster of weighted logs swung down from the canopy, smashing into two Sentinels!
One was knocked off balance, tumbling into the undergrowth, while the other raised its blades to block, splintering the logs but staggering backward.
Russel grinned briefly.
"That’s two more stalled."
Just like that, Russel tried to use various traps, but not all of them could give satisfactory results.
Still, with so many traps used, they at least slowed down.
Soon, another wire snapped beneath his tires, and a net of steel cables shot upward, tangling one Sentinel...
Its blades slashed furiously, cutting through the cords, but not before Russel gained precious distance.
"Come on... come on..." he whispered.
The final trap was the most dangerous... a concealed minefield buried beneath loose soil.
Russel veered sharply, skimming the edge of the marked path.
Thud.
The Sentinels followed, triggering the pressure plates!
Boom!
Boom!
Boom!
Explosions ripped through the forest, and fire and shrapnel immediately tore into their ranks.
Two were blown apart instantly as their parts were scattered across the dirt.
Another moved awkwardly as one blade arm was already mangled.
Russel’s heart pounded.
"This is really troubling."
But the surviving Sentinels were cautious now.
They slowed, their movements were on a certain distance.
They’re gathering data.
If they learn too much, the A.I.
Army will know everything.
Russel felt conflicted.
Nonetheless, he pushed the bike harder, but his arms trembled, exhaustion was finally setting in.
"Shit...
I need to drink a potion."
The Sentinels closed in again with blades slicing through trees.
Russel’s escape route was collapsing.
Then, a shadow streaked overhead.
The roar of engines filled the air.
Russel looked up, relief flooding his chest.
Atom had arrived... mounted on the Dragoon!
The bladed Sentinels halted, as if they were cautious once more.
This time, they weren’t rushing blindly.
They were waiting, studying the mysterious Sentinel above them!
Russel also skidded to a stop as he realized that the reinforcements had arrived.
"Finally...
Atom."
A few minutes ago, Mei looked at the Black Sentinel...
"Atom," she said firmly.
"Russel is being hunted.
Seven Units are after him.
They’re bladed‐arm Sentinels.
He’s leading them into the forest traps, but he won’t last alone.
You will go.
Save him."
The Sentinel did not move, but its optics shifted, locking onto Mei.
She exhaled, then added, "Use the Dragoon.
It’s the fastest way.
You’ll need speed to intercept before they cut him down."
A murmur rippled through the survivors nearby.
The Dragoon was infamous... an unstable, modified flying jetski that few dared to pilot.
Even Wallace frowned.
"Mei... are you sure?
That machine isn’t easy to control."
Mei’s gaze didn’t waver.
"I know.
But Atom isn’t like us.
If anyone can handle it, it’s him."
For a moment, she wasn’t sure if Atom would understand.
The Dragoon required balance, precision, and instinct.
But then, the Sentinel’s optics blinked.
Its systems processed the command, recalling Russel’s face, his voice, and the coordinates of the forest.
Without hesitation, Atom turned, striding toward the Dragoon.
The machine’s engines hummed as it mounted...
Just like that, the roar of turbines filled the air, and in a burst of speed, Atom shot skyward!
Mei tightened her grip on the radio, speaking once more.
"Russel, hold on.
Atom is coming.
Lead them deeper into the ravine.
The traps will probably just weaken them, and Atom will finish the job."
She had no idea if Russel heard her voice, but it should be just fine with Atom making its move!
And with that, the Rank S Sentinel vanished into the forest, ready to clash with the bladed‐arm machines.
Still, Russel’s bike skidded across a slope, nearly tipping.
It was dangerous!
Still, he was able to steady it... as the Sentinels closed in.
One leapt high, blades gleaming, aiming to cleave him in two.
Russel ducked, the blade missing by inches, carving a tree trunk instead.
"Damn it!" he shouted, twisting the throttle.
The bike surged forward, but the Sentinels were moving so fast...
Their movements weren’t mindless; they were cautious, coordinated, as if studying him.
Then, a shadow passed overhead.
Whoosh~ Russel looked up, and soon, he was filled with excitement!
Atom descended on the Dragoon!
Nonetheless, Atom dismounted mid‐air, landing with a thunderous impact that cracked the earth beneath its feet!
But for some reason, the seven-bladed Sentinels circled, showing that they’re cautious of Atom’s appearance!
Then, their eyes glowed red, scanning Atom, recording every movement.
They did not rush blindly.
It seemed that they were gathering data.
Atom’s systems processed all of this instantly.
[ Threat level: high.
Objective: eliminate pursuers.
Protect Russel. ]
The first Sentinel charged...
However, Atom just sidestepped, and its armored hand then moved forward to catch the blade!
Thud!
Sparks erupted as metal met another metal...
With a turn, Atom wrenched the blade downward before driving its knee into the Sentinel’s chest.
Bam!
The machine crumpled, and just like that, its circuits burst before Atom hurled it into a tree!
Boom!

chapters.title: Chapter 341: Looted Item
paragraphs: With Rank S Sentinel making its move, destroying the Rank C Bladed-Arm Sentinels wasn’t that difficult.
In just a few moments, the forest had become silent, save for the faint sound of burning circuits.
Meanwhile, Atom stood among the wreckage with its black armor gleaming faintly in the dim light.
"Good job, Atom..." Russel said with a sigh. He really thought that he was about to die just now.
Around them lay the remains of the seven bladed‐arm Sentinels; their frames were already mangled, but they could still loot something from them.
One by one, Atom bent down, its movements were swift as it knew what to loot from these Sentinels...
From each fallen unit, it extracted the glowing energy cores, storing them carefully within its compartment.
Then, with equal efficiency, it detached the curved blades from their arms.
Clank! Clank! Clank!
The weapons were heavy and still humming faintly with residual power. However, Atom stacked them neatly, as if cataloging trophies.
Russel, still catching his breath, watched in awe.
"You are truly amazing..." His voice cracked, half disbelief, half relief. He wiped sweat from his brow, then forced a grin.
"Guess I owe you my life again."
Atom did not respond. Its eyes flickered once, then returned to scanning the battlefield.
Russel sighed, walking his motorbike closer.
He crouched, tying the salvaged blades together with thick rope.
The bundle was massive, clattering as he secured it to the rear of his bike.
"These will make good study material. Maybe Victor or Vera can figure out how they were built. Or maybe we can forge them into something useful." He chuckled nervously.
"Hell, maybe I’ll hang one on the wall as a reminder not to get chased again."
The Sentinel remained silent, watching.
Russel mounted his bike, testing the weight of the blades dragging behind.
The machine groaned under the load, but it held.
"Nice..."
He then glanced at Atom, who stood beside the hovering Dragoon, motionless.
"You’re coming with me, right? Don’t just stand there like a statue."
Atom’s optics shifted toward him, then back to the forest.
There were no words or acknowledgment.
Russel revved the engine, shaking his head.
"You know, it wouldn’t kill you to say something. Or... well, maybe it would. You’re not built for talking, I get it. Still, a nod would be nice."
The bike then lurched forward with its blades clattering against the dirt as Russel began the ride back. Atom followed, mounting the Dragoon once more.
Soon, the engines roared, carrying the Sentinel smoothly but not too high...
Well, Atom still had to protect Russell, and it didn’t forget its mission.

As they moved, Russel kept talking, his voice filling the silence. "You know, when I first saw them, I thought I was done for. Seven of those things are chasing me... I swear they were enjoying the chase. They’re probably waiting for me to reach our base... No... I’m sure of it. They wanted me to lead them somewhere." He paused, frowning.
"But you showed up. Thanks again, Atom."
The Dragoon hummed overhead, but Atom just stayed silent.

Russel continued. "I don’t know if you understand what that means. But I think they gathered enough information about you. They must’ve sent your information to their network. Next time, they’ll send something worse. Something built to counter you."
He swallowed hard, gripping the handlebars tighter. "And if that happens... I don’t know if even you can win. I hope Kai can help you get even stronger than now."
The forest thinned as they neared the shelter’s perimeter.
Soon, the illusion of the shelter as a hill appeared.
It was perfectly masking the hidden structures beneath.
Russel slowed, glancing back at the bundle of blades dragging behind him.
He also confirmed that there wasn’t anyone following them.
Soon, Russel noticed that the jammers were triggered... It was the base’s defensive device...
At this time, Atom descended beside him, landing with a heavy thud. Its optics scanned the surroundings, also ensuring no pursuit remained.
Russel parked the bike, exhaling deeply.
Just like that, they passed through the illusion!
As soon as he saw the walls and the people guarding it, Russel teared up a little.
"Safe. Finally safe."
He looked at Atom again...
"Thanks. I mean it. You saved me. Even if you don’t say a word, I know you understand."
Atom stood silent. It did not reply but it could understand Russel’s behavior.
Russel shook his head, chuckling under his breath. "You’re impossible. But I guess that’s what makes you reliable..."
He patted the bike, then tugged at the ropes securing the blades. "Come on. Let’s get these inside before someone thinks I decorated my ride with scrap metal."
Together, man and machine crossed back into the shelter’s gate...
The guards were aware of the situation and waved at him.
Russel raised a hand, calling out, "We’re back! And we’ve got souvenirs!"
At this time, Victor sat at his workbench, the salvaged blades laid out before him...
Their edges still looked sharp as if the Sentinels they once belonged to barely used them.
’I wonder what kind of process it had gone through...’
He checked it more closely before running his fingers along the alloy, noting the strange coldness he could faintly feel beneath the surface.
These weren’t ordinary weapons.
"This is perfect..."

Normal swords, hammers, and axes had proven clumsy in the hands of Super Soldiers. Their enhanced strength often shattered conventional steel, and their speed demanded weapons that could endure far greater stress.
But these blades... they seemed different.
Balanced, durable, and forged with a material Victor couldn’t identify.
He activated his Appraisal Skill...
[ You have failed to appraise the item. ]
"Oh well..."
Victor wryly smiled as the system window flickered before him.
’I guess it’s because of insufficient skill level.’
Victor cursed under his breath.
His appraisal was too low to reveal the true properties.
Still, he wasn’t helpless. He had the Tyrant Furnace... an artifact salvaged from the wreckage of defeated mechs.
With it, he could repurpose these blades, melt them down, and reforge them into something new.
Victor then scribbled notes across his ledger... After all, he had many works to do.
Potential integration with Super Soldier blades or gauntlets.
If he succeeded, these weapons could become extensions of the Super Soldiers themselves...
Then, he recalled Kai himself, who had obtained these Super Soldiers.
’I wonder what’s going on in Cameron.’
Victor muttered as Kai hadn’t been replying to their messages for a couple of days now!

chapters.title: Chapter 342: Lucky
paragraphs: Kai exhaled slowly as he looked over the chamber and the piles of loot he could store...
"Cannon Ball... This is too good."
As soon as he finished looking around, he checked out his inventory. He knew he had to be careful with what he carried. With only nine slots available, every decision mattered.
He opened his status window, scanning the list...
[ Inventory List ]
[ Neural Trap x99
Neural Trap x99
Neural Trap x99
Fangpiercer Daggers x2
Crimson Phase Blade x1
Titanbreaker Axe x1
Gene Stimulant x85
Modified Dragoon x1
C‐Grade Cores x99 ]
Kai frowned. "Nine slots... and I’m already full. If I want those cannon balls, I’ll have to make space."
His eyes lingered on the Fangpiercer Daggers.
They were small, easy to conceal, and linked together as a pair.
He pulled them out of his inventory, sliding them into his waist sheath and covered them with his Survivor Jacket... That freed one slot.

Next, he turned to the Titanbreaker Axe. The weapon was massive, heavy, and far too conspicuous. Carrying it openly would only draw suspicion, especially since it had belonged to mercenaries hired by the Cancer Faction.
The Crimson Phase Blade was already risky enough to keep. The daggers could be hidden, but the axe and blade were harder to explain.
Kai sighed. "Sorry, Titanbreaker. You’re too big."
With a flick of his hand, he removed the axe from his inventory, leaving it behind in the depot.
Now he had space.
He reached for the shimmering cannonballs stacked neatly in crates.
Their surface were shiny and seemed to be filled with Spirit energy. Chamber confirmed his suspicion earlier... these were forged from Aetherium, a material so rare it was practically priceless.
[ Aetherium Cannon Ball x99 ]
"I think we hit the jackpot, Chamber."
Kai’s lips curled into a grin as the system confirmed the addition.
"Perfect. These alone could probably upgrade Atom even more... or maybe I can trade it with the Gene Trader or something."
But the depot wasn’t finished surprising him. As he moved deeper into the chamber, he noticed another cache tucked behind the crates.
Smaller boxes, sealed with locks, lined the shelves. With Chamber’s assistance, the locks clicked open, revealing rows of compact devices.
Kai picked one up, turning it over in his hand.
It resembled a grenade, but its casing pulsed faintly with Spirit energy.
[ You have discovered Spirit Shock Orbs! ]
[ Grade: Rare Grade Consumable ]

[ Description: A compact explosive device that releases a concussive wave of Spirit energy upon detonation. Effective against mechanical units, temporarily disabling circuits and sensors. Limited effect on humans. ]
[ Note: Single‐use item. Highly volatile if mishandled. ]
Kai’s eyes widened. "Spirit Shock Orbs... Why are they keeping this? Wait... Maybe these things are confiscated or something?"
Nonetheless, what surprised Kai even more was the fact that he could actually store a crate!
Yes! Unlike the Traps and the Cannon Balls, he didn’t have to store them one by one!
He quickly stored them into his inventory and he realized that the crate seemed to be very special!
[ Spirit Crate x1 ]
Of course, Kai decided to store all these crates in front of him!
[ Spirit Crate x50 ]
Now his inventory read differently...
[ Inventory List ]
[ Neural Trap x99
Neural Trap x99
Neural Trap x99
Crimson Phase Blade x1
Gene Stimulant x85
Modified Dragoon x1
C‐Grade Cores x99
Aetherium Cannon Ball x99
Spirit Crate x50 ]
Kai nodded in satisfaction. "That’s better... Traps, consumables, cores, stimulants, and weapons..."
He glanced once more at the discarded Titanbreaker Axe, lying heavy and silent in the corner. "You’ll have to stay here. Too much baggage."
Kai then looked around trying to look for an item he could carry around... After all, it would be suspicious if there was nothing in his hands at all.
In the end, he decided to carry a crate filled with Plasma Cells! One crate contained at least 30 cells!
There were around 8 more crates of a similar kind, but he decided to just keep the rest inside the chamber.
He could just go back to loot them if given the chance.
In any case, with Chamber’s guidance, Kai sealed the depot again, ensuring no one else would stumble upon the hidden cache.
The corpses of the mercenaries remained inside, buried beneath crates and shadows...
Kai adjusted the daggers at his waist, feeling their weight against his side.
He exhaled, satisfied with the items with him... "Alright. Time to move."
Leaving the depot behind, Kai stepped back into the dim corridors of the fortress.
Kai tightened his grip on the crate of Plasma Cells as he moved to the exit...
Chamber guided him for some time, and soon he began to hear voices echoing ahead.
Survivors were gathering, many of them carrying sacks, crates, and bundles of scavenged loot.
"Alright... We’re here..."
One man moved past with a bag full of ration packs, while another hauled a crate of spare rifle parts.
A group nearby carried bundles of scrap alloys, and still, Kai guessed that they weren’t on par with Aetherium Alloy.

His eyes then moved across each load, cataloging silently... food, weapons, metals, stimulants. Nothing compared to the Aetherium cannonballs hidden in his inventory, but he kept that thought to himself.
Suddenly, shouts rang out.
"Enemy reinforcements are coming! Move it, everyone!"
The urgency rippled through the crowd, and the survivors quickened their pace.
Boots pounded against the stone floor as they rushed toward the exit.
Kai blended into the flow, the crate in his hands making him look like just another scavenger.
Yet he noticed the way several pairs of eyes lingered on him.

Plasma Cells weren’t as rare as Aetherium, but they were still valuable since they were basically fuel for Plasma Rifles, and he heard from Chamber that these cells could also be used for generators and defensive systems.
Just like that, whispers spread quickly.
"He’s carrying Plasma Cells... lucky bastard."
Kai heard it but he kept his expression neutral, adjusting the daggers hidden at his waist beneath his jacket.
He didn’t want attention, but he knew the crate gave him credibility among the looters.

Kai then looked around trying to look for an item he could carry around...
After all, it would be suspicious if there was nothing in his hands at all.
In the end, he decided to carry a crate filled with Plasma Cells!
One crate contained at least 30 cells!
There were around 8 more crates of a similar kind, but he decided to just keep the rest inside the chamber.
He could just go back to loot them if given the chance.
In any case, with Chamber’s guidance, Kai sealed the depot again, ensuring no one else would stumble upon the hidden cache.
The corpses of the mercenaries remained inside, buried beneath crates and shadows...
Kai adjusted the daggers at his waist, feeling their weight against his side.
He exhaled, satisfied with the items with him...
"Alright.
Time to move."
Leaving the depot behind, Kai stepped back into the dim corridors of the fortress.
Kai tightened his grip on the crate of Plasma Cells as he moved to the exit...
Chamber guided him for some time, and soon he began to hear voices echoing ahead.
Survivors were gathering, many of them carrying sacks, crates, and bundles of scavenged loot.
"Alright...
We’re here..."
One man moved past with a bag full of ration packs, while another hauled a crate of spare rifle parts.
A group nearby carried bundles of scrap alloys, and still, Kai guessed that they weren’t on par with Aetherium Alloy.
His eyes then moved across each load, cataloging silently... food, weapons, metals, stimulants.
Nothing compared to the Aetherium cannonballs hidden in his inventory, but he kept that thought to himself.
Suddenly, shouts rang out.
"Enemy reinforcements are coming!
Move it, everyone!"
The urgency rippled through the crowd, and the survivors quickened their pace.
Boots pounded against the stone floor as they rushed toward the exit.
Kai blended into the flow, the crate in his hands making him look like just another scavenger.
Yet he noticed the way several pairs of eyes lingered on him.

Plasma Cells weren’t as rare as Aetherium, but they were still valuable since they were basically fuel for Plasma Rifles, and he heard from Chamber that these cells could also be used for generators and defensive systems.
Just like that, whispers spread quickly.
"He’s carrying Plasma Cells... lucky bastard."
Kai heard it but he kept his expression neutral, adjusting the daggers hidden at his waist beneath his jacket.
He didn’t want attention, but he knew the crate gave him credibility among the looters.

chapters.title: Chapter 343: The Return and the Trade
paragraphs: Kai was a bit disappointed that he had to leave the fortress earlier than he had expected.
After all, Chamber mentioned 10 areas where he could loot some decent items.

They were the Neural Trap Storage, Explosive Depot, Prototype Weapon Lab, Energy Core Vault, Gene Skill Crystal Vault, Adaptive Construct Workshop, Medical Bay for Captured Humans, Data Archive, and the Experimental Node...
’I hope I can just go back here...’Kai muttered to himself as he moved faster.
Then, as he continued to carry the crate of Plasma Cells through the fortress corridors, several survivors from the Cancer Faction and even a few from Taurus noticed him.
Their eyes lit up, and soon voices called out while also moving out...
"Hey, Kai! Trade with us... Look, I’ve got stimulants!" A man from the Cancer Faction said as he waved a bundle of alloy scraps.
"These are special iron plates, rare stuff. Let’s swap!" Someone else shouted,
"I’ll give you these swords, straight from the depot!"
Kai glanced at their offers. Some of the items were genuinely interesting... combat stimulants, special alloys, even weapon components... but he shook his head firmly.
"Not now. Keep your loot. I’ll manage."
The others groaned in frustration but didn’t press further. Everyone was too focused on escaping.
Once outside the fortress, Kai spotted Trent and the Blue Sword Squad waiting near the motorbikes.
The squad had regrouped, and looking at it, he realized that they also obtained a lot of items...
Their faces even looked tense but determined. They were all just waiting for him nervously!
’I guess they can’t wait to leave this place...’
Trent then gave a sharp nod when he saw Kai.
"Good, you made it. Mount up!" Trent said over the loud rumble of engines.
Then, he looked behind them, confirming what Kai already sensed... a swarm of A.I. drones was closing in fast.
Kai swung onto his bike, the crate of Plasma Cells strapped securely.
"Let’s go!" Trent shouted, and the squad accelerated as one.
The convoy quickly passed across the plains, leaving behind some dust...
Still, the drones pursued for a time, but once the group neared the vicinity of Cameron City, the machines slowed.
The A.I. Army didn’t dare breach the city’s perimeter. Its defenses and factions made it too costly a target...
Relief washed over the squad as they passed through the gates.
Thankfully, during this time, there was no sabotage or any ambush...
"Let’s meet up again, Kai." Trent said with a smile before taking off.
Meanwhile, Kai then wasted no time.
As he broke away from the group, he headed straight for his shop.
Inside, he found Farrah admiring the brooch she had received from Hale Libra...
After hearing the bell rang, she finally looked up and was startled when she saw Kai carrying the crate.
"You’re back... and that’s... Plasma Cells?" Her eyes widened as she immediately recognized it.
"You got them?!"
Kai set the crate down with a faint smile. "Yeah. Managed to pull them out before the reinforcements arrived."

Farrah’s excitement was obvious... Plasma Cells were rare enough to make her forget the brooch in her hands. Kai simply leaned against the counter, already planning how to keep his true treasures hidden while letting the cells speak for themselves.
For the Neural Traps and others, he planned to have them all used to his Guild’s Shelter...
After all, he knew that improving his Shelter would allow his Guild to accept more missions and perhaps, receive more System Rewards if his Guild maintained its rankings.
After letting Farrah inspect the Plasma Cells on her own and greeting the two kids, Kai closed the door to his small room at the back of the shop...
The faint scent of dust and old wood lingers in the air.
The space, which doubled as storage, was cluttered with crates and scattered tools, but tonight it was just him and Chamber.
"Chamber... I need to know. Can I return to Citadel‐09 unnoticed? I didn’t finish exploring. There are still several more areas I haven’t touched."
The A.I. assistant’s voice resonated softly in his mind.

[ Reentry is possible, but only with precise planning. To calculate the safest infiltration route, I need more information about you... your current capabilities, items, and genetic enhancements. Without that, I cannot guarantee success. ]
Kai nodded. "Alright. You want to know me? Then I’ll show you."
Kai then decided to inform Chamber of some of his Gift Pack items, but not mentioning his Talent at all.
Still, Kai discussed his Gene Weapons a little. The Strength Gauntlet, War Lance, and his dagger, Specter Edge.
Chamber processed the information instantly.

[ Acknowledged. Your arsenal is versatile... With your consumables, you can easily survive long days of hiding and even if you meet D-Grade and C-Grade Units, you should be able to survive. Now, tell me about your Gene Skills."
Kai hesitated, then opened his status window.
[ Active Skills: Fast Appraisal Lv5, Spirit Dominion Lv2, Titan Step Lv1, Meditation Lv1, High Jump Lv1 ]
[ Passive Skills: Bio‐Adaptive Constitution Lv9, Great Protection Lv3, Slayer’s Flow Lv1, Solid Balance Lv1, Blood Regeneration Lv1 ]
Then, Kai passed the information to Chamber.

[ Excellent. With these skills and items, your survivability is higher than average. Combined with the Dragoon for mobility, you can bypass patrols and reenter Citadel‐09. The fortress is down, but even if its electricity got reactivated, I can help you become invisible from their cameras. Your concealment skill will also help mask you from most scanners. ]
Kai smiled as he heard this...
"So you’re saying it’s possible?"
[ Confirmed. ]
Chamber replied.

[ You can reenter the fortress. However, timing is critical. The A.I. Army will redeploy units to secure the site within forty‐eight hours. If you move before then, unnoticed infiltration is achievable. ]
Kai exhaled as he realized what he must do.
"Good. Then we’ll plan it. I’m not leaving those other areas untouched."
The room fell silent again, but Kai’s mind was already considering his options...
Still, he looked at the table beside him and saw the item he had left before going to the Citadel.
It was the Neural Gear!
’For now... I should check the Perfect World to find a better way to earn 20,000 credits. No... Wait. The Plasma Cells... Maybe I can trade it for some game credits?’

chapters.title: Chapter 344: Entering the Perfect World
paragraphs: Kai immediately shook his head. Instead of trading Plasma Cells for credits, he remembered something important... he had left his account linked here.
In short, survivors in Cameron City could actually purchase items from his shop using Perfect World’s digital currency.
That meant his store had been earning steadily even while he was away. He was curious how much had accumulated over the past few weeks.
With that thought in mind, Kai informed Farrah that he would enter the game world for a few hours.
"Alright! Leave the store to me! Just make sure to send another person here. I can’t stay here forever. I need to focus on leveling up as well!"
"Ok! Don’t worry. I made some arrangements already."
Farrah finally nodded thought she was still distracted by the crate of Plasma Cells.
Just like that, Kai slipped into his small room. He placed the Neural Gear over his head, and the familiar sensation of synchronization washed over him...
Whom~
When his vision cleared, Kai was no longer in Cameron City. He was standing in the bustling square of Reverie Town, the beginner town where his journey had first begun.
It had been a while since he last logged in, but the town hadn’t changed much. There weren’t many new players around in this place.
Well, even if there were thousands of players in this game, they would most likely leave this beginner town in a few weeks or so.
"This really feels amazing... It doesn’t feel like a game at all."
Although there weren’t players like him around, the cobblestone streets were still lively, filled with adventurers, merchants, and townsfolk.
The air carried the scent of baked bread and iron from the blacksmith’s forge nearby...
Kai—or Traceless, as he was known here—flexed his fingers.
He immediately felt the subtle weakening of his strength.
Still, his new Gene Skills from the real world had synchronized into the game system.
His status window reflected them, and he knew his combat potential had risen sharply despite having a low-level character.
Also, he felt that it was a good thing he had taken time away since now, he was stronger than before.
As he stood in the square, a town guard approached him.
"Traceless! Guard Captain Katrina is looking for you."
Kai blinked, then nodded. He remembered the mission he had completed with Katrina before...
[ Mission: Assist the Guard Captain in training recruits. ]
[ Reward: 250 Experience Points, 1 Skill Scroll of choice. ]

At that time, he had completed the mission and still had one unused Skill Scroll sitting in his inventory. Missions that rewarded skills were incredibly rare, and he knew he had been lucky to find it.
He followed the guard to the training grounds near the barracks. There, Katrina was waiting with her armor looking pristine and her sword at her side. She spotted him immediately and smiled.
"Traceless. You came back at the right time," she said firmly.
"I need your help again. The recruits are green, and they need someone experienced to guide them. Will you accept?"
A system window appeared before Kai.
[ Mission Available: Assist the Guard Captain in training recruits. ]
[ Reward: 550 Experience Points, 1 Skill Scroll of choice. ]
Kai’s eyes lit up.
As expected, it was the same mission but with higher experience points.
He didn’t hesitate. "I’ll accept."
He already forgot that he planned to check the amount of game credits he had earned through the trades in the real world.
[ Mission Accepted. ]
As soon as the mission got accepted, Katrina gestured toward the recruits lined up nearby.
"Good. Then let’s begin."
Kai turned to look at them... and immediately realized this time would be different.
"Mhmm?"
The recruits weren’t just ordinary townsfolk holding wooden swords. These were younger adventurers, probably players who had recently joined the game.

’They’re all wearing novice sets... I guess that shelter would send Survivors as young as 12 to play this game. I guess that’s not a bad idea to obtain Gene Skills and have combat experience without real danger.’
One boy held a rusty spear...
Another girl clutched a short sword, but for some reason, she seemed a bit too nervous.
Then, a third recruit carried a shield almost too heavy for him, and he was wobbling as he tried to stand firm... As for the rest, they seemed just like NPCs to him.
Kai exhaled. ’So it’s not just NPC recruits this time. Real players too.’
"I guess this will be quite different."
Katrina nodded.
"Yes. The town has opened training for newcomers. They need guidance, and you’ve proven yourself capable. Show them how to fight, how to survive."
Kai stepped forward... The only reason he was able to accept the mission before was due to the number of Gene Skills that he had.
At that time, he had to show various Skills, showing the Trainees the future that they could obtain.
Traceless then raised a hand. "First, remove your weapons and equipment. For now, you won’t need them."
The recruits exchanged glances but obeyed, setting down their spears, swords, and shields. The clatter of steel echoed across the training ground.
Even the NPCs followed suit, stacking their wooden practice weapons neatly.
Traceless finally stepped forward.
"I’ll show you something different. These aren’t ordinary weapons... they’re bound to me and they’re called Gene Weapons."
He extended his right arm, and with a faint light appeared...
Just like that, the Strength Gauntlet manifested, encasing his hand in a heavy, spirit‐infused iron.
The recruits gasped as they saw this happen.
"This is the Strength Gauntlet," Kai explained. "It enhances my physique, grip strength, and melee power. Every strike carries more weight than a normal blow."
He dismissed it with a flick of his hand, then summoned the War Lance.
The long weapon unfolded in his grasp, and it was quite fascinating how it appeared out of nowhere...
"This is my War Lance. A weapon that is mainly used to pierce armor..."
The recruits murmured in awe. To them, it was like watching a magician conjure weapons from thin air.
Finally, Kai summoned Specter Edge, the spirit‐infused dagger.
It had an unsettling aura that made others really curious.
These Gene Weapons were what made Katrina hire Traceless once again to do some demonstration and help her.
In this Beginner Town, not many people could have such Gene Weapons after all.
And as expected, the recruits were immediately captivated...

"That’s amazing, Sir! But may I ask why you are still here? We heard that the people with Gene Weapons were already hunting tri-horned or even four-horned beasts..." One of the recruits asked, stunning Traceless for a moment.

chapters.title: Chapter 346: Traceless
paragraphs: Kai opened his inventory and pulled out the two Skill Scrolls...
Sword Mastery and Spirit Barrier.
He sat quietly in the guild hall, focusing as the system prompted him to confirm learning the skills.
[ Skill Scroll: Sword Mastery learned. ]
[ Skill: Sword Mastery (Level 0) ]

[ Description: Improves proficiency with bladed weapons. Increases accuracy and stability when wielding such weapons, reducing stamina loss during extended combat. Enhances strike precision and allows smoother chaining of attacks. ]
A surge of clarity filled his mind.

He swiftly took out his Specter Edge... Despite not being a sword, his grip on blades felt steadier, and as he made a few swings, it felt a lot cleaner. The Specter Edge seemed lighter, more responsive as he continued testing it.
Of course, he didn’t test too much... He just made a few practice slashes as he wasn’t in the training ground in the first place.
"Good... this will be helpful when fighting against other Survivors."
Next, he activated the second scroll.
[ Skill Scroll: Spirit Barrier learned. ]
[ Skill: Spirit Barrier (Level 0) ]

[ Description: Forms a temporary shield of condensed Spirit energy around the user. The barrier absorbs incoming damage up to its threshold before dissipating. Effective against ranged and Spirit‐based attacks, but less resistant to heavy melee strikes.
Activation Cost: 30 SP
Cooldown: 10 seconds ]
Of course, without hesitation, he used the skill...
A faint glow surrounded him, forming a translucent shield. He pressed against it with his palm, feeling the resistance. It absorbed the force, shimmering before fading.
"A defensive skill... perfect for emergencies."
Satisfied, Kai dismissed the interface.
He had tested both scrolls, and they worked exactly as promised.
Finally, he logged out.
Back in Cameron City, he joined Farrah and the children, Xian and Xinyi, for dinner.
As always, their laughter filled the shop, easing the tension of the day.
Afterward, Kai discussed the situation...
Apparently, many factions were pressuring Farrah to sell the Plasma Cells.

In the end, after some discussions, he decided to sell them since they weren’t in his territory anyway... It wouldn’t be easy to keep those items in their hands with so many large factions around them.
Furthermore, Kai was planning to sneak back into the broken citadel someday to loot more.
Then, at this time, Farrah suggested trading them for hoverboards.
"Hoverboards... Right!"
Kai laughed, agreeing to her suggestion.
They looked cool, and he let her handle negotiations.
"Very well... Just make sure to inform the Aries Faction first... We’re still indebted to them."
"Alright! I’ll let them know!"
Once dinner was done, Kai returned to his small room, placed the Neural Gear over his head, and reentered Perfect World.
Whom~
Once again, he appeared within the town, and soon, he saw the mission marker glow...
[ Guard caravan en route to Leonine Town. ]
At the town gates, a caravan of wagons and pack beasts was already assembled. Merchants bustled about, securing crates and barrels, while guards checked weapons they had...
The caravan leader, a stout man named Julius, spotted Traceless and waved.
"You’re the one who accepted the mission? Good. We’ll need your strength. The road to Leonine is dangerous."
Traceless nodded. "I’ll keep the caravan safe."
The journey began at dawn.
The caravan rolled out of Reverie Town...
They had five wagons in total, each pulled by sturdy draft beasts.
Around twenty merchants traveled with them, while a dozen hired guards marched in formation. They had spears and crossbows at the ready.
As for Traceless, he was kept to the left flank.
The first day passed quietly until midday, when growls erupted from the forest.
Awooo~
A pack of mutated wolves burst from the shrubs...
They were horned beasts with sharp fangs...
"Careful!"
They immediately realized that there were at least fifteen of them, moving in coordinated formation.
"Wolves!" one of the guards shouted, raising his spear.
The caravan jolted to a halt, merchants scrambling to protect the wagons.
The guards formed a defensive line, but the wolves were fast, circling to flank.
"Experience Points..." Traceless muttered as he stepped forward, his foot slamming into the dirt. Titan Step activated, the ground trembling as shockwaves rippled outward!
He knew that it was impossible to use multiple Titan Steps because of his low level but since there were many of them, he didn’t mind emptying his SP right now!
Just like that, several wolves staggered, as their charge was disrupted.
Seizing the moment, Traceless relied on his Sword Mastery and summoned Specter Edge...
He really wanted to test how he would fare against these beasts.
Thankfully, he was not disappointed. He was able to cut through the beasts’ hides with efficiency that stunned the guards.
Two wolves leapt toward a wagon... However, Traceless raised his hand and triggered Spirit Barrier!
It shimmered into existence!
Thud!
A translucent wall absorbed the impact as the beasts slammed against it...
They could only snarl in frustration, before guards speared them down.
Then, he wielded his dagger to push them back...
The battle lasted minutes but felt longer.
Guards coordinated as the merchants stayed hidden...
Still, the guards were strong, and they were already expecting this level of danger.
By the time the last beast fell, the caravan was shaken but intact. No one died in the process.
Soon, the looting process began. It was truly game-like as the beasts’ bodies dissipated, leaving pelts, fangs, meat, gold coins, and other random stuff.
Of course, Kai gained experience points as well, and he even leveled up thanks to the level difference.
Apparently, the wolves were at least level 15... If not for his Gene Skills and Gene Weapons, he wouldn’t be able to win at all.
Thanks to that, he was able to refresh his dwindling Spirit Points, allowing him to save some SP recovery potions.
By evening, the caravan camped near a river.
Fires were made as merchants cooked meals, and Kai sat quietly, since he was considering whether training with his dagger would also increase his mastery.
In the end, he felt that it wasn’t that harmful to train, so he decided to practice with his Dagger, in hopes of increasing his mastery level.
The second day quickly arrived and it was harsher.
The caravan moved its way through a narrow terrain between cliffs and scattered boulders.
Five wagons creaked forward with their wheels grinding against stone.
Although it wasn’t their first time, twenty merchants huddled nervously inside or walked beside their goods, while twelve guards kept formation with spears and crossbows at the ready.
Seeing how guarded they were, Traceless stayed near the front, as he also felt that this was a good place for ambush...
Well, even if the merchants were only NPCs, he didn’t really want them to die here.
Suddenly, figures appeared on the cliff above.
A dozen rogue adventurers descended with their armor mismatched.
Furthermore, their weapons were obviously emitting ill intent.
Their leader, a scarred man wielding twin axes, sneered as he stepped forward.
"Drop the cargo," he shouted. "Or we’ll take it by force."
’Ohhh... A bandit group...’Traceless thought immediately.
The merchants froze as they assessed the level of strength of these bandits.
Meanwhile, the guards tightened their formation, but hesitation flickered in their eyes.
They weren’t in a good spot to fight after all,
The terrain advantage was obviously with the bandits.
Kai then stepped forward calmly, Spirit energy gathering around him.
Soon, Spirit Barrier shimmered into existence, a translucent dome wrapping him in protection.
It wouldn’t last for long, but it would help them avoid any surprise attacks...
As expected, the rogues laughed, and soon, everyone heard it.
Thud! Thud! Thud!
Arrows and staggers were immediately stopped by the Spirit Barrier!
"Y-you..."
Seeing that the surprise attack failed, the group finally charged!
Steel clashed against the barrier as blades scraped across its surface.
The shield held firm, absorbing the blows.
Traceless moved deliberately, waiting for the right moment.
Then, with a burst of speed, he dismissed the barrier and charged forward.
"You must have higher experience points. Don’t run!" Traceless said with a laugh.
Specter Edge flashed, guided by Sword Mastery. His strikes were swift, and it didn’t take long before two rogues fell while clutching wounds.
Then, another swung wildly, only to be staggered by Kai’s sudden Titan Step, the ground cracking beneath his weight!
Boom!
The shockwave threw several off balance, giving the guards courage to press forward!
"Haha! Let Traceless create chaos!"
"Seize them!"
"Good job, adventurer!"
"Protect the caravan!"
"Kill them!"
The battle raged for minutes.
Thanks to Traceless’ brave movement to charge forward, the guards were able to have a better position!
Traceless’s presence had truly turned the tide. His barrier shielded the caravan at critical moments, and his blade carved through the rogues so easily!
Finally, the scarred leader had enough... He swiftly realized the fight was lost.
"Fall back!" he shouted while moving back!
As soon as the command was issued, the rogues retreated into the hills, leaving behind their wounded.
However, there was no way Traceless would let these experience points leave so easily!

Effective against ranged and Spirit‐based attacks, but less resistant to heavy melee strikes.

chapters.title: Chapter 347: Completing the Mission
paragraphs: "Don’t let them escape!"
Traceless immediately chased after the retreating rogues, his figure quickly moving across the rocky terrain.
The scarred leader glanced back and was visibly surprised to see that someone was actually pursuing them.
’Aren’t you supposed to protect your goods?!’
Indeed, he had assumed that the adventurer would remain with the caravan and help protect the merchants, but this one particular person seemed to have a completely different objective in mind.
Just like that, Traceless smiled as he knew that he could actually reach them with his current speed.
’I know for sure that you’ll be giving me a lot of Experience Points.’
He had already gained quite a bit from fighting the mutated wolves on the first day, and these rogue adventurers were obviously stronger than those beasts.
If he could eliminate all of them, there was a good chance that he could level up again before reaching Leonine Town.
As he thought about this, Traceless accelerated.
One of the rogues noticed him approaching and immediately turned around, raising his sword.
"You! Don’t come any closer!"
Traceless didn’t bother responding.

The rogue swung his sword toward him, but he easily shifted his body to the side. At the same time, Specter Edge appeared in his hand, and with the assistance of his newly acquired Sword Mastery, his dagger moved smoothly through the opening in the man’s defense.
The rogue’s expression changed.

He had expected Traceless to be an ordinary adventurer who was simply a little stronger than the caravan guards. However, after exchanging only a single attack, he realized that the difference between them was much greater than he had expected.
"Y-you’re a player?!" The rogue was shocked.
He thought that the people in the caravan were all NPCs!
Traceless smiled as he didn’t care whether he was hunting Players or NPCs...
Even if they were players, the death penalty was only losing login rights for 24 hours anyway.
[ You have defeated a Level 13 Rogue Adventurer Player. ]
[ Experience Points gained. ]
[ You have obtained 28 Silver. ]
[ You have obtained a Low-Grade Healing Potion. ]
’Not bad.’
Traceless immediately looked ahead.
The other rogues were still retreating, but they had already started to separate from one another.
Some were running toward the hills while others were attempting to hide among the large rocks scattered around the area.
This was actually convenient for Traceless.

If they stayed together, they might have been able to overwhelm him through numbers. However, after their formation collapsed, they were simply giving him opportunities to deal with them individually.
He quickly chased after another rogue.
The man seemed to have noticed what was happening and immediately changed direction, attempting to circle around a large boulder. Unfortunately, Traceless had already seen him.
"You’re not getting away."
Traceless activated Titan Step.
Boom!
The ground trembled as the force of his movement spread outward, and the rogue’s body immediately lost its balance.
Before he could recover, Traceless had already arrived in front of him.
Specter Edge was drawn!
The rogue tried to block, but his movements were too slow.
[ You have defeated a Level 14 Rogue Adventurer. ]
[ Experience Points gained. ]
"That’s easier than I thought... I guess it’s because he’s not a Player." Traceless muttered... Still, he didn’t stop.
He continued chasing after the remaining enemies, and soon, the entire situation became a one-sided hunt.

The rogue adventurers had initially attacked the caravan because they believed they had the advantage. They had the high ground, they had the element of surprise, and their leader was clearly more powerful than the ordinary guards accompanying the merchants.
Unfortunately, they had completely underestimated the one person who could actually change the outcome of the battle.
Traceless.
One by one, the rogues fell... They were composed of low-level players and NPCs...
Some were defeated by Traceless himself, while others were left severely wounded after fighting against the caravan guards.
The scarred leader eventually realized that continuing the fight would only lead to more casualties.
"Fall back!"
He shouted as he quickly moved toward the western hills.
The remaining rogues immediately followed his order, abandoning their wounded companions as they desperately tried to escape.
Traceless frowned when he saw this.
’The leader is actually quite decisive.’
He had originally planned to continue chasing, but after looking at the distance between them, Traceless decided against it.
’I guess I already gained enough experience.’
There was no reason to abandon the caravan just to chase a five or so scattered enemies...
He had already defeated most of the rogue adventurers, and he felt that that was enough.
Traceless turned around and walked back toward the caravan.
When he finally returned, several of the guards were already collecting the weapons and items left behind by the defeated rogues.
Julius immediately approached him.
"You actually chased after them."
"Of course."
Traceless smiled faintly.
"They were running away, so I thought it would be a waste to let them escape."
Julius stared at him for a moment before laughing.
"I suppose that’s one way to look at it."
He then looked toward the hills where the rogue leader had escaped.
"Unfortunately, their leader managed to get away."
"That’s fine."
Traceless was also not too disappointed.
He had already gained a considerable amount of Experience Points, and there was no guarantee that the scarred man would have given him a good reward anyway.
The guards soon finished collecting the items.

There were several weapons, some low-grade armor, and a few healing potions among the loot. The caravan had also managed to protect most of its cargo, so the attack had not caused any significant losses.
Julius looked at Traceless with a complicated expression.
"If you hadn’t rushed forward earlier, I’m afraid we would have suffered a lot more casualties."
Traceless simply waved his hand.
"We were all part of the same mission. I just did what I was supposed to do."
Although he said this, Traceless was secretly quite satisfied.
This caravan mission was becoming much more interesting than he had initially expected.
He had already fought mutated wolves, rogue adventurers, and now had a chance to fight stronger opponents while traveling toward Leonine Town.
’It seems that accepting this mission was the right decision.’
With that thought in mind, the caravan continued moving.
Just like that, the second day of the journey eventually came to an end.
The caravan found a suitable location near a small stream and established camp for the night. The guards immediately began setting up their defenses while the merchants prepared their meals.
Traceless sat near one of the wagons and looked at his status window.
[ Level: 8 ]
[ Experience: 82% ]
[ Energy: 46/120 ]
He had gained a considerable amount of Experience Points during the two battles, and although he hadn’t leveled up yet, he was already very close.
His Spirit Points or Energy had also recovered significantly.
’The natural recovery is actually quite useful.’

Traceless had initially been worried that using Titan Step repeatedly would force him to rely too much on Energy Recovery Potions. However, as long as he had enough time to rest between battles, his Spirit Points could recover naturally.
This meant he could conserve his potions for more dangerous situations.
He then looked at Specter Edge.
Since he had just acquired Sword Mastery, he was curious about whether simply using the dagger would gradually increase the skill’s proficiency.
He had already noticed a slight difference when fighting the rogue adventurers.
His attacks felt more natural, and he had an easier time controlling the dagger during consecutive strikes.
’If I keep using it, I should eventually be able to increase the level.’
Traceless didn’t know exactly how the skill’s proficiency system worked, but he had already learned that the game seemed to reward actual experience.
Instead of simply waiting around, he decided to practice.
He moved away from the camp and found an open area where he could safely swing his dagger.
At first, he simply performed basic movements.
Then, he gradually increased his speed.

Specter Edge moved through the air repeatedly as Traceless practiced different angles and attack patterns. He wasn’t trying to learn an entirely new fighting style. Instead, he was simply trying to become more comfortable with the weapon.
After several minutes, he noticed something.
[ Sword Mastery proficiency has increased. ]
Traceless paused.
’It really works.’
He looked at the notification with interest.
It seemed that the skill could be improved through actual usage, and this meant that he could potentially increase its effectiveness simply by continuing to fight and train.
Satisfied, Traceless continued practicing for a while before finally returning to the camp.
The third day arrived.
By this point, the caravan had already traveled a considerable distance from Reverie Town, and the environment had begun to change.
The forests were becoming denser, but at the same time, there were more signs of civilization along the road.
Old watchtowers could occasionally be seen in the distance, and the roads were wider and better maintained than those around the Beginner Town.
Traceless immediately realized that they were getting close.
’Leonine Town shouldn’t be far now.’
He had heard from Katrina that Leonine was much larger than Reverie Town and served as one of the important settlements near the frontier.
Naturally, he was looking forward to seeing it.
After all, his main reason for accepting the caravan mission was to reach the city and discover what kind of opportunities were available there.
As the caravan continued moving, Traceless stayed near the front, and soon, he realized that he had already spent a lot of time using the Neural Gear!
Farrah and the other members of the Guild must be worried already!
